| W1 raw gate p | 0.0686 (+8.6%) | 0.1081 (+18.8%) |
| **W1' tanh(p/0.1)** | **0.0671 (+6.2%)** | **0.1025 (+12.6%)** |

The magnitude hypothesis was *partly* right — restoring unit
magnitude recovers a third of the wall-shear penalty and a quarter of
the pressure penalty — but the preregistered falsifier (still > 10%
worse on wall shear) **fires**. The e_phi pseudovector channels are
load-bearing in a way no parity-odd gate restores. Two candidate
explanations remain, and they are distinguishable without training:

- **L1 (labels are not reflection-covariant).** DrivAerML's
  time-averaged fields on mirror-symmetric cars need not be
  mirror-symmetric (asymmetric wake modes, finite averaging windows,
  mesh asymmetry). If a material fraction of the wall-shear energy is
  mirror-antisymmetric, an exactly covariant head *cannot* fit it by
  construction and the "defect" the M3 audit found was, in effect,
  the head learning the labels' asymmetry. **Preregistered
  measurement:** on mirror-symmetric DrivAerML cases, pair each
  surface point with its mirror image (nearest neighbour after
  reflecting through the symmetry plane) and compute the
  antisymmetric energy fraction ||v(Mx) − M v(x)||² / ||v||² for wall
  shear and |p(Mx) − p(x)|² / |p|² for pressure. Prediction if L1
  explains W1/W1': wall-shear antisymmetric fraction ≳ 10%, larger
  than pressure's. Falsifier: both ≪ 5% → labels are covariant and
  the problem is the head's basis (L2 below).
- **L2 (basis, not parity).** With the e_phi channels gated, the
  true-vector basis is {d, n, r̂, e_θ,n, e_θ,d}; where r̂ is nearly
  parallel to n or d the θ-complements vanish and the basis is
  locally rank-deficient, so the pseudovectors may have been serving
  as a generic tangent completion. Test only if L1 is refuted.

**Program note.** Whatever L1 shows, the parity fix stays in the
codebase default-off: on this dataset a physically correct head is
measurably worse, and the honest statement is that exact
reflection covariance is a contract the *labels* may not honour.

## 2026-09-02 — L1 verdict: DrivAerML labels are mirror-covariant to <1%, but a miscalibrated threshold hides that this can still account for most of the parity penalty {#sec-nb-l1-verdict}

**Measurement** (`results/l1_label_covariance_2026-09-02.json`; 48
val cars at full resolution, 14.6–19.8M cells each, cell-area
weighted). DrivAerML geometry mirrors about y = 0 to 3e-6 m; the mesh
itself is mirror-conformal over the bulk of the surface (median
mirror-pair distance 0.003 cell lengths), and 95% of cells pair
within one cell length. The mirror-antisymmetric energy fractions
of the labels are tiny: **pressure A_p = 0.93%** (mean-subtracted),
**wall shear A_v = 0.67%**, unchanged by k=8 spatial smoothing (so it
is genuine smooth asymmetry, not pairing noise). The least symmetric
channel is the side-force component v_y at 1.9% of its own energy —
the expected weak asymmetric-wake signature — but it carries only
10% of wall-shear energy. Wall shear is *more* symmetric than
pressure.

**Preregistered verdict: the falsifier fires** (both ≪ 5%; the
prediction A_v ≳ 10% missed by 15x). **But the threshold was
miscalibrated**, and this is the second such error this week (N1,
@sec-nb-n1-verdict). I compared an *energy-fraction* statistic to a
*rel-L2 penalty* without converting. The A statistic is 4x the
antisymmetric-part energy, so the truly unfittable wall-shear energy
for an exactly covariant head is A_v/4 = 0.17%. Errors add in
quadrature on a small baseline: sqrt(0.0910² + 0.0017) = 0.0999, a
**+9.8% penalty** in the extreme case where the unconstrained head
fits that component perfectly. The observed W1' penalty is +12.6%
(@sec-nb-w1p-verdict). So label antisymmetry, though below 1% in
energy, can account for *most* of the covariant head's disadvantage.
The lesson for future preregistrations: state thresholds in the
units of the readout they must explain, and derive them.

**The discriminating follow-up (L1b, data-only, dispatched now).**
Compute the same antisymmetry statistic on the *predictions*: the
unconstrained v3c head's val wall-shear predictions, and the
parity-fix head's. If v3c's predictions are as antisymmetric as the
labels (A ≈ 0.67%), the head is exploiting the labels' asymmetry and
L1 accounts for the penalty; if its predictions are nearly symmetric
(A ≪ labels'), the unconstrained head is *not* fitting the
antisymmetric part and the penalty must come from the covariant
basis losing rank where r̂ aligns with n or d (L2). The parity-fix
head's predictions must show A ≈ 0 by construction — a deployment
check of the contract.

**Side result worth keeping.** Mirror pairing gives a *model-free*
handle on label structure that N1 lacked: the antisymmetric energy is
smooth, not point-iid, so DrivAerML's labels carry little white
noise at the cell level; whatever "shared residual" the four models
have in common (N1: 71%) is not iid label noise either.

## 2026-09-02 — L1b: the unconstrained head never exploited label asymmetry (L1 nil, L2 live); true-vector basis arms preregistered {#sec-nb-l1b-l2-prereg}

**L1b result** (`results/l1b_prediction_antisymmetry_2026-09-02.json`).
The mirror-antisymmetry statistic computed on *predictions* at the
10,000-point val subsample, on identical mirror pairs for every model
(pairing error dominates the absolute level, so the exactly covariant
parity heads define the floor and the per-case *excess* over it is
the informative quantity): unconstrained MT2-v3c excess
−0.002 ± 0.001 (i.e. zero), GeoTransolver +0.001, the labels on the
same pairs **+0.012 to +0.016**. The unconstrained head predicts
fields exactly as mirror-symmetric as the constrained ones and does
*not* reproduce the labels' 0.67% antisymmetry. **L1 is nil.** The
covariant head's +12.6% wall-shear penalty is therefore a
representation effect — the gate removes two of seven basis
directions (and where |p| is small, removes them precisely on the
symmetry plane) — not a labels effect.

**L2 preregistered here** (two arms, two seeds each, otherwise the
frozen v3c protocol; thresholds stated in the readout's own units per
the N1/L1 lesson):

- **true5** (capacity control): drop the two e_phi pseudovector
  channels outright, no gate — a 5-vector all-true basis
  {d̂, n̂, r̂, e_θ,n, e_θ,d}. Exactly reflection-covariant by
  construction (contract test added). Prediction: wall-shear rel-L2
  within the W1/W1' band (0.102–0.108, i.e. +12% to +19% over v3c's
  0.091) — the penalty is the lost channels, not the gate.
- **true7** (the fix): replace the two pseudovectors with the *true*
  vectors e_φ,n × d̂ and e_φ,d × n̂ (pseudovector × vector =
  vector), restoring seven directions with exact reflection
  covariance and no gating (contract test: reflection and rotation
  exact to 1e-10). Prediction: wall shear within 3% of v3c
  (≤ 0.094) and pressure within seed spread (≤ 0.066). Falsifier:
  wall shear > 0.100 (> 10% over v3c) → the specific pseudovector
  directions carry something no true-vector completion supplies,
  which would reopen the labels question at the *query-point* level
  (a model-in-the-loop covariance check at exactly mirrored points).

If true7 lands, MT2 gains exact O(3) covariance (rotations *and*
reflections) at no accuracy cost, and the parity_fix gate is
retired in its favour. 18/18 contract tests pass.

## 2026-09-02 — L2 verdict: dropping the pseudovector channels costs +23% wall shear, and the "true7" arm was a derivation error; the real constraint is coefficient parity (W2 preregistered) {#sec-nb-l2-verdict}

**Results** (DrivAerML val, 2 seeds; v3c reference 0.0632 pressure /
0.0910 wall shear):

| basis | pressure | wall shear |
|---|---|---|
| true5 (drop e_φ channels) | 0.0707 (+12%) | 0.1120 (+23%) |
| "true7" (e_φ,n×d̂, e_φ,d×n̂ added) | 0.0716 (+13%) | 0.1146 (+26%) |
| W1 raw gate / W1' tanh gate | +8.6% / +6.2% | +18.8% / +12.6% |

**true5 confirms the capacity reading**: removing the two
pseudovector channels costs about what gating them did (a little
more — the gates at least kept them alive away from the symmetry
plane). **true7 fails its falsifier (> 0.100) — but the arm was
invalid, and the reason is the finding.** e_φ,n × d̂ is perpendicular
to e_φ,n, hence lies in span{r̂, n̂}; likewise e_φ,d × n̂ ∈ span{r̂, d̂}.
The two "new" vectors added no direction, so true7 ≡ true5 within
seed noise, exactly as observed. My derivation error, disclosed.

**The correct statement of the problem.** {r̂, n̂, d̂} already span
R³, so *every* direction is available; what differs is the parity of
the coefficient needed. Components along true-vector directions take
even coefficients; the component along e_φ ∝ n̂ × r̂ (a
pseudovector direction) needs a **parity-odd coefficient**, and the
trunk emits only even invariants. The unconstrained head fakes it
with even coefficients (breaking covariance, M3), the gates supply
oddness through a single pseudoscalar p = r̂·(n̂×d̂) that vanishes
on the entire symmetry plane and wherever r̂, n̂, d̂ are coplanar
(W1, W1'), and the true-vector bases give up the direction (L2).
L1b's finding that the unconstrained head's predictions are already
mirror-symmetric fits: it learned an approximately covariant function
by *using* the e_φ directions off-plane; the exact versions took
those directions away.

**W2 preregistered here: the odd-coefficient head.** Build K = 7
pseudoscalars per point — the triple product of {r̂, n̂, d̂} plus six
triple products involving the point's soft slice anchor position ẑ
and anchor normal m̂ (true, equivariant vectors from a
measure-weighted assignment) — and set each e_φ coefficient to
Σ_k p_k g_k(h) with g even. Exactly O(3)-covariant (reflections and
rotations) and translation-invariant by construction (contract test,
19/19 passing, including a liveness check that the odd channels are
not silently zero); not extinguished where any single pseudoscalar
vanishes. Two seeds, frozen v3c protocol. **Prediction, in readout
units:** wall shear ≤ 0.094 (within 3% of v3c) and pressure ≤ 0.066.
**Falsifier:** wall shear > 0.100 → the even-coefficient pseudovector
head's advantage is not about parity at all but about optimization
(e.g. the two extra unconstrained channels acting as a
better-conditioned overparameterization), which would be tested next
by an unconstrained 9-channel head.

## 2026-09-02 — Independent critic review: two of MT2's stated contracts are not implemented; M4 closure retracted; program reframed {#sec-nb-critic-review}

At Peter's request a fresh-context critic reviewed the whole written
record with no framing from the program (report:
`results/critic_review_2026-09-02.md`, 17 graded claims). The two
most consequential findings were **verified in-session against the
code** before being accepted:

1. **MT2 is not scale-equivariant** (critic C4, confirmed). A
   geometric 2x rescale of the input (points ×2, areas ×4) changes
   the output by **63%** (fp64, random weights). `reference_length`
   is a constant 8.0, and the only "scale" contract test ever written
   (`test_measure_weight_scale_invariance`) checks measure-*weight*
   rescaling — exact to 1e-16 — not geometry. Every chapter that
   calls MT2 "similarity-equivariant" is wrong; the correct statement
   is SE(3)-equivariant (rotations + translations), with a fixed
   length gauge. **Consequence:** the M1 scale-relaxation arm
   (@sec-nb-m1-verdict-wave-close) tested nothing — it appended a
   log-size feature to a model that already saw absolute size — so
   its "refuted" verdict is void, and the literature synthesis's
   over-symmetrization hypothesis was never actually tested.
2. **MT2 is not measure-complete** (critic C6, confirmed). The
   centroid is an unweighted `points.mean`; under 10:1 biased density
   it shifts by **0.94 RMS radii**. The M4 "closed by derivation"
   verdict (@sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg) is **retracted** — the audit
   missed the very first line of the geometry reduction. The P3
   density floor (4.3–4.5x) therefore has an implementation
   component after all.
3. **The drive-degree-1 contract is vacuous in deployment** (C7): the
   recipe feeds a unit vector (`U_inf_dir`), so the output scaling by
   |drive| is identically 1; and physically pressure is degree 2 in
   speed, Cp degree 0. The contract test is exact and the contract is
   irrelevant.

Also accepted from the report: MT2's peak memory is 9.8 GB against
GeoTransolver's 4.6 GB on the same DrivAerML protocol (C16 — the
review chapter's cost table is wrong); the "DrivAerML gap was label
noise" framing survives in chapter 17 despite N1 retracting it
(C14); every 2026-08/09 verdict is two seeds without a paired
statistic; the HiLift dataset config lives only job-locally on AGA;
and the program has been optimizing a 48-case DrivAerML val ratio
rather than its stated boundary→interior generalization objective
(volume recipes exist in the tree and MT2 has never run on them).
Two claims I do not yet accept without checking: that the G3 MT1 arm
used the moment decoder with the proved m ≤ 2 ceiling rather than
the kernel decoder that chapter 6 reports at 0.075 on frequency-OOD
(being re-run, below), and the exact 3.7x density-sensitivity figure.

**Actions taken today, all preregistered before running:**

- **S1 — a real similarity gauge.** New flag `similarity_gauge`:
  measure-weighted centroid and measure-weighted RMS-radius
  normalization replace the unweighted mean and the constant
  reference length. Contract test added for *geometric* scale
  equivariance (points ×k, areas ×k² → identical output) alongside
  the existing weight-scale test. Arms: v3c + gauge, 2 seeds,
  DrivAerML frozen protocol, then the P3 biased-density probe and the
  SHIFT-SUV zero-shot pair on the new checkpoints. Predictions in
  readout units: in-family within seed spread of v3c (≤ 0.066); **P3
  density ratio drops from 4.3–4.5x to below 2x** (the unweighted
  centroid was the dominant density leak); zero-shot estate improves
  from 0.83–0.90 (a truly similarity-covariant model cannot bind to
  DrivAerML's absolute size). Falsifier for the last: estate
  unchanged within seed spread → absolute size was not the transfer
  leak and the G2 mechanism list is back to GeoTransolver's
  pointwise features.
- **P1' — GeoTransolver canonicalization control** (eval-only): align
  each input to a canonical frame from U_inf (and the geometry's
  principal axes for the remaining rotation), run the frozen GT
  checkpoint, rotate outputs back; re-read the P1 rotation orbit. If
  GT recovers its in-pose accuracy off-pose at zero training cost,
  the "equivariance is worth 1.6x" headline is void and MT2's
  rotation robustness is a convenience, not a capability.
- **G3' — rerun the G3 ladder's MT1 arm with the kernel decoder** to
  resolve the chapter-6-vs-G3 contradiction on frequency
  generalization (< 3 GPU-hours).

**Reframing accepted.** MT2 should be described as an SE(3)-equivariant
soft-slice transformer with a learned local geometry basis; the
differentiators that survive are exact rotation/translation
covariance (with the O(3) extension under test in W2), learning-rate
robustness, and the measurement methodology. "Similarity-equivariant",
"measure-complete", "equal-or-lower cost", "drive-degree contract",
and "the DrivAerML gap was noise" are retired from the book pending
the S1 result, and chapters 02 and 17 will be corrected in the same
pass that records S1.

## 2026-09-02 — G3 frequency verdict OVERTURNED: the kernel-decoder MeshTransformer generalizes across BC frequency content (T1 0.070 vs 1.00); the original arm measured a proved nullspace {#sec-nb-g3-kernel-rerun}

**The critic's confound was real.** G3's `mt1_linear` arm used the
*moment* query decoder (`make_model("mesh_transformer", "reference")`,
recorded in every artifact's config block), and chapter 3
(`#sec-ceiling`) *proves* that decoder can emit only angular orders
m ∈ {0, 1, 2} in linear scalar mode. G3's T1 test — drive modes 5–8
with the constant removed — is entirely m ≥ 3 content, so
rel-L2 ≈ 1.0 was structurally guaranteed. The notebook's sentence
"the model has simply never learned the harmonic response to those
modes … a data/coverage limit, not an architecture gap"
(@sec-nb-g3-verdict) was wrong for that arm: it *could not represent*
them. Chapter 6's kernel-decoder result (freq-OOD 0.0748) is on the
same suite and the same OOD axis, under a different training protocol.

**Rerun** (post-hoc decoder control, labelled as such, not
preregistered): arm `mt1_kernel` = the singular-only exact
double-layer kernel decoder, otherwise identical to `mt1_linear`
(linear field mode, explicit gauge, reference capacity; 104k vs 136k
parameters, inside the arm range). Same training set, seeds, epochs,
optimizer, evaluation; ORD job 33696718, 3 seeds. Artifacts
`results/g3/g3_partial_mt1_kernel_seed*.json`,
`results/g3/g3_reduction_with_kernel.json`.

| arm | T0 | T1 modes 5–8 | T2a ×2 | T2b ×4 | T3 geom |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **mt1_kernel** | **0.0158** | **0.0701** (4.4×) | 0.0163 (1.03×) | 0.0154 (0.97×) | **0.0232** (1.46×) |
| mt1_linear (moment) | 0.0723 | 1.0043 (13.9×) | 0.0667 (0.92×) | 0.0632 (0.87×) | 0.0898 (1.24×) |
| mt2_bscalar | 0.0624 | 1.1485 (18.4×) | 0.3883 (6.2×) | 0.7289 (11.7×) | 0.0669 (1.07×) |
| softslice_2d | 0.1114 | 1.2090 (10.9×) | 0.4979 (4.5×) | 0.7760 (7.0×) | 0.1221 (1.10×) |

**Verdict.** The kernel-decoder MeshTransformer **does generalize
across boundary-condition frequency content** (T1 0.070, 14× better
than the moment decoder's 1.00, reproducing chapter 6's 0.075 under
G3's protocol) and is the best arm on every axis: 4× lower
in-distribution error than the next best, exact amplitude
extrapolation from linearity, and the lowest geometry-OOD error. The
G3 "no architecture generalizes frequency content" line is
**retracted**; the correct statement is that the *soft-slice* family
(mt2_bscalar, softslice_2d) and the moment decoder fail on that axis,
while an exact-kernel decoder succeeds. The structural reading: an
exact Green's-function operator carries the PDE's spectral response
for free, whereas learned routing must have seen each mode.

**Why this matters for direction.** This is the strongest
generalization result the program owns, and it belongs to the
architecture line (MT1 / learned boundary-integral operators, chapters
3 and 6) that the program *pivoted away from* to chase DrivAerML
in-family accuracy with GT-class routing — the local hill the critic
identified. The open question is whether the mechanism transfers to
3D aerodynamics, where the exact kernel is the Laplace/potential-flow
double layer and viscous effects are corrections: a **3D
kernel-decoder arm on DrivAerML/HiLift** (the `learned_bie` line,
`results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`) is now the highest-value
unturned stone, to be preregistered against the G-ledger axes rather
than in-family accuracy alone.

## 2026-09-02 — P1' verdict: canonicalization gives GeoTransolver exact pose invariance at zero training cost, but a 1.15–1.7x in-pose penalty from sub-degree frame tilt; the "worth 1.6x" headline becomes "worth 1.15–1.2x, plus robustness to pose error" {#sec-nb-p1-canon-verdict}

**The control the critic asked for** (`results/p1_canonicalization_control_2026-09-02.json`;
eval-only, frozen GeoTransolver DrivAerML checkpoints, 2 seeds, 48 val
cases). Canonical frame: U_inf → +x, roll about it from the
area-weighted in-plane covariance (sign from the third moment;
0/48 cases within 5% of eigenvalue degeneracy), vector outputs rotated
back before the metric. Reproduction anchor held bit-for-bit (orbit
raw 32.2x / 30.1x). Incidental finding: the P1 probe's yaml says
"z-rotation" but the transform's default mode is uniform SO(3), so P1
has always been a full-orientation orbit (angles 44–179°) — a stronger
test than documented.

**Results** (pressure rel-L2; ratio to in-pose raw):

| pose | raw GT | canonicalized GT |
|---|---|---|
| in-pose | 0.0530 / 0.0533 (1.00x) | 0.0847 / 0.0918 (**1.60x / 1.72x**) |
| SO(3) orbit | 1.71 / 1.60 (32x / 30x) | 0.0847 / 0.0918 (same as in-pose) |
| yaw 90°, yaw 180°, roll 90° | 17–31x | identical to in-pose to 4 decimals |

Canonicalization makes GeoTransolver **exactly pose-invariant** at
zero training cost — but costs 1.6–1.7x in-pose. The follow-up
control explains why: **GeoTransolver is hypersensitive to sub-degree
frame tilt** — a fixed roll of 0.5° about U_inf costs 1.2–1.3x, 1°
costs 1.7–1.8x, 2° costs 3.2–3.4x, 5° costs 6.5–6.8x. The
canonical frame estimated from the 10,000-cell eval sample is off by
0.82° on average (max 2.2°); estimated from 1M cells it is off by
0.39°, and the canonicalization penalty falls to **1.15–1.19x**
(in-pose and orbit alike).

**Verdict.** The headline "exact equivariance is worth 1.6x" survives
only against rotation *augmentation* (1.84–1.91x). Against the
correct steel-man — canonicalized GeoTransolver with a well-estimated
frame — MT2's exact-equivariance advantage is **~1.15–1.2x**, not
1.6x, and the book's P1 framing must say so. What the control adds is
arguably more valuable than what it removes: a *quantified pose-error
sensitivity* for the non-equivariant baseline (1° → 1.7x) that MT2 is
immune to by construction. In any deployment where the freestream
direction or vehicle alignment carries even a degree of uncertainty,
that is the operative difference, and it is now a measured curve
rather than an argument.

**P1'' preregistered here** (the remaining steel-man step, launched
now): *train* GeoTransolver in the canonical frame (canonicalization
as a dataset transform, 2 seeds, frozen protocol otherwise), so the
model sees the estimator's sub-degree tilt noise during training.
Prediction: canonically trained GT lands within 1.05x of raw GT
in-pose and is pose-invariant; falsifier: penalty stays ≥ 1.15x → the
tilt sensitivity is intrinsic to GeoTransolver's coordinate features,
not an artefact of training in a single pose. Either outcome fixes
the honest exchange rate between exact equivariance and
canonicalization for the book.

## 2026-09-02 — 3D kernel arm scoped: the surface-to-surface kernel decoder already ran and was null; the right next step is a potential-flow oracle gate (K0), then a symmetric feature arm (K1) {#sec-nb-kernel3d-scoping}

**Scoping** (`results/kernel3d_arm_scoping_2026-09-02.md`), prompted
by the G3 kernel result (@sec-nb-g3-kernel-rerun). The naive plan —
"put the exact-kernel decoder on DrivAerML" — is already in the
record: `conf/model/mesh_transformer_surface_flagship.yaml` trained at
scale, and chapter 16's factorial (`#sec-drivaerml-factorial`) shows
its exact members buying 0–8% in-family and nothing zero-shot. The
document argues this null is *structural to the surface-to-surface
formulation* on a 0.1%-coverage point subsample (the exterior trace is
½I + compact K; exact panel integrals on a Monte Carlo sample carry a
~34% quadrature floor), not evidence against the 3D kernel mechanism.
The 2D result's leverage lives in boundary→interior — which is the
program's stated north-star objective, and the axis on which MT2 has
never been run (critic C-hill). Inventory: every piece that
*evaluates* a 3D Laplace kernel exists and is tested
(`kernel_decoder.py` triangle members, Barnes–Hut backend); every
piece that *solves* a learned BIE is 2D/complex-plane-bound.

**Preregistered, in readout units:**

- **K0 — potential-flow oracle gate (eval-only, zero parameters).**
  Exact 3D single/double-layer integrals on a closed coarse remesh per
  vehicle, Neumann data U_inf·n, Morino second-kind solve,
  Bernoulli Cp, compared to DrivAerML val pressure. **Gate: rel-L2
  < 0.90** (a viscous, separated car; prior 0.55–0.80). If the oracle
  is *worse* than that, "exact kernel = Laplace, viscous = learned
  correction" is refuted for this dataset and no learned kernel arm
  runs. Cost: eval-only, < 10 GPU-hours.
- **K1 — symmetric feature arm (conditional on K0 passing).** K0's
  field (Cp_pf and the tangential potential velocity, both exactly
  similarity-invariant with no reference length) as a declared input
  to *both* MeshTransformer2-v3c (lr 1e-3) and GeoTransolver (lr
  3e-3), 2 seeds each. Predictions: in-family unchanged (|Δ| ≤
  0.004); **SHIFT-SUV estate zero-shot improves** (MT2 0.997 → ≤ 0.85,
  GT 0.614 → ≤ 0.55); P3 density ratio ≤ 8x (from 13–14x for
  MT2-v3c on that instrument). Falsifier: neither architecture moves
  ≥ 0.10 on estate → the potential-flow prior does not carry
  transfer, K2 not launched.
- **K2 — mechanism arm (conditional on K1):** exact measure-weighted
  layer operators as a fixed exchange channel inside MT2's slice
  block.
- **K-alt (independent of K0–K2, admits the interior problem):** the
  existing kernel-decoder MeshTransformer, unchanged, on
  `drivaer_ml_volume.yaml` — boundary→interior, where the 2D
  mechanism's spectral leverage actually lives. Deferred until K0
  reads out, to keep the cluster share on S1/W2/P1''/ladder.

**Side facts from the scoping worth keeping:** the one G-ledger axis
the existing kernel-decoder arm already wins is P3 density bias
(1.7–2.1x vs GeoTransolver 3.6x vs MT2-v3c 13–14x on that probe
version); no watertightness check exists anywhere in the aero recipe
(K0 adds a Gauss-identity gate); degree 0, not MT2's degree 1, is the
correct drive law for pressure *coefficients*.

## 2026-09-02 — K0 gate FAILS: inviscid potential flow is not a usable prior for DrivAerML pressure (oracle rel-L2 4.8 vs 0.77 for the case mean); the 3D kernel line does not launch {#sec-nb-k0-verdict}

**Result** (`results/k0_potential_flow_oracle_2026-09-02.json`; 45 of
48 val cars passing the watertightness and Gauss-identity gates;
~6 GPU-hours). The zero-parameter exact potential-flow oracle —
Morino second-kind solve on a closed 4 cm marching-cubes remesh,
Bernoulli Cp, read at the recipe's exact 10,000 evaluation points —
scores a measure-weighted **rel-L2 of 4.79 (median 1.97, every case
> 1.6)** against the CFD pressure. On the same points, predicting
Cp = 0 scores 1.00 and Cp = case mean scores **0.774**. The
preregistered gate (< 0.90) **fails by a factor of five**, and no
numerical explanation survives the controls: clipping outliers gives
1.7; the oracle-optimal affine rescale reaches only 0.73; the remesh
resolution sweep (4/6/8 cm) shows no trend; the sphere validation is
exact (Cp error 0.07%, second-order convergence, Gauss identities to
1e-15). The physics is the failure: 69% of the surface has label Cp
in [−0.5, 0] — the separated-base pressure deficit — where inviscid
flow predicts ≈ 0 to +0.13, and inviscid suction peaks are 2–3× too
strong. **Verdict: for a bluff separated body, "exact kernel =
Laplace, viscous effects = correction" is refuted; K1 and K2 do not
launch on DrivAerML.**

**What this bounds.** The G3 kernel result (@sec-nb-g3-kernel-rerun)
stands: an exact Green's-function operator generalizes for free *when
it is the PDE's operator*. RANS aerodynamics of a car has no cheap
exact operator — the dominant physics is separation — so the
program's "structure buys generalization" thesis is bounded exactly
where the available structure stops matching the PDE. The remaining
kernel path is K-alt (a *learned* density through the exact 3D
double layer on the boundary→interior problem, where the operator is
at least the right *kind*), and it should be argued on that footing,
not on potential flow. Two repo findings for the recipe: the
DrivAerML `vehicle` patch is oriented inward (signed volume
−6.3 to −8.0 m³), and `physicsnemo.mesh.repair.fix_orientation`
propagates by normal dot-product, which fails across folds > 90°.

## 2026-09-02 — W2 collapsed in training (pressure 0.77, wall shear 0.74): an implementation failure, not a parity verdict; W2' (zero-init, bounded pseudoscalars) is the last rung of this thread {#sec-nb-w2-verdict}

The odd-coefficient head (@sec-nb-l2-verdict) trained to a
near-mean predictor on both fields — pressure 0.770 / 0.761, wall
shear 0.743 / 0.738 — so the shared trunk was wrecked, not just the
vector head. The preregistered falsifier fires trivially, but this is
**not** a scientific verdict on coefficient parity: the arm failed to
train. Likely causes, from the code: the odd gate was randomly
initialized (so from step 0 the head emitted large pseudovector-
direction outputs), and the anchor triple products were unbounded
(anchor positions are O(1) in the gauge, but the products enter
unnormalized). **W2'** (launched now, 2 seeds): the odd gate is
zero-initialized so training starts as the stable true5 head and the
odd channels grow from zero, and the anchors are unit-normalized so
every pseudoscalar lies in [−1, 1]; contract tests updated (O(3)
covariance verified with the gate perturbed to non-zero; 23/23).
Prediction unchanged: wall shear ≤ 0.094. **This is the final rung
of the parity thread**: five head variants have been trained
(W1, W1', true5, true7, W2); if W2' also fails to beat 0.100 the
program records "exact O(3) covariance of the vector head costs
≥ 10% wall shear on DrivAerML with every construction tried" and
moves on — the critic's hill-climbing warning applies here.

## 2026-09-03 — Parity thread CLOSED: W2' diverged to NaN at epoch 95; exact O(3) covariance of MT2's vector head costs ≥ 10% wall shear or fails to train under every construction tried {#sec-nb-parity-thread-closed}

W2' (zero-initialized odd gate, unit-normalized anchors, bounded
pseudoscalars) reached epoch 95 and produced `Train Loss: nan`
(both seeds; lanes cancelled at once). With the cap declared in
@sec-nb-w2-verdict, the thread closes. Ledger of the six
constructions, all on the frozen DrivAerML protocol (v3c reference:
pressure 0.0632 / wall shear 0.0910):

| head | reflection covariance | pressure | wall shear |
|---|---|---|---|
| v3c default (pseudovector channels, even coeffs) | violated (M3) | 0.0632 | **0.0910** |
| W1 raw gate p | exact | +8.6% | +18.8% |
| W1' tanh(p/0.1) | exact | +6.2% | +12.6% |
| true5 (channels dropped) | exact | +12% | +23% |
| true7 (invalid: replacements ∈ span{r̂,n̂}) | exact | +13% | +26% |
| W2 odd head (K=7 pseudoscalars) | exact | collapsed 0.77 | 0.74 |
| W2' zero-init, bounded | exact | **NaN @95** | — |

**Closing statement for the book.** MT2's vector head reaches the
e_φ (pseudovector) directions with parity-even coefficients, which
formally violates reflection covariance (M3). The labels are
mirror-covariant to < 1% energy (L1) and the trained head's
predictions are empirically as covariant as the exactly constrained
ones (L1b), so the violation is a *representation convenience* the
optimizer uses, not a physical error the model makes. Every exact
construction tried either removes needed capacity (gates, true
bases: ≥ 12% wall-shear penalty) or destabilizes training (odd
coefficient heads: collapse, NaN). The default head is retained;
`parity_fix`, `vector_basis`, and `odd_head` stay in the code as
documented negative results. The unexplored fix — parity-odd
*features in the trunk* rather than a bolt-on odd head — is left for
MT3's design and is not pursued further here, per the critic's
hill-climbing warning. Six trained variants on one head is where a
demanding reviewer would say stop; we stop.

## 2026-09-03 — P1'' verdict: GeoTransolver trained in the canonical frame is exactly pose-invariant at 1.01x cost; the exact-equivariance accuracy headline is gone {#sec-nb-p1pp-verdict}

**Result** (`results/p1pp_canonical_training_2026-09-03.json`;
2 seeds, DrivAerML val, metrics in the original frame). GeoTransolver
trained with the canonicalization transform in its pipeline (U_inf →
+x, principal-axis roll, the realistic 10,000-cell frame estimate):

| pose | canonically trained GT (s42 / s43) | raw GT reference |
|---|---|---|
| in-pose, no canon at eval | 0.0536 / 0.0535 | 0.0530 / 0.0533 |
| in-pose, canon at eval | 0.0535 / 0.0534 | 0.0847 (1.60x) |
| SO(3) orbit, canon at eval | **0.0536 / 0.0534** | 0.0847 |

**The preregistered prediction held (≤ 1.05x): the penalty is 1.01x.**
The sub-degree tilt hypersensitivity that cost the frozen raw
checkpoint 1.6–1.7x (@sec-nb-p1-canon-verdict) was an artefact of
training in one exact pose; a model that sees the estimator's tilt
noise during training simply learns to ignore it. Canonically trained
GeoTransolver is **exactly pose-invariant** (orbit = in-pose to four
decimals) at a **1% accuracy cost**, with zero architectural change.

**What this does to the program's claims.** The P1 headline —
"exact rotation equivariance is worth 1.6x" — is **retired**. Its
honest replacement: *given a known freestream direction and a
geometry with a resolvable principal frame (both true for every
vehicle dataset in this program; 0/48 degenerate cases),
canonicalization delivers the same pose invariance as exact
equivariance at ~1% cost and no architectural constraint.* The
augmentation baseline (1.84–1.91x) that made equivariance look
valuable was the wrong steel-man. MT2's exact equivariance remains a
genuine *contract* — it holds for any geometry, including ones whose
principal frame is degenerate or whose freestream is unknown — but on
the datasets this program measures, it is not an accuracy advantage.
Combined with high-lift parity (@sec-nb-hl-verdict) and the retired
scale/measure claims (@sec-nb-critic-review), the differentiators MT2
still holds on measured axes are: learning-rate robustness (R1) and
whatever the HiLift generalization ladder shows. This is the critic's
"single biggest risk" materializing, and it is better known than
assumed.

**Generality caveats, so the retirement is not over-read:**
canonicalization needs a known freestream (true in aerodynamics, not
in every PDE surrogate setting) and a sign-resolvable principal frame
(cars: skewness sign 48/48 consistent; a symmetric body would need
another disambiguator); the equivariant model needs neither.

## 2026-09-03 — S1 verdict: the real similarity gauge is free in-family and cuts MT2's biased-density penalty from 13–14.5x to 1.20x; zero-shot transfer unchanged {#sec-nb-s1-verdict}

**Result** (`results/s1_similarity_gauge_2026-09-03.json`; 2 seeds
each, seed-matched against v3c; configs differ only in
`similarity_gauge: true`):

| run | in-family p / wss | estate | fastback | P3 biased (10:1) | P3 ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **v3c + gauge** s42 / s43 | 0.0638 / 0.0922 · 0.0629 / 0.0896 | 1.036 / 0.862 | 1.039 / 0.856 | 0.0766 / 0.0758 | **1.20x / 1.20x** |
| v3c s42 / s43 | 0.0636 / 0.0916 · 0.0627 / 0.0904 | 0.946 / 0.988 | 0.979 / 0.984 | 0.926 / 0.812 | 14.55x / 12.95x |

**Prediction 1 (in-family within seed spread): held.** The
measure-weighted centroid and RMS-radius gauge cost nothing on either
field. **Prediction 2 (P3 density ratio < 2x): held decisively** —
the 10:1 biased-sampling penalty falls from **13–14.5x to 1.20x** on
the p3v3 instrument (biased-sampling error 0.077 against a uniform
0.064). The unweighted centroid *was* the dominant density leak, and
the earlier "information-limited floor" reading (M4,
@sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg, already retracted in @sec-nb-critic-review)
is now positively refuted by measurement: the floor was an
implementation gap. With the gauge, MT2 is the most density-robust
architecture the program has measured on this instrument
(GeoTransolver 3.6x, kernel-decoder MeshTransformer 1.7–2.1x,
MT2-v3c 13–14.5x, **MT2-gauge 1.20x**) — and it is exactly the
property the SE(3) + measure contracts were supposed to deliver.
**Prediction 3 (zero-shot estate improves): falsifier fired.** Estate
0.949 mean vs 0.967, inside a two-seed spread of 0.17 and inside
v3c's own cross-seed range (0.90–1.12); fastback identical. Absolute
size was not the transfer leak; the G2 mechanism list reverts to
GeoTransolver's pointwise features. Disclosure: the preregistration
quoted a v3c estate baseline of "0.83–0.90" that matches no v3c run
(seeds 42–46 span 0.90–1.12) — a transcription error, the third
threshold/baseline slip this week, caught by the seed-matched
re-reduction.

**Adoption.** `similarity_gauge=true` becomes the reference MT2
configuration for all new runs (frozen checkpoints keep the constant
gauge; the flag stays default-off in code for that reason and the
book's MT2 description now states both). The HiLift ladder's MT2
lanes predate this and are recorded as v3c-constant-gauge. The honest
MT2 claim set after this week: exact SE(3) equivariance as a
contract (not an accuracy edge, P1''); learning-rate robustness
(R1); **biased-density robustness at 1.2x** (S1); in-family parity
with GeoTransolver on high-lift and a 1.085x deficit on DrivAerML at
best-vs-best learning rates.

## 2026-09-03 — G5 preregistration drafted (PRE-DATA): single-factor generalization on the forthcoming cfd-datagen corpus; dataset recommendations filed {#sec-nb-g5-prereg}

Peter is generating a new 3D RANS corpus (`~/gh/cfd-datagen`) designed
to isolate generalization factors. A forked session reviewed it and
filed two artifacts, archived here verbatim:
`results/cfd_datagen_feedback_2026-09-03.md` (recommendations to the
dataset run: counterfactual *twin* draws per random-number namespace —
pose, physics, scale, layout, mesh — so single-factor tests are exact
rather than marginal; multiple draws for the val/test geometry banks;
mesh-refinement twins for a per-stratum discretization-error floor;
`body_id` on the no-slip boundary; export of half-window
block-difference fields; realized-regime diagnostics) and
`results/g5_cfd_datagen_generalization_preregistration_2026-09-03.md`
(status PRE-DATA; kept as prose rather than converted to JSON so
nothing is lost in translation).

**G5 in one paragraph.** Six arms on the new corpus, every threshold
in readout units: **A1 pose twins** (exact SE(3) axis — MT2's twin
difference must sit at its own mesh-realization floor; raw
GeoTransolver fails by ≥ 5x on the two profiles without a freestream
frame; canonicalized GeoTransolver matches MT2 within 1.05x where a
frame exists); **A2 scale twins** — the *first real test of the
similarity gauge*, at fixed Reynolds number across 0.02–20 m
(GeoTransolver predicted to exceed 2x at a 10x scale change); **A3
Reynolds twins** (coverage axis — prediction from G2/G3: no
architecture transfers a decade of Re better than another); **A4 mesh
twins** (the label-noise floor that defines "resolvable" for every
other arm — a between-architecture difference smaller than the floor
is reported as not resolvable); **B1 bank-held-out geometry** (the
strong G2, at two training sizes to test the transfer-slope
hypothesis); **B2 profile-held-out boundary conditions** (do explicit
BC operators buy anything on realized 3D flows). Architectures:
GeoTransolver raw and canonicalized, MT2 with the gauge, the
kernel-decoder MeshTransformer as the GLOBE-lineage arm; surface task
first, then the boundary→interior volume task the program has never
run MT2 on. The A-arms are void unless the twin-draw recommendation is
adopted, which is why the preregistration exists before generation.
Tech tree: node **G5 PLANNED**, gated on the corpus launch.

## 2026-09-03 — HiLift ladder, data-efficiency rungs: MT2 is 2.5–2.9x more accurate than GeoTransolver at 35 and 210 training cases, converging to parity at 1,260 {#sec-nb-hl-ladder-dataeff}

**First half of the ladder readout** (prereg `499bcfe8`;
`results/hilift_ladder_reduction_2026-09-03.json`). Both
architectures at lr 1e-3 (each one's best on the full split), 500
epochs, 2 seeds, evaluated on the *shared* 180-case val set that the
`full`, `scarce` and `super_scarce` splits have in common — so these
three rungs are directly comparable:

| training cases | GeoTransolver (min–max) | MeshTransformer2 (min–max) | MT2 / GT |
|---|---|---|---|
| 35 (`super_scarce`) | 0.392 (0.375–0.409) | **0.138** (0.135–0.141) | **0.35** |
| 210 (`scarce`) | 0.159 (0.157–0.160) | **0.064** (0.062–0.067) | **0.41** |
| 1,260 (`full`) | 0.042 | 0.041 | 0.98 |

**Prediction P1 of the preregistration held, and not marginally.**
MT2 is **2.9x more accurate at 35 cases and 2.5x at 210**, with seed
spreads an order of magnitude smaller than the gap; MT2 trained on 210
cases (0.064) is already as good as GeoTransolver trained on 1,260
would have been on DrivAerML (0.053–0.063 range), and better than
GeoTransolver on 210 by the same factor the whole month-one DrivAerML
chase was about. The curves cross to parity only at the full split.
This is the **first measured architecture-driven generalization
advantage in 3D** in the program — on data-efficiency, the axis the
north-star correction named first — and it is the Branch A condition
of the MT3 decision rule (`results/mt3_preregistration_skeleton_2026-09-03.md`,
r(35) ≤ 0.85; measured 0.35).

**Steel-man before believing it (preregistered now, launched now).**
The protocol holds epochs fixed, so at 35 cases both models take ~9
optimizer steps per epoch — 4,500 steps total — and the ladder
inherited lr 1e-3 from the full split. GeoTransolver's collapse at
small n could be under-training or an lr mismatch at small n rather
than an architectural property; on DrivAerML's G1 ladder the same
protocol gave parity at n = 14, which argues against that, but it is
cheap to test: **GeoTransolver `super_scarce` and `scarce` at lr 3e-3
(500 epochs) and at lr 1e-3 with 1,000 epochs, 2 seeds each (8 small
lanes).** Prediction: the best of these stays ≥ 2x MT2 at 35 cases.
Falsifier: any GeoTransolver control within 1.2x of MT2 at 35 cases →
the data-efficiency gap is a protocol artefact and the Branch A
decision is void. The OOD half of the ladder (aoa, stall) is still
training; its verdict and the single sealed test evaluation follow.

## 2026-09-04 — HiLift ladder training complete: in-distribution results on the OOD splits, and the sealed test protocol declared before it runs {#sec-nb-hl-ladder-ood-indist}

**All 16 ladder lanes trained and evaluated on their own validation
sets** (`results/hilift_ladder_reduction_2026-09-03.json`). The two
OOD-axis splits train on their low-side populations (aoa: 788 cases
at low angle of attack; stall: 942 pre-stall cases) and validate on
in-distribution held-out cases from the same populations:

| split (train n) | GeoTransolver s42 / s43 | MT2 s42 / s43 | MT2 / GT |
|---|---|---|---|
| aoa (788) | 0.0285 / 0.0317 | 0.0205 / 0.0209 | **0.69** |
| stall (942) | 0.0289 / 0.0304 | 0.0204 / 0.0210 | **0.70** |

These are *in-distribution* numbers and extend the data-efficiency
curve (@sec-nb-hl-ladder-dataeff) with two more rungs: MT2/GT is
0.35 at 35 cases, 0.41 at 210, ~0.70 at 788–942, 0.98 at 1,260. The
absolute errors are lower than on the full split because the low-AoA
and pre-stall populations are attached-flow cases.

**Sealed test evaluation — protocol declared here, before any test
case is read.** Per the ladder preregistration (`499bcfe8`), the
HiLift test splits are evaluated exactly once. What runs: the eight
OOD-lane checkpoints (aoa and stall × both architectures × seeds
42/43), each on *its own split's curated test list* (`aoa_test`: 900
high-AoA cases; `stall_test`: 723 post-stall cases) taken verbatim
from the dataset's `manifest.json`, with the frozen inference
configuration (resolution 10,000, val-identical sampling seed, the
same `infer.py`). No data-efficiency lane touches test. Readouts, in
the units of the MT3 decision rule
(`results/mt3_preregistration_skeleton_2026-09-03.md`):
d_axis = (OOD-test pressure rel-L2) / (in-distribution val pressure
rel-L2) per architecture and seed. **Predictions** (from the ladder
prereg): stall is the harder axis for both (d_stall > d_aoa);
GeoTransolver's transfer compounding (G2) predicts d_GT < d_MT2 on at
least one axis. **Decision rule** (Branch B trigger): d_GT ≤ 0.8 d_MT2
on an axis, resolvable above seed spread → run the raw-coordinate
mechanism discriminator before any MT3 design; otherwise Branch A
(data-efficiency) stands. No reruns, no configuration changes after
the numbers are seen; if a lane fails for an infrastructure reason,
it is rerun with the identical configuration and the failure is
recorded.

**2026-09-04 addendum — first steel-man control lands: the lr
hypothesis is refuted at 35 cases.** GeoTransolver `super_scarce` at
lr 3e-3 (500 epochs, 2 seeds): pressure **0.392 / 0.481** — no better
than its lr 1e-3 ladder lanes (0.375 / 0.409), and worse on one seed,
against MT2's 0.135–0.141. The preregistered falsifier (a control
within 1.2x of MT2, i.e. ≤ 0.166) is not approached: GeoTransolver's
small-data collapse is not a learning-rate mismatch. The
under-training hypothesis (1,000-epoch lanes, currently past epoch
500 of 1,000) and the 210-case controls remain to be read; the
data-efficiency result (@sec-nb-hl-ladder-dataeff) stands provisional
on those alone.

## 2026-09-04 — Sealed test verdict: both architectures degrade ~10x on AoA and stall extrapolation; MT2 keeps the lower absolute error, GeoTransolver the smaller ratio; Branch B triggers on stall {#sec-nb-hl-sealed-test}

**One-shot evaluation, run exactly as declared**
(@sec-nb-hl-ladder-ood-indist; `results/hilift_sealed_test_2026-09-04.json`;
job 657341; 900 high-AoA and 723 post-stall test cases; no reruns, no
failures).

| axis | model | in-dist val p | OOD test p | d = test/val | OOD test velocity / wss |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| aoa | GeoTransolver | 0.0285 / 0.0317 | 0.300 / 0.330 | **10.5** | 0.22 / 0.34 |
| aoa | MT2 | 0.0205 / 0.0209 | **0.241 / 0.248** | 11.8 | 0.25 / 0.37 |
| stall | GeoTransolver | 0.0289 / 0.0303 | 0.274 / 0.277 | **9.3** | 0.19 / 0.33 |
| stall | MT2 | 0.0204 / 0.0210 | **0.261 / 0.259** | 12.6 | 0.19 / 0.32 |

**Reading, in order of importance.** (1) **Neither architecture
generalizes across a physical-regime boundary.** Extrapolating from low
to high angle of attack, or from attached to separated flow, costs
both models roughly a factor of ten in pressure error; the OOD test
errors (0.24–0.33) are worse than the *35-case* in-distribution error.
This is the 3D analogue of G3's frequency-content null: coverage of
the regime, not architecture, governs this axis. (2) **MT2 keeps the
lower absolute OOD error on pressure on both axes** (0.244 vs 0.315
aoa; 0.260 vs 0.276 stall), so its in-distribution advantage shrinks
but does not invert. (3) **GeoTransolver has the smaller degradation
*ratio*** because its in-distribution floor is higher (0.030 vs
0.021): the two architectures converge to similar OOD error from
different starting points. Prediction "stall harder than aoa" held for
MT2 only.

**Decision rule, applied by the letter.** The MT3 skeleton's Branch B
trigger is d_GT ≤ 0.8 d_MT2, resolvable above seed spread: aoa gives
0.885 (not triggered); **stall gives 0.741 with disjoint seed
intervals (worst-case pairing 0.769) — triggered.** So the
preregistered next step is the mechanism discriminator, not an MT3
design. **Caveat, stated before it runs:** this trigger is driven by
the denominator. A ratio criterion rewards a worse in-distribution
model, and in absolute OOD terms MT2 is ahead; a reader should weigh
the discriminator's *absolute* OOD readout at least as heavily as the
ratio. The rule is followed because it was committed in advance and
because the question it asks — is GeoTransolver's residual transfer
edge carried by pointwise raw-coordinate features? — is worth a cheap
answer either way.

**B1 — raw-coordinate discriminator, preregistered here.** MT2 with
the similarity gauge plus a `raw_coord_channel` that appends the raw
gauge-normalized coordinates and normal components to the seed
invariants, deliberately breaking SE(3) equivariance (24/24 contract
tests, including one asserting it *does* break rotation equivariance).
Two seeds, `stall` split, lr 1e-3, 500 epochs, otherwise frozen.
Readouts: in-distribution val pressure; OOD stall-test pressure; d.
**Predictions in readout units:** if pointwise raw features carry
transfer, MT2+raw's d moves at least halfway from MT2's 12.6 toward
GeoTransolver's 9.3 (d ≤ 11.0) *and* its absolute OOD pressure drops
below 0.245; if it does not (d ≥ 12.0 or OOD pressure ≥ 0.255), the
carrier is elsewhere and the next discriminator is a GeoTransolver
ablation removing its raw coordinates. **Test-split use:** the sealed
protocol permitted one evaluation of the existing models; B1 requires
one additional evaluation on `stall_test`, limited to the two new B1
checkpoints only, with the identical configuration — declared here,
before the lanes exist. No previously evaluated model is re-evaluated.

**2026-09-05 operational addendum (AGA I/O degradation).** Since the
evening of 2026-09-04 every running lane on AGA (B1 and the six
remaining GeoTransolver controls) has been I/O-bound: per-step times
of 4–6 s with individual stalls of 400+ s against a normal 0.27 s, so
an epoch takes 400–560 s instead of 60–140 s. This coincides with the
admins' network isolation work (their requeue of the last ladder lane
was the first symptom). I mis-read the flat epoch counters as a hang
and cancelled the running links; the chain-ahead successors resumed
from checkpoints within a minute at a cost of ≤ 5 epochs per lane, but
the slowdown persists on the new nodes, so it is storage/fabric-side,
not job-side. At the current pace B1 needs ~2 more days rather than
~10 hours. No configuration is changed; the lanes run until the
cluster recovers. Lesson recorded: the recipe's log timestamps are
cluster-local (UTC−7); compare them to `date`, not `date -u`.

**2026-09-05 protocol note (validation cadence).** To get the B1
discriminator and the remaining GeoTransolver controls through AGA's
I/O degradation, the recipe gained an optional `training.val_interval`
(default 1; commit `710999a0`) and the eight running lanes were
resumed from their checkpoints with `val_interval=25`. This changes
*nothing* about training: validation feeds only the log line and
metric table, while checkpointing and the scheduler are independent of
it (verified in `train.py` before the change), and every headline
number comes from the separate `infer.py` evaluation of the final
checkpoint. It does change the wall-clock: per-epoch full-validation
passes were the dominant cost under slow I/O. Recorded so the
B1/control train logs' sparser validation lines are not mistaken for a
protocol difference against the ladder lanes.

## 2026-09-05 — Same-family control preregistered: plain Transolver on the HiLift data-efficiency rungs (is the 2.8x MT2's contracts, or GeoTransolver's geometry encoder?) {#sec-nb-transolver-control-prereg}

**Why.** The AB-UPT baseline scoping
(`results/abupt_baseline_scoping_2026-09-05.md`) found no AB-UPT in
PhysicsNeMo (a faithful surface variant is 31–44 engineer-hours and
needs a design note from the primary paper first), but a plain
**Transolver** is already recipe-ready (`conf/model/transolver_surface.yaml`)
and has never been run on HiLiftAeroML. It is the same attention
family as GeoTransolver with no geometry encoder, no ball-query
context path, and no MT2 contracts — exactly the control that
separates two readings of the data-efficiency result
(@sec-nb-hl-ladder-dataeff): *MT2's geometric contracts buy small-data
accuracy* versus *GeoTransolver's geometry encoder loses it*.

**Arm T1 (launched now).** Transolver on `super_scarce` (35) and
`scarce` (210), 2 seeds each, lr 1e-3 (GeoTransolver's best on the
full split; Transolver has no prior tuning on this dataset, so a 3e-3
sibling is added at 35 cases only, 2 seeds, to cover the lr axis
cheaply), 500 epochs, val_interval 25, otherwise the frozen ladder
protocol; scored on the shared 180-case val set. **Predictions in
readout units:** Transolver at 35 cases lands in GeoTransolver's band,
0.30–0.50 (the gap is contract-specific); **falsifier:** Transolver
≤ 1.3 × MT2 = **≤ 0.18 at 35 cases** → the advantage is not
MT2-specific, GeoTransolver's geometry encoder is the small-data
liability, and the headline must be restated before publication. A
secondary readout at 210 cases (MT2 0.064, GT 0.159) discriminates the
same way with the 1.3x bar at 0.084. The sealed test split is not
touched by this arm.

## 2026-09-05 — Scheduling entry: north star restated (accurate, generalizable, useful surrogates for steady boundary-driven 3D PDEs); the ready frontier is boundary→interior {#sec-nb-sched-2026-09-05}

Peter restated the goal as advancing "a more accurate, generalizable,
and ultimately *useful* model architecture for steady, boundary-driven,
3D PDE-governed physical systems." Reconciling the tech tree against
that statement:

- **Running** (cluster, I/O-degraded): B1 raw-coordinate discriminator
  (Branch B of the MT3 rule), the GeoTransolver small-n steel-man
  controls (first of four refuted the lr explanation), and the T1
  plain-Transolver same-family control on the small-data rungs. Together
  they decide whether the data-efficiency headline
  (@sec-nb-hl-ladder-dataeff) is MT2-specific and whether GeoTransolver's
  residual OOD edge is its raw-coordinate features.
- **Ready and unmeasured, and the closest to the restated goal:**
  boundary→interior prediction. Every result so far is surface-to-surface.
  The program's scope statement, the critic (C-hill), and the 2D kernel
  result all point at the interior task as the axis where exact-operator
  structure has leverage and where query-independence becomes a
  first-class property (interior queries are never tokens). MT2 has no
  native off-surface decode path — its query-independent read blocks
  require query normals — so this is an architecture step, not just a
  dataset switch. Scoping dispatched (`results/volume_arm_scoping_2026-09-05.md`
  when it lands): data contract of the volume recipes, readiness of
  GeoTransolver-volume and the kernel-decoder MeshTransformer flagship,
  the minimal covariant normal-free query mode for MT2, and a pilot-gated
  V0 arm with predictions in readout units.
- **Deferred:** AB-UPT implementation (gated on T1), G5 (gated on the
  cfd-datagen corpus), MT3 design (gated on B1 + controls + V0).

## 2026-09-05 — T1 verdict (35 cases): plain Transolver lands in GeoTransolver's band (0.40–0.63), not MT2's 0.14; the data-efficiency gap is MT2-specific {#sec-nb-t1-35-verdict}

**Result** (same shared 180-case val set as the ladder; 2 seeds each):

| model @ 35 training cases | lr | pressure rel-L2 |
|---|---|---|
| Transolver | 1e-3 | 0.634 / 0.616 |
| Transolver | 3e-3 | **0.406 / 0.398** |
| GeoTransolver (ladder, lr 1e-3; control lr 3e-3) | | 0.375 / 0.409; 0.392 / 0.481 |
| **MeshTransformer2** (ladder, lr 1e-3) | | **0.135 / 0.141** |

**Prediction held; falsifier (Transolver ≤ 0.18) not approached.** The
same-family, no-geometry-encoder Transolver collapses at 35 cases
exactly as GeoTransolver does (its best, 0.40 at lr 3e-3, sits inside
GeoTransolver's 0.30–0.50 band), so the small-data liability is not
GeoTransolver's geometry encoder and the 2.8x advantage is not an
artefact of one baseline. Two Transolver-family architectures at their
better learning rate are 2.8–2.9x behind MT2 at 35 cases. Transolver
also shows the same lr sensitivity as GeoTransolver (1.55x between
1e-3 and 3e-3), consistent with R1. The 210-case Transolver lanes are
still training and will be read the same way (bar: ≤ 0.084).

**What this does and does not establish.** It establishes that the
data-efficiency advantage belongs to something MeshTransformer2 has
that neither Transolver-family model has: the candidates are the exact
SE(3) equivariance, the measure-weighted soft-slice routing, and the
invariant local geometry basis. It does not yet say *which*; the
natural next discriminator is a single-factor ablation of MT2 at 35
cases (equivariance broken via the raw-coordinate channel already
built for B1; measure weights off; local basis off), one flag at a
time, 2 seeds each — cheap at this rung (~4 epochs/minute) and
preregistered below as A35. A faithful AB-UPT implementation remains
gated: with two Transolver-family models already in the same band,
the marginal information from a third is low relative to its 31–44
engineer-hour cost.

**A35 preregistered here.** MT2 at 35 cases, lr 1e-3, 2 seeds per arm:
(i) `raw_coord_channel=true` (breaks SE(3)); (ii) `use_measure_weights=false`;
(iii) `use_local_features=false` if the default config has them on,
else this arm is the gauge on/off pair (`similarity_gauge` true vs
the v3c constant gauge). Readout: shared-val pressure rel-L2 vs the
ladder's 0.138. **Prediction:** breaking equivariance costs the most
(≥ 1.5x, i.e. ≥ 0.21), measure weights matter less at uniform
sampling (≤ 1.15x), the gauge is neutral in-family (S1). **Falsifier
for the equivariance reading:** the raw-coordinate arm within 1.15x of
0.138 → equivariance is not what buys small-data accuracy and the
routing/basis becomes the candidate.

## 2026-09-05 — V0 preregistered: the first boundary→interior measurement (DrivAerML volume), with MT2's new interior-query mode {#sec-nb-v0-prereg}

**The architecture step.** MT2's query-independent decode required a
normal at every query, so it could not decode off-surface points.
The `interior_queries` mode derives an equivariant proxy normal per
query from the source anchors — the geometric soft assignment of the
query position to the slice anchors (width `anchor_normal_rho`, gauge
units), applied to the anchor mean normals — so every existing
invariant, read block and the vector head work unchanged. No new
learned modules (the thin-pipe collapses of v5a1/v5a2 and W2 argue
against them). Contract test: off-surface queries without normals are
exactly SE(3)-covariant (1e-10) and query-set independent (1e-12);
25/25 pass. Explicit query normals (e.g. SDF normals) override the
proxy, which gives a zero-code companion arm.

**Scoping** (`results/volume_arm_scoping_2026-09-05.md`): the
DrivAerML volume recipe is a complete boundary→interior contract
(interior points with velocity/pressure/nut targets, the subsampled
vehicle boundary kept alongside with measure weights, per-point SDF
and SDF normals); GeoTransolver-volume is wired but has never produced
a number in this program; the kernel-decoder MeshTransformer decodes
at interior points natively and needs only a yaml (flagship minus the
trace terms); HiLift volume is not runnable as committed. All arms
share a dataset variant adding the freestream direction, the
reference length, the degenerate-cell guard, and a scalars-first
target order (MT2 emits scalars then vectors).

**V0 arms, pilot-gated** (1 seed × 50 epochs; gate: pressure rel-L2
≤ 0.6 and descending, ≤ 60 GB, ≤ 1 s/step), then 2 seeds × 500
epochs at the frozen protocol: GeoTransolver-volume; MT1-kernel-volume;
MT2-interior (proxy normals); MT2-interior-sdf (SDF normals as query
normals). **Predictions in readout units** (val-mean interior
pressure rel-L2 ratios; no absolute volume number exists in the record,
so absolute bands are priors, not predictions): MT2-interior / GT in
[1.3, 2.5] — falsifiers ≤ 1.2 (the v5 entanglement finding was
surface-specific) and ≥ 3.0 (no MT2 interior product without query
interaction); MT1-kernel / GT in [1.5, 3.0] on pressure and
[1.0, 2.0] on perturbation velocity, **and ≤ 1.0x GT in the far band
(SDF ≥ 0.5 L_ref)** — MT1 ≥ 1.5x GT there closes the kernel line for
good. **New ledger axes this task enables** (eval-only on the V0
checkpoints): exact query-independence as a first-class property
(interior queries are never tokens for MT1/MT2-interior, always
tokens for GeoTransolver), query-resolution transfer at fixed source,
SDF-band-stratified error, and surface-trace consistency against the
surface labels the boundary tokens already carry.

**A35 launched alongside** (@sec-nb-t1-35-verdict): MT2 at 35 cases with
one factor removed at a time — equivariance (raw-coordinate channel),
measure weights, gauge — to name which of MT2's ingredients buys the
data-efficiency result.

**2026-09-05 addendum — steel-man controls 3 of 4 in: none approaches
the falsifier.** GeoTransolver at 35 cases: lr 3e-3 → 0.392 / 0.480;
1,000 epochs at lr 1e-3 → 0.373 / 0.429 — versus its ladder lanes
0.375 / 0.409 and the 1.2x-MT2 bar of 0.166. At 210 cases: lr 3e-3 →
0.220 / 0.290, *worse* than the ladder's 0.159, versus a bar of
0.077. Neither more optimizer steps nor a higher learning rate moves
GeoTransolver toward MeshTransformer2 at small n; together with the
T1 Transolver result (@sec-nb-t1-35-verdict) the data-efficiency
advantage is now robust to learning rate, training length, and the
choice of Transolver-family baseline. The last control pair
(210 cases, 1,000 epochs) is still training; the hero figure's
"provisional" footnote comes off when it lands.

## 2026-09-05 — V0 pilot gate: all four boundary→interior arms pass; GeoTransolver leads the interior task 2.9–6x at 50 epochs; promoted to 2 seeds × 500 epochs {#sec-nb-v0-pilot}

**First boundary→interior numbers in the program** (DrivAerML
volume, 48 val cases, 10,000 interior query points and 10,000 boundary
tokens per case, 50-epoch pilots, seed 42, lr 1e-3; interior rel-L2):

| arm | pressure | velocity | nut | vs GT (pressure) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver-volume | **0.093** | **0.169** | **0.159** | 1.0 |
| MT2-interior (SDF query normals) | 0.269 | 0.397 | 0.631 | 2.9x |
| MT2-interior (anchor proxy normals) | 0.375 | 0.482 | 0.715 | 4.0x |
| kernel-decoder MeshTransformer | 0.577 | 0.605 | 0.817 | 6.2x |

**Gate (≤ 0.6 and descending): all four pass**, the kernel arm
barely. Facts fixed by the launch: 150–166 million interior points per
case on disk (the model sees a 10,000-point sample, ~6e-5 coverage);
the volume manifest is the surface instrument's own 435/48 split; all
arms fit in 4–9 GB at ~0.35 s/step.

**Early reading, not a verdict.** GeoTransolver dominates the interior
task at pilot stage: MT2's query-independent read path is 2.9–4x
behind, echoing the surface-era finding that passive decoding costs
accuracy (v5a3: 2.7–3.9x), and the exact-kernel decoder is 6x behind,
echoing its surface null. Two of the preregistered predictions
(@sec-nb-v0-prereg) are already under pressure: MT2-interior/GT was
predicted in [1.3, 2.5] with a falsifier at ≥ 3.0 (the proxy-normal
variant sits at 4.0 at pilot; the SDF variant at 2.9), and MT1-kernel/GT
in [1.5, 3.0] (6.2 at pilot). Pilot ratios can move with 10x more
training, so the full runs decide; if they hold, the honest statement
for the goal is that *for boundary→interior on this task, token-level
query interaction (GeoTransolver's) is worth ~3x over passive
equivariant decoding, and the exact Laplace kernel buys nothing* —
which would locate the "useful architecture" question squarely in how
to give MT2 interior queries interaction without giving up
query-independence. Also worth noting for the SDF-band readout to
come: SDF query normals beat the anchor-derived proxy by 1.4x, so the
query's local geometry information matters more than its exact
covariance recipe.

**Promotion:** all four arms to 2 seeds × 500 epochs at the frozen
protocol (val_interval 10), then the full eval battery including the
SDF-band stratification and the exact query-independence check.

## 2026-09-05 — A35 verdict: exact equivariance is NOT what buys the data-efficiency (raw coordinates cost nothing); measure weights *hurt* at 35 cases; the invariant seed parameterization and the relational routing are the surviving candidates (A35b preregistered) {#sec-nb-a35-verdict}

**Result** (MT2 at 35 HiLift cases, shared val pressure rel-L2, 2 seeds;
reference MT2 ladder 0.135 / 0.141, mean 0.138):

| ablation | pressure (s42 / s43) | vs reference |
|---|---|---|
| + raw coordinates (breaks SE(3) equivariance) | 0.1430 / 0.1430 | **1.04x** |
| measure weights OFF | **0.1210 / 0.1231** | **0.88x** |
| similarity gauge ON | 0.1510 / 0.1471 | 1.08x |

**The equivariance reading is falsified.** Adding raw coordinates,
which makes MT2 non-equivariant, changes the 35-case error by 4% — far
inside the 1.15x falsifier band — so exact SE(3) equivariance is not
the ingredient that buys the 2.8x small-data advantage. Two further
surprises: turning **measure weights off improves accuracy by 12%** at
35 cases (uniform 10k sampling makes the area weights a source of
gradient variance rather than information; the density robustness
they buy (S1) is a different axis), and the gauge is 8% *worse* at this
rung (neutral in-family at full data, S1). Note the raw-coordinate arm
still *has* the invariant seeds — it adds coordinates on top — so the
invariant feature parameterization {|r|, r̂·d, r̂·n, n·d} remains a
live candidate even though exactness does not matter.

**A35b preregistered here** — the two remaining candidates, one flag
each, 2 seeds, 35 cases, lr 1e-3 (implemented and contract-tested:
27/27): (i) `seed_mode=raw` — the five invariant seeds *replaced* by
the raw vectors [r, n, d] (GeoTransolver-style inputs; breaks
equivariance); (ii) `use_relational_geo=false` — the anchor-relational
invariants removed from slice routing and readback (Transolver-style
feature-only slicing; stays exactly equivariant). **Predictions:** if
the invariant seed set is the carrier, (i) degrades ≥ 1.5x (≥ 0.21)
and (ii) stays within 1.15x; if the relational routing is the carrier,
the reverse; if neither moves ≥ 1.3x, the advantage is distributed and
the honest statement becomes "MT2's soft-slice design as a whole,
not any single contract". Falsifier for the whole line: both within
1.15x. The ablations launch now under the existing A35 script pattern.

**2026-09-05 addendum (A35b launch incident).** The `use_relational_geo=false`
lanes died at step 1 under DDP with "parameters that were not used in
producing loss": the slice blocks built their relational-geometry
projections unconditionally and skipped them in forward. Fixed in the
job-local copy for the relaunch and ported to the repo with a
regression test that checks every parameter receives a gradient for
each flag variant (32/32) — the single-process contract suite could not
have caught this. Both A35b variants are now training and accepted; an
early, non-readout observation is that the no-relational-geometry
variant runs at 2.0 GB versus 9.8 GB for every other MT2 arm and trails
in validation loss at epoch 50.

## 2026-09-05 — Full V0 verdict: on boundary→interior, GeoTransolver's token-level query interaction is worth 2.6–3.1x over MT2's passive equivariant decode and 8x over the exact-kernel decoder; Branch V launches {#sec-nb-v0-verdict}

**Result** (DrivAerML volume, 48 val cases, 10,000 interior queries
from 10,000 boundary tokens, 500 epochs, lr 1e-3, 2 seeds; interior
rel-L2, `results/a35_v0_reduction_2026-09-05.json`):

| arm | pressure (s42 / s43) | velocity | nut | pressure vs GT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver-volume | **0.0622 / 0.0618** | **0.133** | **0.094** | 1.0 |
| MT2-interior, SDF query normals | 0.166 / 0.153 | 0.308 | 0.372 | **2.57x** |
| MT2-interior, anchor proxy normals | 0.195 / 0.191 | 0.337 | 0.418 | **3.11x** |
| kernel-decoder MeshTransformer | 0.499 / 0.492 | 0.549 | 0.727 | **8.0x** |

**Against the preregistration** (@sec-nb-v0-prereg). MT2-interior/GT
was predicted in [1.3, 2.5] with falsifiers at ≤ 1.2 and ≥ 3.0: the
SDF-normal variant lands at 2.57 (just outside the band, above it) and
the proxy-normal variant at 3.11 (**falsifier fires**: without query
interaction there is no MT2 interior product). The kernel decoder was
predicted in [1.5, 3.0]: **8.0x**, far outside; its preregistered
lifeline is the far-band readout (SDF ≥ 0.5 L_ref ≤ 1.0x GT), which is
being computed from the saved per-point predictions and is not
expected to survive an 8x aggregate deficit. Seed spreads are 1–8% of
the means, so every ratio is resolvable.

**Reading for the restated goal.** The 2D lesson (an exact operator
generalizes for free when it *is* the PDE's operator) does not carry to
separated 3D aerodynamics in either form the program tried: the
potential-flow prior is useless (K0) and the learned-density kernel
decoder is 8x behind a plain attention model on interior fields. What
*does* separate the architectures on the interior is **interaction at
the query**: GeoTransolver treats interior queries as tokens that
attend to everything; MT2's passive read of slices, boundary tokens and
a local kernel loses 2.6x even with the best query-side geometry (SDF
normals), and 3.1x with the covariant proxy. Query-side local geometry
matters (SDF normals buy 1.2x over the proxy), but the dominant term is
interaction. This locates the useful-architecture problem exactly where
the MT3 skeleton's Branch V put it: give interior queries interaction
*without* making predictions depend on the batch of queries.

**Decision rule applied: Branch V launches.** MT2-interior/GT ≥ 2.0 on
both variants → the equivariant latent-volume-token arm
(`latent_volume_tokens`, K = 3·n_slices + 1 interacting tokens placed
covariantly off the boundary; built and contract-tested 2026-09-05,
@sec-nb-sched-2026-09-05) runs on the SDF-normal base: 1-seed
50-epoch pilot (gate: pressure ≤ 0.6 and descending, memory fits),
then 2 seeds × 500 epochs. **Prediction in readout units:**
MT2-interior-LVT / GT ≤ 1.5 (halving the gap) with exact query
independence retained (1e-12). **Falsifier:** ≥ 2.0 → interaction at
the query itself is required; the honest product is then
"GeoTransolver for interior accuracy, MT2 for contracts," and the next
candidate is interaction with a canonical probe set re-computed per
request but never across the request's queries.

## 2026-09-05 — SDF-band stratification: the exact-kernel line closes (far-band velocity 16.7x GT; its "≤1.0x pressure" is a zero-output artefact); MT2's interior deficit grows with distance from the wall {#sec-nb-v0-sdf-band}

**Method** (`results/v0_sdf_band_2026-09-05.json`; eval-only on the
saved full-V0 predictions; the 10k interior sample and its SDF are
bit-identical across all eight runs; the all-points band reproduces the
aggregate metrics to five digits). Preregistered bands in the recipe's
centred nondimensional frame with L_ref = 8: near < 2 m, mid 2–20 m,
far ≥ 20 m physical. The sample is overwhelmingly near-wall (97.8% /
2.0% / 0.12%; median SDF 5 mm), so the far band holds 4–25 points per
case; a 2.5 m far band (1.8% of points) is reported alongside.

**Kernel-decoder verdict: the line closes.** On the preregistered far
band the kernel decoder's pressure ratio is 0.59x GT — *formally* the
≤ 1.0x survival criterion, but it is an artefact: its far-field
pressure output has decayed to exactly zero (|Cp| < 1e-6 against a true
RMS of 0.0055), which is the trivial rel-L2 floor of 1.000 in every case,
and GeoTransolver scores 1.71 there only because its ~0.01 Cp error
exceeds that tiny signal. On the one well-conditioned far field,
velocity (true RMS 0.95 |U∞|), the kernel decoder is **16.7x GT**
(perturbation velocity 22x; RMS error 0.34 |U∞| vs 0.027). In the 2.5 m
band its pressure is 4.5x and velocity 8.6x GT. There is no SDF band
under any definition where the kernel decoder is within 1.5x of
GeoTransolver on velocity. **The preregistered falsifier fires; the
0.59x pressure number is not survival and is not reported as such.**
Together with K0 and the surface-era factorial, the exact-Laplace
kernel is now closed for separated 3D aerodynamics on every readout
the program owns.

**MT2-interior, stratified** (SDF-normal variant, pressure / velocity
vs GT): near 2.54x / 2.28x → mid 3.7x / 4.7x → far 3.3x / 5.4x. The
scoping document predicted the passive-decode price would be worst
*near* the wall (a local-detail deficit); it is the opposite:
**near-wall is MT2's best band and the deficit grows with distance.**
That is the signature of missing *volumetric* context, not missing
local detail — the slices and anchors are boundary-centric and the
local kernel readout sees only boundary tokens, so far-field queries
have nothing off-surface to read. This is exactly the gap Branch V's
latent volume tokens are built to fill (@sec-nb-v0-verdict), so the
LVT pilot now has a specific stratified prediction: its gain over the
SDF-normal base should be *larger in the mid and far bands than near
the wall*. A GeoTransolver weakness surfaces too: far-band pressure
rel-L2 of 1.71 — worse than predicting zero 20 m from the body.

**2026-09-05 addendum — Branch V pilot gate: passes, but the prediction
is under pressure from the start.** MT2-interior with SDF query normals
plus latent volume tokens, 50 epochs, seed 42: interior pressure
**0.340**, velocity 0.445, nut 0.756 — against the SDF-normal base's
own 50-epoch pilot of 0.269 / 0.397 / 0.631. The gate (≤ 0.6 and
descending) passes, so per the rule the arm promotes to 2 seeds × 500
epochs; but at pilot length the 769 latent tokens make the model 1.26x
*worse*, not better, and the same comparison held throughout training
(epoch-49 val loss 0.035 vs 0.026). Two readings are possible and the
full run separates them: the extra tokens slow early convergence
(the base itself improved 1.68x from pilot to full), or they dilute the
measure-weighted slice routing that the boundary tokens rely on. The
preregistered full-run prediction (LVT/GT ≤ 1.5) and falsifier (≥ 2.0)
stand unchanged; the stratified prediction (gain largest in the mid/far
bands) will be read from the SDF-band analysis on the full checkpoints.

## 2026-09-05 — T1 verdict (210 cases): plain Transolver lands at 0.091, above the 0.084 bar but 1.8x better than GeoTransolver; MT2's edge at 210 is 1.4x against the best same-family baseline {#sec-nb-t1-210-verdict}

**Setting.** The HiLift data-efficiency ladder (@sec-nb-hl-ladder-dataeff)
measured MeshTransformer2 (MT2) 2.5x more accurate than GeoTransolver at
210 training cases (pressure rel-L2 0.064 vs 0.159 on the shared 180-case
validation set). The same-family control preregistered at
@sec-nb-transolver-control-prereg trains plain **Transolver** — the same
soft-slice attention family as GeoTransolver, with no geometry encoder,
no ball-query context and none of MT2's contracts — on the same rungs,
to separate "MT2's structure buys small-data accuracy" from
"GeoTransolver's geometry encoder loses it". At 35 cases the verdict was
clean (@sec-nb-t1-35-verdict): Transolver collapsed into GeoTransolver's
band. This entry reads the 210-case rung.

**Result** (lr 1e-3, 500 epochs, 2 seeds, shared val set;
`results/t1_transolver_control_reduction_2026-09-05.json`):

| model @ 210 training cases | lr | pressure rel-L2 | vs MT2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver (ladder) | 1e-3 | 0.160 / 0.157 | 2.5x |
| GeoTransolver (steel-man control) | 3e-3 | 0.220 / 0.290 | 4.0x |
| **Transolver** | 1e-3 | **0.092 / 0.089** | **1.4x** |
| **MeshTransformer2** (ladder) | 1e-3 | **0.062 / 0.067** | 1.0 |

**The preregistered bar holds, narrowly, and the honest reading is a
qualification.** The falsifier was Transolver ≤ 1.3x MT2 = 0.084; the
measured 0.0905 mean is 1.41x MT2, so the advantage is still
MT2-specific at this rung. But Transolver is **1.76x more accurate than
GeoTransolver** at 210 cases with the identical learning rate, whereas at
35 cases the two were at parity (0.40 vs 0.39 at each one's better lr).
Most of the 2.5x MT2/GeoTransolver gap at 210 is therefore GeoTransolver
falling behind its own backbone, not MT2 pulling ahead of the family: the
geometry encoder and context path that GeoTransolver adds are a liability
between 35 and 210 cases on this dataset. The full-split rung (1,260) has
no Transolver lane, and GeoTransolver reaches MT2 parity there (0.042 vs
0.041), so whether the geometry encoder ever pays for itself on HiLift is
open — a 1,260-case Transolver pair would answer it but is a benchmarking
question, not an architecture one, and is parked.

**What changes.** The hero figure (@fig-hilift-data-efficiency) now
carries the Transolver series and both factors per rung, and its caption
states the claim as: *2.9x at 35 cases against both baselines; 1.4x
(Transolver) to 2.5x (GeoTransolver) at 210; parity at 1,260*. The
architecture question A35/A35b is asking — which MT2 ingredient carries
the small-data advantage — is unchanged, because the 35-case rung, where
the effect is largest, is exactly where all Transolver-family variants
collapse together.

**Steel-man applied to the control too.** Transolver at 210 cases was
run only at lr 1e-3; at 35 cases it preferred 3e-3 by 1.55x. Two lanes at
210 cases and lr 3e-3 (seeds 42, 43; `t1_hl_transolver_scarce_lr3e3_*`)
launched now, same protocol. **Prediction:** they land within 0.08–0.10
(lr 3e-3 helps less at 210 than at 35, as it did for GeoTransolver, which
got *worse*). **Falsifier of the 1.4x statement:** Transolver lr 3e-3 ≤
0.070 → MT2's 210-case advantage over the best same-family baseline is
within seed spread and the figure's 210-rung annotation must say so.

## 2026-09-05 — Derivation from the A35b memory anomaly: MT2's peak training memory falls 2.75x (9.8 → 3.6 GB at 10k tokens) from an exact pool-then-project rewrite; MT2 now trains in less memory than GeoTransolver {#sec-nb-geo-pool-memory}

**Setting.** The critic review (@sec-nb-critic-review, C16) established
that MeshTransformer2 (MT2) costs about twice GeoTransolver's peak
training memory on the DrivAerML surface protocol — 9.8 GB against
4.6 GB at 10,000 surface tokens — and chapter 17 retired the
"equal-or-lower cost" claim on that basis. The A35b ablation launch
(@sec-nb-a35-verdict, addendum) then produced an anomaly: the
`use_relational_geo=false` variant, which removes the anchor-relational
invariants from slice routing and readback, trained at **2.0 GB** while
every other MT2 arm sat at 9.8 GB. Removing eight scalar features per
point–slice pair should not remove four fifths of the memory. This
entry derives where the memory actually goes and removes it exactly.

**The derivation, from the code rather than the description.** In each
slice block, MT2 forms the relational invariants
`geo` of shape (B, N, S, 8) — for every point and every slice anchor,
the distance, its log, and six direction cosines — and uses them twice:
a linear map to one logit per pair refines the routing, and a linear map
to hidden/2 features per pair, pooled over slices with the point's slice
mixture, is read back into the point. The second use was written as
"project, then pool": `einsum(mix, geo_feat(geo))`. Autograd saves the
projected tensor (B, N, S, hidden/2) for the backward pass of the einsum.
At the recipe's dimensions (N = 10,000, S = 256, hidden = 192, so
hidden/2 = 96) that is 2.5e8 elements, about 0.5 GB in bfloat16, **per
layer, times twelve layers ≈ 5.9 GB**, plus the (B, N, S, 8) invariants
and the (B, N, S, 3) direction tensors saved for the dot products (a
further ~1 GB). The relational-geometry path accounts for roughly 7 GB
of the 9.8 GB, which is exactly the 9.8 → 2.0 GB drop the ablation
exposed. The invariants themselves are cheap; the *projected* pairwise
activation is the cost.

**The fix is an identity, not an approximation.** The projection is
affine, $W g + b$, and the slice mixture is a softmax over slices, so
$\sum_s m_{ns} (W g_{ns} + b) = W \sum_s m_{ns} g_{ns} + b$. Pooling
first and projecting second — `geo_feat(einsum(mix, geo))` — produces
the same tensor and saves a (B, N, 8) activation instead of
(B, N, S, hidden/2). The same rewrite applies to the passive read blocks
of the decoder. Nothing about the model changes: same parameters, same
function, same contracts.

**Verification.**

- Exactness: a new contract test checks the identity on both block
  types at fp64 to 1e-12 absolute (33/33 tests pass); at the model level,
  the old and new code with identical weights differ by 3.9e-15 max
  absolute (1.3e-15 relative) in fp64 on a 4,000-point cloud.
- Memory, measured locally (RTX 4090, forward + backward under bf16
