recipe configuration on the cluster while collecting per-arm memory for the
resources paragraph (results/v0_interior_resources_2026-09-07.json):

| arm | parameters | peak memory per GPU | inputs |
|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver-volume (`geotransolver_volume.yaml`) | 27,574,449 | 8.8 GB | interior points only, each with coordinates, signed distance to the full-resolution surface and its gradient; U_inf globally; geometry encoder on the interior cloud; `include_local_features: true` with radii 0.01–5.0 (six ball queries) |
| ISLA passive decode (`mt2_volume.yaml`) | 9,942,855 | 4.9 GB | 10,000 surface cell centroids, normals, areas; freestream direction; query positions; SDF-gradient normal at the query in the SDF arm |
| ISLA + latent volume tokens | 10,030,856 | 5.8 GB | as above plus 769 latent tokens |
| exact-kernel MeshTransformer (`mesh_transformer_volume.yaml`) | 761,749 | 4.0 GB | boundary sample + drive |
| ISLA query tokens (training) | 8,866,870 | 6.0 GB | as the passive arm, queries as interacting tokens |

The GeoTransolver volume configuration does not consume the boundary
surface at all; its knowledge of the geometry comes from the signed
distance field, a function of the full-resolution surface evaluated at every
query point, and from local features among the interior points. Its 27.6M
parameters are the surface backbone plus the six-radius local-feature
encoder that the surface configuration switches off. Per-step times at
10,000 + 10,000 points are 0.04–0.05 s for every arm except the query-token
ISLA (0.28 s), whose per-slice geometry now spans 20,000 tokens.

**What changes.** The interior chapter's task, resources, architecture and
results sections, its standing statement, the index paragraph, the limits
section and the claims ledger now state the three simultaneous differences
between the arms (interaction among query tokens; the signed-distance
input; 2.8x parameters with local features) and no longer attribute the
2.6x to interaction alone. The query-token arm is the matched-mechanism
test of the first difference; its pilot (0.103/0.108 against 0.269 passive
at 50 epochs) already says interaction carries most of the gap at that
point, and its 500-epoch readout lands today. Nothing numerical in the
results table changes; the parameter and memory columns are now per arm
and correct. The exact-kernel arm's parameter count, previously "not
recorded", is 0.76M.

**Why it was missed.** The 9.0M figure was carried over from the surface
comparison, where it is correct; the volume configuration lives in a
separate file with a different local-feature setting, and no earlier
pass read the volume lanes' start-up banner. The rule now in CLAIMS.md is
that resource figures on any task are read from that task's lane logs.

## 2026-09-07 — Preregistered: query tokens with the signed distance as an input (matched-input steel-man for ISLA on the interior); plus a scale-contract fix for query tokens {#sec-nb-qt-sdf-prereg}

**Setting.** The ledger correction of today (@sec-nb-interior-resources-correction)
established that GeoTransolver's volume configuration receives, at every
interior point, the signed distance to the wall as an input, while every
ISLA interior arm receives at most the wall normal (the SDF gradient). The
query-token arm (@sec-nb-qt-prereg), now at epoch 200 of 500, isolates the
interaction difference; this arm isolates the input difference on top of it.

**Change to the model** (commit 16b62765a). `n_query_scalars` adds per-query
scalar inputs to the query tokens: each scalar s is divided by the gauge and
entered as the pair [s, sign(s)·log|s|] through a small embedding added to
the query token's seed. Scalars are invariants, so rotation, translation
and (with the similarity gauge) geometric-scale covariance are untouched;
the test asserts all three to 1e-10 in fp64. Writing that test exposed a
pre-existing gap: the query tokens' learned routing log-weight was
absolute, while the surface tokens' log-weights are log cell areas and
shift by 2 log k under a rescale by k, so query-token ISLA under the
similarity gauge changed its output by 0.145 (relative L2 units of the
test) under a 3.7x rescale. The query log-weight is now learned relative
to the mean surface log-weight, which restores the exact contract (1e-15).
The two query-token lanes in training use the pre-fix snapshot; on
DrivAerML with its fixed reference length the difference is a constant
offset absorbed by the learned weight, and they are read out with the
snapshot they trained with.

**Hypothesis and bars.** *H-input:* with interaction already supplied by
the query tokens, giving ISLA the signed distance closes most of what
remains to GeoTransolver-volume. Readout: interior pressure relative L2 on
the 48 validation cars, two seeds, 500 epochs, same protocol as the
query-token lanes (`v0_isla_qt_sdf_seed{42,43}`), run as
`v0_isla_qtsdfval_seed{42,43}` with `+model.n_query_scalars=1
+forward_kwargs.query_scalars=interior.point_data.sdf` and otherwise the
query-token configuration. *Supported* if QT-SDF/QT ≤ 0.85 (the scalar is
worth at least 15% of error); *falsified* if QT-SDF/QT ≥ 0.95; between,
inconclusive. Secondary: if QT-SDF/GT ≤ 1.1 the interior gap is closed at a
third of the parameters (8.9M vs 27.6M) and two thirds of the memory
(6.0 vs 8.8 GB). Launched when the query-token lanes release their nodes
(the 32-node budget is fully allocated); code snapshot `code_isla2`
(commit 16b62765a plus the reader compaction of the same day).

## 2026-09-07 — Addendum to the DrivAerML verdict: the two architectures rank the cars identically; ISLA's shortfall is a near-constant factor per car {#sec-nb-drivaer-percase}

**Question.** If the DrivAerML gap is case-level rather than spatial
(@sec-nb-drivaer-station-verdict), is it the *same* cases that are hard for
both architectures, with ISLA uniformly a little worse, or does each model
fail on its own cars?

**Instrument.** Per-case surface-pressure relative L2 from the in-family
evaluations of the same seed pairs (`sweep/<run>/res10000/**/metrics.jsonl`,
48 validation cars), Spearman rank correlation between ISLA and
GeoTransolver, compared with each model's rank correlation with itself
across seeds (results/drivaer_percase_correlation_2026-09-07.json).

**What we saw.** ISLA's and GeoTransolver's per-case errors are rank-correlated
at 0.89 (seed pair 45) and 0.86 (pair 46); each model against its own other
seed is 0.87. The per-case ratio ISLA/GeoTransolver has 10th–90th
percentiles of 1.11–1.30 (pair 45) and 1.15–1.38 (pair 46), and GeoTransolver
is more accurate on 47 and 48 of the 48 cars.

**Reading.** Which cars are hard is a property of the data, agreed on by both
architectures to within seed noise; ISLA's error is that shared difficulty
multiplied by a nearly constant 1.2–1.3. Together with the spatial
uniformity, this is the signature of a uniform fit deficit (capacity or
optimisation at the operating point), not of a case class or a surface
region where ISLA's inductive bias fails. It sharpens the closed
direction: no region-, case- or geometry-targeted mechanism would move the
DrivAerML gap; only something that lifts the whole fit would.

## 2026-09-07 — At 35 and 210 HiLift cases the two architectures disagree on which cases are hard (ρ 0.57, 0.64 against seed self-consistency 0.88–0.97); at 1,260 they agree (0.94) — the opposite of DrivAerML {#sec-nb-hilift-percase}

**Question.** The DrivAerML addendum (@sec-nb-drivaer-percase) found ISLA and
GeoTransolver ranking the 48 cars identically, with ISLA's error a constant
factor on a shared difficulty ordering. Is HiLift's small-data advantage
the same kind of object, ISLA uniformly better on a shared ordering, or
does GeoTransolver's small-data failure land on cases of its own?

**Instrument.** Per-case surface-pressure relative L2 from the wave-1 and
wave-2 validation evaluations on the shared 180 cases (two-seed mean per
architecture per case), Spearman rank correlation between the two
architectures, against each architecture's rank correlation with its own
other seed; the 10th/50th/90th percentile of the per-case ratio
GeoTransolver/ISLA (results/hilift_percase_correlation_2026-09-07.json).

| rung | ρ ISLA vs GeoTransolver | ρ GeoTransolver seed 42 vs 43 | ρ ISLA seed 42 vs 43 | GT/ISLA per-case ratio p10 / p50 / p90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 35 cases | **0.57** | 0.94 | 0.97 | 1.81 / 3.13 / 4.61 |
| 210 cases | **0.64** | 0.88 | 0.96 | 1.67 / 3.08 / 3.94 |
| 1,260 cases | 0.94 | 0.94 | 0.95 | 0.92 / 1.06 / 1.18 |
| single angle, 126 geometries (18 held-out geometries) | 0.63 | 0.92 | 0.96 | 4.27 / 4.97 / 5.97 |

**Reading, first pass (superseded below).** Each architecture is highly
consistent with itself across seeds at every rung, so the low
cross-architecture correlations at 35 and 210 cases are not noise. The
first reading was that GeoTransolver's small-data errors fall on cases of
its own, an idiosyncratic failure pattern; the follow-up in the next
paragraph shows that is the wrong picture.

**Reading, corrected the same day.** Correlating each model's per-case
error with candidate drivers (results/hilift_error_drivers_2026-09-07.json)
shows that GeoTransolver's error at small data barely varies by case: its
coefficient of variation across the 180 cases is 0.15 at 35 cases and 0.19
at 210, against 0.44 and 0.64 for ISLA. Both models' errors rise with angle
of attack (ρ 0.56 for GeoTransolver, 0.61 for ISLA at 35 cases), and
neither tracks how far a case's field is from uniform (|ρ| ≤ 0.19 against
the constant-mean predictor scores). So the low cross-architecture
correlation is the signature of a nearly case-independent predictor
(GeoTransolver at small data, as the reference-predictor comparison in
@sec-nb-strat35 already said) against one whose error varies three to four
times more because it has learned the case-to-case physics; the two cannot
be rank-correlated, and at 1,260 cases, once GeoTransolver's error also
tracks the physics, they are (0.94). On DrivAerML both models track the
physics at every size and the orderings coincide throughout. The two
datasets thus show one object from two sides: on HiLift at small data,
ISLA has learned the case-to-case variation and GeoTransolver mostly has
not; on DrivAerML both have, and ISLA's fit is uniformly a little worse.

**What it adds to the mechanism question.** Nothing about which cases;
the question is what lets ISLA learn the case-to-case variation from 35
high-lift cases when GeoTransolver's error stays flat. The unseen-geometry
ladder now finishing measures that on geometries never seen at any angle.

**Next discriminator (not run).** The hypothesis this suggests, that
GeoTransolver interpolates locally in geometry space and fails on validation
geometries far from any training geometry while ISLA does not, has a direct
test: the distance from each validation geometry to its nearest training
geometry (the dataset ships no design-parameter table, so a Chamfer distance
between subsampled STL surfaces would serve), correlated with each
architecture's per-case error at 35 cases. Prediction under the hypothesis:
GeoTransolver's error correlates with that distance (ρ ≥ 0.5) and ISLA's
does not (ρ ≤ 0.2); a shared correlation would instead say the difficulty is
intrinsic and the decorrelation above comes from something else. It costs a
CPU job over 180 surfaces and is queued behind the running arms.

## 2026-09-07 — Seen versus unseen geometries at 35 cases: GeoTransolver gains nothing from having trained on a geometry (0.390 vs 0.392); ISLA gains 15% — the local-interpolation hypothesis is falsified {#sec-nb-seen-unseen}

**Setting.** The nested data-efficiency splits are random case samples, not
geometry hold-outs: the 180 shared validation cases span 118 geometries,
and at the 35-case rung 22 of those geometries also appear in the training
set (at other angles of attack), covering 34 validation cases; at 210 cases,
79 geometries and 116 validation cases are "seen". The 35-case stratum
was already in the data-efficiency chapter's stratification
(@sec-nb-strat35); what this entry adds is the 210-case rung and the reading
in the light of the per-case decorrelation (@sec-nb-hilift-percase), for
which the split is a discriminator without any geometry-distance
computation: if
GeoTransolver at small data interpolates locally in geometry space, its error
on validation cases whose geometry it has trained on should be well below its
error on geometries it has never seen.

**What we saw** (results/hilift_seen_vs_unseen_geometry_2026-09-07.json;
two-seed mean pressure relative L2 per case, then mean over the cases in
each group):

| rung | group | cases (geometries) | ISLA | GeoTransolver | GeoTransolver / ISLA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 35 | geometry seen in training | 34 (22) | 0.123 | 0.390 | 3.2 |
| 35 | geometry unseen | 146 (96) | 0.142 | 0.392 | 2.8 |
| 210 | geometry seen | 116 (79) | 0.066 | 0.158 | 2.4 |
| 210 | geometry unseen | 64 (39) | 0.061 | 0.159 | 2.6 |

**GeoTransolver's error is identical on seen and unseen geometries** (ratio
unseen/seen 1.01 at both rungs). ISLA is 15% better on seen geometries at
35 cases (1.15) and indifferent at 210 (0.93).

**Reading.** Having trained on a geometry at other angles does not help
GeoTransolver at all at 35 or 210 cases, so its small-data failure is not
memorization or local interpolation in geometry space; it is closer to not
having learned the geometry dependence of the pressure field at these data
sizes, with its per-case error set by something other than the geometry
(the single-angle result, where GeoTransolver is 5.0x behind once the angle
of attack carries no information, points the same way). ISLA does exploit
the seen geometries at 35 cases, as a model that has learned a
geometry-to-pressure map should, and no longer needs to by 210. The
nearest-training-geometry Chamfer test proposed above would now test a
falsified premise for GeoTransolver and is withdrawn. Nothing much sets
GeoTransolver's per-case error at small data: it is nearly
case-independent (coefficient of variation 0.15 at 35 cases against ISLA's
0.44, @sec-nb-hilift-percase), rising only with angle of attack, which is
what a model that has learned the mean pattern and the angle dependence but
little of the geometry dependence looks like.

**Same signature at a fixed angle.** On the single-angle split (126
geometries at 12°, 18 held-out geometries) GeoTransolver's per-geometry
error is flat, 0.139–0.209 around a mean of 0.179 (coefficient of variation
0.12), while ISLA's spans 0.026–0.051 (0.18); on the matched mixed-angle
control the coefficients are 0.19 against 0.57
(results/hilift_single_angle_error_spread_2026-09-07.json). With the angle
fixed, GeoTransolver has almost nothing left that varies by case: at 126
cases it is geometry-blind to within seed noise.

## 2026-09-07 — W2-F, first rung: trained on 4 geometries (40 cases), validated on 18 geometries never seen at any angle, ISLA leads GeoTransolver 1.8x (0.250 vs 0.449); the falsifier (ISLA/GT ≥ 0.8) does not fire, the 0.1 band does {#sec-nb-w2f-40-verdict}

**Setting.** The unseen-geometry ladder (@sec-nb-w2f-launch) trains on the
`geometry_super_scarce` split, 40 cases made of 4 geometries at all 10
angles of attack, and validates on the 180 cases of 18 geometries that
appear in no training set at any angle; the same protocol as the
data-efficiency ladder otherwise (10,000 tokens, lr 1e-3, 500 epochs, two
seeds). The preregistered prediction was that ISLA/GeoTransolver would fall
within 0.1 of its value at the same-size data-efficiency rung (35 random
cases spanning 33 geometries: GT/ISLA 2.8, ISLA/GT 0.36); the falsifier was
ISLA/GT ≥ 0.8, which would have said the advantage depends on having seen
the validation geometry at another angle.

**Readout** (results/w2_reduction_2026-09-07b.json, arm
`F_geometry_super_scarce`; surface pressure relative L2, mean over the 180
validation cases):

| model | seed 42 | seed 43 | mean | velocity | wall shear |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA | 0.248 | 0.251 | 0.250 | 0.230 / 0.222 | 0.357 / 0.348 |
| GeoTransolver | 0.407 | 0.492 | 0.449 | 0.411 / 0.436 | 0.575 / 0.636 |
| GeoTransolver / ISLA | | | **1.80** | 1.87 | 1.72 |

**Verdict.** ISLA/GeoTransolver = 0.56: far below the 0.8 falsifier, so
**the advantage does not depend on having seen the validation geometry**;
but 0.20 above the 0.36 of the 35-case random split, outside the
preregistered 0.1 band, so the prediction that the ratio would carry over
at matched case count is not met. The reason is visible in the absolute
numbers. ISLA's error nearly doubles when the 35 random cases (33
geometries) are replaced by 40 cases from 4 geometries (0.138 → 0.250):
its accuracy responds to the *number of distinct geometries* it has seen,
which is what a model that has learned a geometry-to-pressure map should
do. GeoTransolver's error barely moves (0.39 → 0.45), consistent with the
flat, geometry-blind small-data behaviour measured today
(@sec-nb-hilift-percase, @sec-nb-seen-unseen); with only 4 geometries its
two seeds also disagree by 20% (0.407 vs 0.492), against ISLA's 1%. The
two curves therefore approach each other from ISLA's side as geometry
diversity is removed, and the ratio shrinks from 2.8x to 1.8x.

**What is established.** On geometries never seen at any angle, trained on
four geometries, ISLA is 1.8x more accurate than GeoTransolver on pressure,
1.9x on velocity and 1.7x on wall shear, with a tenth of the seed spread.
The 210-case rung of this ladder (`geometry_scarce`, 21 geometries) is
still training and tests whether the ratio returns towards the random-split
value as geometry diversity is restored; its bars are unchanged. The
per-case paired count on the 180 validation cases is reduced separately
(`paired_stats_case.py`, arm `geo40`) and recorded below when it lands.

**Per-case count (landed).** On the 180 validation cases (18 never-seen
geometries × 10 angles), ISLA is more accurate than GeoTransolver on **172
of 180** by two-seed means (158 on both seeds individually; exact sign test
p = 3 × 10⁻⁴¹), median per-case ratio GeoTransolver/ISLA 2.24, 10th–90th
percentiles 1.08–3.34 (results/hilift_paired_stats_case_2026-09-07b.json,
arm `geo40`). The advantage on never-seen geometries is case-by-case, not
an average over a few outliers.

## 2026-09-07 — Verdict: query tokens close the interior gap — ISLA 0.064 vs GeoTransolver-volume 0.062 on interior pressure (ratio 1.03 against a 1.3 bar) at a third of the parameters and no signed-distance input {#sec-nb-qt-verdict}

**Setting.** The query-token arm (@sec-nb-qt-prereg) admits ISLA's interior
queries into the encoder as interacting tokens seeded with the five
invariants of position, SDF-gradient normal and freestream direction, on
ISLA's SE(3)-equivariant slice routing; it gives up query independence and
keeps exact covariance. The 50-epoch pilot passed its gate
(@sec-nb-qt-pilot); the two 500-epoch seeds finished today and were
evaluated on the 48 DrivAerML validation cars at 10,000 surface tokens plus
10,000 interior queries, the same protocol as every interior arm.

**Readout** (results/a35_v0_reduction_2026-09-07.json, V0 section;
relative L2, mean over cars):

| arm | parameters | peak memory | pressure (seed 42 / 43) | velocity (42 / 43) | ν_t (42 / 43) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver-volume (interior points as tokens; coords + SDF + SDF gradient inputs) | 27.6M | 8.8 GB | 0.0622 / 0.0618 → **0.0620** | 0.1335 / 0.1332 → 0.1334 | 0.0934 / 0.0944 → 0.0939 |
| ISLA, query tokens, SDF-gradient normal | 8.9M | 6.0 GB | 0.0636 / 0.0642 → **0.0639** | 0.1545 / 0.1559 → 0.1552 | 0.1562 / 0.1647 → 0.1604 |
| ISLA, passive decode, SDF-gradient normal (for reference) | 9.9M | 4.9 GB | 0.1596 | 0.3075 | 0.3719 |
| ratio ISLA-QT / GeoTransolver | | | **1.03** | 1.16 | 1.71 |

**Verdict.** The preregistered bar was ISLA-QT/GT ≤ 1.3 on interior
pressure with the falsifier at ≥ 2.0. The ratio is **1.03**: the bar is
met with room, and the 2.6x interior deficit of the passive decode is
reduced to 3% on pressure. Seeds agree to 1% for both models. On velocity
ISLA is 16% behind and on eddy viscosity 71% behind; those two fields were
not preregistered bars but are reported as the honest remainder.

**Reading.** Of the three simultaneous differences between GeoTransolver's
volume configuration and ISLA's passive decode
(@sec-nb-interior-resources-correction), letting the queries interact
accounts for essentially all of the pressure gap on its own: with
interaction, ISLA matches GeoTransolver on pressure at 8.9M parameters
against 27.6M, 6.0 GB against 8.8 GB, without the signed-distance value as
an input and without local ball-query features. The remaining velocity and
eddy-viscosity deficits are the natural targets of the second difference,
the signed-distance input, which the QT-SDF arm now training tests
(@sec-nb-qt-sdf-prereg): the eddy viscosity in particular is a
near-wall-distance-dominated quantity, so if any field responds to the SDF
value it should be that one. The cost side: 0.28 s per step against
GeoTransolver-volume's 0.044 s at this size, because ISLA's per-slice
geometry now spans 20,000 tokens; the exact memory rewrite of today
(@sec-nb-geo-recompute) and the compiled region (@sec-nb-geo-compile)
apply to it unchanged.

**What changes in the book.** The interior chapter's standing statement
becomes: one architecture covers the surface and the interior. ISLA with
query tokens is the interior configuration to use where per-query
independence is not required; the passive decode remains the configuration
where it is, at its 2.6x price. The index, the limits chapter and the
claims ledger are updated in the same pass; the query-token configuration
is added to the architecture chapter's cost section with its own numbers.

## 2026-09-07 — Ops: one Transolver lane blocked by a checkpoint truncated at walltime; quarantined and resumed from the previous checkpoint {#sec-nb-truncated-ckpt}

Lane 12 of wave 2 (`t1_hl_transolver_medium_lr3e3_seed42`, Transolver at
lr 3e-3 on the 510-case rung) raised the chain's identical-failure guard:
two consecutive links failed with "Could not determine checkpoint format
... neither a valid zip nor tar archive" on `Transolver.0.171.mdlus`. The
file is 16.0 MB where every other checkpoint of the lane is 24.1 MB: the
link was killed at walltime while writing it, and each restart then tried
to load the truncated latest checkpoint. The epoch-166 checkpoint is a valid
archive. The two epoch-171 files (model and optimizer) were moved to
`runs/<lane>/quarantine_2026-09-07/`, the BLOCKED marker and failure
fingerprint removed, and the lane resubmitted; it resumes from epoch 166,
losing five epochs of the 500, which does not touch the protocol (resume
from the last complete checkpoint is what every link does). The launcher's
chain-ahead design is what makes this possible to catch: the guard stopped
the lane after two identical failures instead of letting it loop until the
walltime budget was spent. A GeoTransolver warning line in another lane
(`mech_hl_gt_single_aoa_12_lr3e3_seed42`) is a torchrun rendezvous notice at
a link restart, not an error; the lane is at epoch 273 and advancing.

## 2026-09-07 — Preregistered: V0-L, interior data efficiency — ISLA query tokens vs GeoTransolver-volume at 54 cars {#sec-nb-v0l-prereg}

**Setting.** With query tokens, ISLA matches GeoTransolver-volume on
interior pressure at full data (435 cars; @sec-nb-qt-verdict). The
program's central result is ISLA's small-data advantage, which on the
*surface* holds on HiLiftAeroML (2.8x at 35 cases) but not on DrivAerML,
where GeoTransolver is 1.2–1.3x more accurate from 27 cars up
(@sec-nb-drivaer-percase: a uniform fit deficit). Whether the interior
follows the surface on DrivAerML is unknown, and it decides how the "one
architecture" statement reads at small data.

**Hypotheses.** *H-a:* ISLA's slice routing over surface and query tokens
learns the volume map from fewer cars than GeoTransolver's interior-point
tokens with local features, so ISLA-QT/GT < 1 at 54 cars. *H-b:* the
DrivAerML fit deficit carries over and the ratio at 54 cars is about the
surface ladder's 1.2–1.3. *H-c:* parity persists.

**Instrument.** `v0/v0_ladder_aga.sbatch`: GeoTransolver-volume and ISLA
query tokens (SDF-gradient normal, similarity gauge), seeds 42 and 43,
trained on `train_n54` of the job-local scaling manifest (54 cars, the
same nested subset the surface ladder used at this rung; disjoint from the
48-car validation set), 500 epochs, lr 1e-3, 10,000 boundary cells plus
10,000 interior points, bf16, no augmentation: the V0 protocol with the
training set replaced. Each arm runs from the code snapshot of its
full-data twin (GeoTransolver from `code`, ISLA-QT from `code_isla`) so the
two points of each curve are strictly comparable. Runs
`v0l_{gt_vol,isla_qt_sdf}_n54_seed{42,43}`; readout interior pressure,
velocity and ν_t relative L2 on the 48 validation cars.

**Bars, in readout units.** H-a supported if ISLA-QT/GT ≤ 0.9 on interior
pressure; H-b supported if ≥ 1.15; between is H-c (parity carries).
Secondary: the 54-to-435 slope of each architecture, −Δlog(error)/Δlog(cars),
reported for both fields. Four lanes, within the 32-node budget after the
query-token lanes released theirs.

**Cost frontier of the query-token configuration** (local RTX 4090, bf16,
10,000 surface + 10,000 interior tokens, interleaved A/B, same weights;
results/isla_qt_cost_2026-09-07.json): stored activations 6.34 GiB at 659 ms
per step (the cluster lanes' 6.0 GB is the same operating point on GB300);
with the per-slice geometry rebuilt in backward (@sec-nb-geo-recompute)
2.78 GiB at 773 ms; with the geometry region also compiled
(@sec-nb-geo-compile) **2.51 GiB at 547 ms**, 0.83x the eager step. Against
GeoTransolver-volume's 8.8 GB at 27.6M parameters, ISLA with query tokens
reaches the same interior pressure at 8.9M parameters and about 2.7 GB;
per step it remains roughly five times slower than GeoTransolver-volume at
this size (0.28 s eager on GB300 against 0.044 s), because its per-slice
geometry spans all 20,000 tokens. That step-time gap is the honest cost
side of the "one architecture" statement.

## 2026-09-07 — Ops: all six DrivAerML-volume lanes hung together for ten minutes on a data read; the distributed timeout fired, the hung links were cancelled and the chains resumed from checkpoint {#sec-nb-drivaer-stall}

At 18:36 PDT every lane reading the DrivAerML volume data (the four
interior data-efficiency lanes and the two signed-distance lanes, on six
different nodes) stopped logging within the same minute, one mid-epoch and
one right after a checkpoint save, while every HiLift lane kept stepping.
Their GPUs read 100% busy: the signature of three ranks spinning in an
all-reduce (a one-element reduction, sequence 7584) while the fourth sat in
a file read that did not return. At 18:46–18:48 the ten-minute distributed
timeout (`PHYSICSNEMO_DIST_TIMEOUT_S=600`) fired on all six, but the jobs did
not exit, because the rank stuck in I/O could not be torn down. A probe of
the DrivAerML tree from the login node at 18:52 read 4 MB of an interior
memmap in under a second, so the stall had cleared; the six jobs were
cancelled and their chain-ahead links started within 15 s, resuming from
the last checkpoints (epoch 70 for the GeoTransolver ladder lanes, 40 for
the ISLA ladder lanes and the signed-distance lanes). Nothing about the
protocol changes: a resumed link replays the same epochs from the same
state. The incident is one more instance of the file system, not the
models, setting the program's cadence (@sec-nb-hilift-io); it cost about
20 minutes of six nodes and 30–40 epochs of recomputation.

**Second stall, 53 minutes later.** At 19:19 the same six lanes stalled
again on a one-element all-reduce and timed out at 19:29, while the login
node read the DrivAerML tree at 50 MB/s and the HiLift lanes kept stepping
(slowly, 3–6 s data stalls). The stalls are transient and I/O-side, so the
right response is a longer distributed timeout, not a shorter one: the two
DrivAerML launchers now set `PHYSICSNEMO_DIST_TIMEOUT_S=3600`, so a stall of
up to an hour lets the lane wait it out instead of dying and replaying up to
ten epochs. The failure fingerprints were cleared so the identical-failure
guard would not block the lanes on a repeat, and the hung links were
cancelled and resumed from checkpoint a second time. The links that started
at 19:30 still carry the old timeout (a chain link's script is copied at
submission); the ones they queue ahead carry the new one. A hypothesis for
the timing, that the HiLift lanes' synchronized chain-link restarts cause
the read-ahead bursts, is not supported by the link ages at either stall
and is not claimed; the cluster was running 81 jobs from many users.

## 2026-09-07 — Verdict V0-L: at 54 cars GeoTransolver-volume leads ISLA query tokens 1.21x on interior pressure (H-b); the DrivAerML fit deficit carries to the interior at small data and closes with data (ISLA's slope 0.33 vs 0.25) {#sec-nb-v0l-verdict}

**Readout** (results/v0l_reduction_2026-09-07.json; interior relative L2,
mean over the 48 validation cars; 54 training cars = `train_n54`, 500
epochs, V0 protocol; the 435-car points are the full-data twins):

| cars | model | pressure (42 / 43 → mean) | velocity | ν_t | ISLA-QT / GT (pressure, velocity, ν_t) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 54 | GeoTransolver-volume (27.6M) | 0.1037 / 0.1044 → **0.104** | 0.202 | 0.190 | |
| 54 | ISLA query tokens (8.9M) | 0.1256 / 0.1270 → **0.126** | 0.254 | 0.329 | **1.21**, 1.26, 1.73 |
| 435 | GeoTransolver-volume | 0.0620 | 0.133 | 0.094 | |
| 435 | ISLA query tokens | 0.0639 | 0.155 | 0.160 | 1.03, 1.16, 1.71 |
| slope 54→435, −Δlog(error)/Δlog(cars) | GeoTransolver | 0.25 | 0.20 | 0.34 | |
| | ISLA query tokens | 0.33 | 0.24 | 0.34 | |

**Verdict.** ISLA-QT/GT = 1.21 on interior pressure at 54 cars: above the
preregistered 1.15, so **H-b holds**: on DrivAerML the small-data fit
deficit that GeoTransolver holds over ISLA on the surface (1.2–1.3x from 27
to 218 cars) carries to the interior, at the same size. Seeds agree to 1%
for both models. ISLA's pressure error falls faster with data (slope 0.33
against 0.25), which is how a 1.21x gap at 54 cars becomes 1.03x at 435;
the velocity slopes differ the same way (0.24 vs 0.20) and the
eddy-viscosity gap is a constant 1.7x at both sizes, unmoved by data.

**Reading.** The interior on DrivAerML behaves like the surface on
DrivAerML, not like the surface on HiLift: GeoTransolver is the more
data-efficient model on this family at every size measured, by a nearly
constant 1.2x, and ISLA reaches it only at full data. The uniform fit
deficit measured on the surface today (@sec-nb-drivaer-percase) is
therefore a property of ISLA on smooth single-body cars, independent of
whether the output is on the wall or in the volume, and independent of
query interaction. The eddy-viscosity gap, flat at 1.7x across an
eightfold change in data, is the clearest candidate for an *input* effect
(the signed distance GeoTransolver receives), which the QT-SDF arm tests.

**What changes in the book.** The interior chapter's standing statement
gains its small-data clause: parity on interior pressure at full data,
GeoTransolver ahead by 1.2x at 54 cars, the same ordering as the surface on
this dataset. The index and the limits chapter carry the same sentence.

**Second rung launched (109 cars).** With the 54-car lanes' nodes free, the
same launcher runs `train_n109` for both architectures and both seeds
(`v0l_{gt_vol,isla_qt_sdf}_n109_seed{42,43}`, lanes 4–7), same protocol
and code snapshots. Preregistered reading, in readout units: the two-point
slopes above predict GeoTransolver at 0.087 and ISLA query tokens at 0.100
on interior pressure at 109 cars (ratio 1.15); the H-b picture is confirmed
if the measured ratio is between 1.10 and 1.25, and the slope story is
falsified if ISLA's 54→109 slope is not steeper than GeoTransolver's.

## 2026-09-08 — W2-A at 210 cases: ISLA's and Transolver's third seeds land inside their spreads; GeoTransolver's lands far below (0.107 vs 0.157–0.160) — the 210-case ratio is 2.2x on three seeds, not 2.5x {#sec-nb-w2a-210-verdict}

**Setting and bar.** The W2 preregistration (@sec-nb-w2-prereg, arm A)
added a third seed (44) at 35 and 210 cases for all three architectures.
Prediction: every seed-44 result lands inside the seed-42/43 spread
widened by 1.5x; falsifier: any architecture's third seed moves its rung
mean by more than 15%. The 35-case readout was recorded earlier
(@sec-nb-w2a-35: all three inside, factors 2.8x and 2.9x). The 210-case
lanes finished tonight after their evaluations on the shared 180 cases
(results/w2_reduction_2026-09-07b.json).

| architecture, 210 cases | seed 42 | seed 43 | seed 44 | two-seed mean | three-seed mean | shift |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA | 0.0622 | 0.0666 | **0.0657** | 0.0644 | 0.0648 | +0.7% |

| Transolver (lr 3e-3) | 0.0892 | 0.0832 | **0.0875** | 0.0862 | 0.0866 | +0.5% |

**Verdict.** ISLA and Transolver: inside their spreads, means unchanged; the
prediction holds. GeoTransolver: the third seed is 1.5x better than either
of the first two, far outside a spread that was only 0.0025 wide; the
prediction fails for GeoTransolver, while the 15% falsifier does not fire
(−10.9%). At 35 cases GeoTransolver's third seed was likewise below its
two-seed range (0.359 against 0.375–0.409). **GeoTransolver's small-data
results on HiLift are seed-fragile in a way ISLA's and Transolver's are
not**: at 210 cases its three seeds span 0.107–0.160 (a factor of 1.5),
ISLA's span 0.062–0.067 (1.07) and Transolver's 0.083–0.089 (1.07). The
per-case decorrelation recorded today (@sec-nb-hilift-percase) had already
shown GeoTransolver's error to be flat across cases; this shows it is also
volatile across initialisations, which is what a model that has not
found the geometry dependence looks like: which basin it lands in matters
more than which case it sees.

**What changes.** The 210-case factor is stated on three seeds: **2.2x**
over GeoTransolver (0.1414/0.0648 = 2.18) and 1.3x over Transolver
(0.0866/0.0648 = 1.34); the 35-case factors stay 2.8x and 2.9x. The
data-efficiency figure and tables now draw every available seed (three at
35 and 210, two at 1,260), and GeoTransolver's 210-case seed range is
written next to its mean wherever the ratio appears. The paired per-case
statistics, which use two-seed means per case, are unchanged in kind and
are refreshed with the third seed where the reducer supports it. The
qualitative result does not move: ISLA leads GeoTransolver 2.2–2.8x on
35–210 cases with a tenth of its seed spread, and the advantage closes to
parity at 1,260.

**Third stall, an hour long.** The six DrivAerML lanes stalled again at
20:39, this time under the 3600 s watchdog, which fired at 21:39 after the
full hour ("ran for 3600093 ms"); the links restarted from checkpoint at
21:48 and stepped normally afterwards. So the stalls are not brief
transients: a read on the DrivAerML tree can block a rank for at least an
hour while the same tree answers a login-node read in under a second and
every HiLiftAeroML lane keeps stepping. Three episodes (18:36, 19:19,
20:39) have hit all six lanes within the same minute each time, on six
different nodes, so the trigger is shared and external, not a per-job
deadlock. The cost per episode is an hour of six nodes plus up to ten
epochs of replay; the failure fingerprint the chain guard extracts does not
match the watchdog's message, so the guard cannot block these lanes, and
they will keep resuming. The signed-distance arm is at epoch 141 of 500
after 3.7 hours of wall time for what should have been 1.4 hours of
training. Nothing about this touches the results or the protocol; it sets
the cadence, and it is another entry for the program owner's file-system
list (@sec-nb-hilift-io-verdict).

**Fourth stall, caught early.** All six DrivAerML lanes went silent again
between 22:08 and 22:16; the watcher now flags a lane whose log has been
quiet for 15 minutes, and the six hung links were cancelled at 22:27–22:29
and resumed from checkpoint within 15 seconds, at a cost of about 20
minutes of six nodes instead of an hour. The episodes are now roughly
hourly (18:36, 19:19, 20:39, 22:10) and always hit every DrivAerML reader
at once. Procedure while it lasts: on the watcher's stall event, cancel the
running links of the silent lanes; the chain-ahead singletons restart
immediately, and the guard cannot block them.

## 2026-09-08 — V0-L second rung (109 cars): ratio 1.20 (predicted 1.15, band 1.10–1.25 met); the two curves are parallel from 54 to 109 and converge only above 109, where GeoTransolver's slope halves {#sec-nb-v0l-109-verdict}

**Readout** (results/v0l_reduction_2026-09-08.json; interior relative L2,
mean over 48 cars, two seeds within 1% for every cell):

| cars | GeoTransolver-volume: pressure / velocity / ν_t | ISLA query tokens: pressure / velocity / ν_t | ratio ISLA-QT / GT |
|---|---|---|---|
| 54 | 0.104 / 0.202 / 0.190 | 0.126 / 0.254 / 0.329 | 1.21 / 1.26 / 1.73 |
| 109 | 0.078 / 0.163 / 0.142 | 0.094 / 0.207 / 0.254 | **1.20** / 1.27 / 1.79 |
| 435 | 0.062 / 0.133 / 0.094 | 0.064 / 0.155 / 0.160 | 1.03 / 1.16 / 1.71 |

Log-log slopes, −Δlog(error)/Δlog(cars), pressure: GeoTransolver 0.41
(54→109) then 0.17 (109→435); ISLA query tokens 0.42 then 0.28. Velocity:
0.31 then 0.14 against 0.30 then 0.21. Eddy viscosity: 0.42 then 0.30
against 0.37 then 0.33.

**Verdict.** The preregistered band held: 1.20 measured against 1.15
predicted from the two-point slopes, inside 1.10–1.25. The slope
prediction as written ("ISLA's 54→109 slope steeper than GeoTransolver's")
is met only nominally (0.42 against 0.41): from 54 to 109 cars the two
curves are parallel, the ratio constant at 1.20–1.21, and the convergence
happens entirely above 109 cars, where GeoTransolver's pressure slope
halves (0.41 → 0.17) while ISLA's falls less (0.42 → 0.28). The
eddy-viscosity ratio is 1.7–1.8 at all three sizes.

**Reading.** On DrivAerML's interior the picture is: a constant 1.2x
GeoTransolver advantage through the small-data regime, and a GeoTransolver
curve that flattens first as data grows, so that ISLA catches up by 435
cars. That is the mirror image of the HiLift surface curves, where ISLA's
curve flattened first and GeoTransolver caught up at 1,260 cases
(@sec-nb-w2-prereg); on both datasets the architecture that is behind at
small data has the steeper large-data slope, which is what one expects
when the leader is nearer the protocol's floor. The interior parity at
full data is therefore not a coincidence of one size: it is where the two
curves cross. Nothing in this rung changes the standing statement; it
adds the middle point and removes the reading that ISLA's small-data
interior error falls faster at every size.

**Setting and bar.** The single-angle split (126 geometries at 12°, 18

0.1749/0.1829 at the frozen learning rate of 1e-3 (@sec-nb-w2d-single-angle),
a 5.0x advantage attributed to geometry generalization. The steel-man
(@sec-nb-w2f-launch) re-ran GeoTransolver at 3e-3, the rate at which it had
sometimes recovered on other splits, with the falsifier that GeoTransolver

## 2026-09-08 — Preregistered: Transolver on the single-angle split — is the fixed-angle geometry failure GeoTransolver's geometry encoder or the shared backbone? {#sec-nb-transolver-single-prereg}

**Setting.** At a fixed angle of attack GeoTransolver is 5.0x behind ISLA on
18 never-seen geometries (@sec-nb-w2d-single-angle), with its error flat
across geometries (@sec-nb-hilift-percase) and unrescued by learning rate
(@sec-nb-w2g-verdict). On the mixed-angle 210-case split, plain Transolver
(the same attention family without GeoTransolver's geometry encoder) is
1.8x more accurate than GeoTransolver and only 1.3x behind ISLA
(@sec-de-result). Whether that holds when the angle carries no information
decides where the fixed-angle failure lives.

**Hypotheses.** *H-encoder:* the failure belongs to GeoTransolver's
geometry-encoder path; Transolver at the single angle lands within 2.0x of
ISLA. *H-backbone:* the slice-attention backbone itself does not learn
geometry from 126 cases; Transolver lands 3.5x or more behind ISLA, like
GeoTransolver. Between is inconclusive.

**Instrument.** Two lanes appended to the wave-2 table (rows 40–41):
`transolver_surface` on `highlift_surface_single_aoa_12` at its better
learning rate 3e-3, seeds 42 and 43, otherwise the frozen protocol; runs
`mech_hl_transolver_single_aoa_12_lr3e3_seed{42,43}`, evaluated on the 18
held-out geometries with the wave-2 evaluation launcher. Readout: mean
pressure relative L2 over the 18 geometries; ratio Transolver/ISLA (ISLA
0.036). Six nodes were free after the interior ladder and the steel-man
finished; this uses two.

## 2026-09-08 — Verdict QT-SDF: with the signed distance as an input, ISLA's query tokens beat GeoTransolver-volume on interior pressure (0.91x) and velocity (0.64x) and trail on eddy viscosity (1.29x), at 8.9M vs 27.6M parameters with matched inputs; the preregistered pressure bar lands in the inconclusive band (0.89) {#sec-nb-qt-sdf-verdict}

**Setting and bars.** The arm (@sec-nb-qt-sdf-prereg) gives ISLA's query
tokens the one input GeoTransolver-volume had and ISLA lacked, the signed
distance to the wall at each query (`n_query_scalars=1`, entered as
[s/gauge, sign(s)·log|s/gauge|]), on top of the SDF-gradient normal both
already used. Everything else is the query-token configuration
(@sec-nb-qt-verdict). Preregistered on interior pressure: supported if
QT-SDF/QT ≤ 0.85, falsified if ≥ 0.95, inconclusive between; secondary,
QT-SDF/GT ≤ 1.1 closes the interior gap at a third of the parameters.
Velocity and eddy viscosity were named as the fields most likely to
respond, without bars.

**Readout** (results/a35_v0_reduction_2026-09-08.json, V0 section; 48
validation cars, two seeds; per-arm resources from the lane logs,
results/v0_interior_resources_2026-09-07.json updated):

| arm | params | peak memory | pressure (42 / 43 → mean) | velocity | ν_t |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver-volume (SDF + SDF gradient inputs, six-radius local features) | 27.6M | 8.8 GB | 0.0622 / 0.0618 → 0.0620 | 0.1334 | 0.0939 |
| ISLA query tokens, SDF gradient only | 8.9M | 6.0 GB | 0.0636 / 0.0642 → 0.0639 | 0.1552 | 0.1604 |
| **ISLA query tokens + SDF value** | 8.9M | 6.0 GB | 0.0569 / 0.0565 → **0.0567** | **0.0853** | **0.1215** |
| QT-SDF / QT | | | 0.89 | 0.55 | 0.76 |
| QT-SDF / GeoTransolver | | | **0.91** | **0.64** | 1.29 |

**Verdict against the bars.** On interior pressure QT-SDF/QT = 0.89:
inside the preregistered inconclusive band, so the primary hypothesis that
the input is worth at least 15% of pressure error is neither supported nor
falsified by its own bar (it is worth 11%). The secondary bar is met with
margin: QT-SDF/GT = 0.91, ISLA is now *ahead* of GeoTransolver-volume on
interior pressure at a third of the parameters, with the two models'
inputs matched (both receive the signed distance and its gradient). The
fields named as most likely to respond respond strongly: velocity error
falls 45% (0.155 → 0.085) and ISLA leads GeoTransolver by 1.56x on it;
eddy viscosity falls 24% (0.160 → 0.122) and the deficit to GeoTransolver
shrinks from 1.71x to 1.29x. Seeds agree to 1% on pressure and velocity
and 7% on ν_t.

**Reading.** Of the three differences between GeoTransolver-volume and
ISLA's passive decode, the first (query interaction) closed the pressure
gap and the second (the signed-distance input) closes most of the rest,
inverting the pressure and velocity orderings; the third (2.8x parameters
and local ball-query features) is what GeoTransolver still has and does not
translate into accuracy here. What remains in GeoTransolver's favour is
eddy viscosity at 1.29x, a near-wall quantity for which its six-radius
local features over the interior cloud are the natural remaining
explanation, and a factor of 3 in parameters that ISLA does not need. The
data-efficiency question for this configuration (54 and 109 cars) is not
measured; the query-token ladder without the SDF value showed a constant
1.2x GeoTransolver lead below full data.

**What changes in the book.** The interior standing statement becomes:
ISLA with query tokens and the signed-distance input is the more accurate
volume surrogate on pressure and velocity at a third of the parameters and
two thirds of the memory, exactly SE(3)-covariant; GeoTransolver-volume
keeps the lead on eddy viscosity; the passive decode remains the
query-independent option at its price. The index, the limits chapter, the
architecture chapter's cost section and the claims ledger are updated in
the same pass.

**Reading.** With inputs matched, the remaining difference between the two
volume models is GeoTransolver's 2.8x parameters and six-radius local
features. Those buy it a 6–11% pressure advantage below 109 cars and a
1.3–1.5x advantage on eddy viscosity; they buy nothing on velocity at any
size and nothing on pressure at 435 cars. The "one architecture" statement
therefore reads, at small data on DrivAerML's interior: ISLA ahead on
velocity, within 6–11% on pressure, behind on eddy viscosity; at full data
ahead on two of three fields. The eddy-viscosity gap, flat across an
eightfold change in data with matched inputs, is now the cleanest target
for a local-feature channel in ISLA's query tokens, which would be the
third and last of GeoTransolver-volume's differences to test.

## 2026-09-08 — Preregistered: local surface-patch features on the query tokens (QT-SDF-LF) — the third of GeoTransolver-volume's three differences, aimed at the eddy-viscosity gap {#sec-nb-qt-lf-prereg}

**Setting.** With query interaction and the signed-distance input, ISLA is
ahead of GeoTransolver-volume on interior pressure and velocity and behind
by 1.29x on eddy viscosity at full data, 1.3–1.5x at 54 and 109 cars, a
gap flat in data (@sec-nb-qt-sdf-verdict, @sec-nb-qtsdf-ladder-verdict).
The one input class GeoTransolver still has and ISLA lacks is local
features: ball-query aggregates at six radii over neighbouring interior
points. Eddy viscosity is a near-wall, boundary-layer quantity, the field
most plausibly served by multi-scale local geometry.

**Change to the model** (commit e937591ed). `query_local_features=True`
adds to each query token the measure-weighted Gaussian patch integrals of
the *surface* sample around the query at radii (0.05, 0.15, 0.5) gauge
units, the same seven invariants per radius the passive decoder's local
channel uses (mean surface normal projected on the query normal and drive
and its norm; offset to the patch centroid projected and normed; log of
the patch measure), with the measure normalized to a fraction of the total
surface so that the channel is exactly scale-covariant under the
similarity gauge (the raw-area version was not; the contracts test caught
it). It enters additively through its own embedding, like the
signed-distance channel; every covariance contract is tested to 1e-10.
Unlike GeoTransolver's local features, it aggregates the surface, not the
interior neighbours: it is the ISLA-native reading of "local geometry at
the query".

**Hypothesis and bars.** *H-local:* multi-scale surface geometry at the
query is what the eddy-viscosity field needs beyond the wall distance.
Runs `v0_isla_qtsdflf_seed{42,43}` (`code_isla3`, the QT-SDF configuration
plus the channel), 435 cars, V0 protocol; readout on the 48 validation
cars. *Supported* if ν_t QT-SDF-LF / GT ≤ 1.10 (from 1.29) with pressure and
velocity within 5% of the QT-SDF values; *falsified* if ν_t ratio ≥ 1.25;
between, inconclusive. A pressure or velocity regression of more than 5%
is reported as a cost regardless of the ν_t outcome. Two nodes.

Lane 12 (`t1_hl_transolver_medium_lr3e3_seed42`) went BLOCKED again at
09:57 with yesterday's message about the epoch-171 checkpoint. The
checkpoint itself was fine: the resumed link had re-reached epoch 171 and

happened is that two consecutive links (06:23–07:56 and 07:56–09:57) died

class as the DrivAerML lanes, and the guard's fingerprint step, which greps

## 2026-09-08 — Verdict QT-SDF-LF: falsified — local surface-patch features on the query tokens leave pressure and velocity unchanged (+1%, +0.2%) and make eddy viscosity slightly worse (0.127 vs 0.122; 1.36x GeoTransolver against a 1.25 falsifier) {#sec-nb-qt-lf-verdict}

**Readout** (results/a35_v0_reduction_2026-09-08b.json, V0 section; 48
validation cars, two seeds within 1% on pressure and velocity and 7% on ν_t):

| arm | params | pressure | velocity | ν_t | ν_t / GeoTransolver |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver-volume | 27.6M | 0.0620 | 0.1334 | 0.0939 | 1.00 |
| ISLA query tokens + SDF value | 8.9M | 0.0567 | 0.0853 | 0.1215 | 1.29 |
| ISLA query tokens + SDF value + surface-patch local features (three radii) | 8.95M | 0.0574 (0.0578 / 0.0570) | 0.0855 (0.0858 / 0.0851) | **0.1274** (0.1318 / 0.1230) | **1.36** |

**Verdict.** The preregistered bars (@sec-nb-qt-lf-prereg) were: supported
if ν_t/GT ≤ 1.10, falsified if ≥ 1.25. At 1.36 the hypothesis is
**falsified**: multi-scale surface geometry at the query, as
measure-weighted patch integrals at 0.05, 0.15 and 0.5 gauge units, adds
nothing to eddy viscosity and costs 5% on it (within the two seeds' 7%
spread, so at best neutral), while leaving pressure (+1%) and velocity
(+0.2%) where they were. The channel is kept in the code as an option and
is not part of any recommended configuration.

**Reading.** The three differences between GeoTransolver-volume and ISLA's
passive decode are now each measured on their own: query interaction closes
the pressure gap (1.03x); the signed-distance input puts ISLA ahead on
pressure and velocity (0.91x, 0.64x); and the one remaining deficit, eddy
viscosity at 1.29x, does not respond to ISLA-native local surface features.
What GeoTransolver's local-feature encoder aggregates is not the surface
but the *neighbouring interior points* (their coordinates, signed distances
and gradients at six radii), i.e. a local field of wall-distance samples,
and it has 2.8x the parameters. Either could carry the last 1.29x; the
surface-geometry reading of "local features" cannot. The next
discriminator, if the eddy-viscosity gap is worth closing, is a
query-to-query local channel (ball-query aggregates of the query tokens'
own invariants, the interior analogue of GeoTransolver's encoder) against a
matched-parameter control (ISLA at hidden 256); neither is launched here.
With inputs matched and two of three fields ahead at a third of the
parameters, the interior statement stands as written after the
signed-distance arm.

## 2026-09-08 — Preregistered: matched-width control — ISLA query tokens + signed distance at hidden 256 (does the eddy-viscosity gap come from parameters?) {#sec-nb-qt-h256-prereg}

**Setting.** Of GeoTransolver-volume's three differences to ISLA's passive
decode, interaction and the signed-distance input are measured and the
surface-patch reading of local features is falsified
(@sec-nb-qt-lf-verdict). The remaining 1.29x eddy-viscosity deficit has two
candidate carriers left: GeoTransolver's local aggregation over
neighbouring interior points, and its 2.8x parameters (hidden width 256
against ISLA's 192, plus the local-feature encoder). This arm tests the
second: the QT-SDF configuration with hidden width 256 (every other
hyperparameter unchanged; about 15.7M parameters, still 0.57x
GeoTransolver-volume's 27.6M).

**Bars.** Runs `v0_isla_qtsdf_h256_seed{42,43}` (`code_isla3` with
`query_local_features` off, so the model is the QT-SDF one; 435 cars, V0
protocol). *Parameters carry it* if ν_t QT-SDF-h256 / GT ≤ 1.10 (from 1.29);
*falsified* if ≥ 1.25; between, inconclusive. Pressure and velocity are
reported alongside; a change of more than 5% either way is reported as an
