### Geometry-level paired statistics {#sec-nb-audit-geometry-stats}

The audit's point was that a HiLiftAeroML validation set is not 180
independent draws: the random-split validation set holds 180 cases on 118
geometries (69 geometries at one angle, 40 at two, 9 at three to five), and
the unseen-geometry and fixed-angle sets hold 18 geometries (ten angles each,
or one). The per-case rows behind every paired statistic, with geometry and
angle identifiers and per-seed errors, are now published in
results/hilift_paired_stats_geometry_2026-09-08.json (reducer alongside), and
the statistics are recomputed with the geometry as the unit: case errors
averaged within geometry, a two-sided sign test over geometries, the median
and 10–90% range of the geometry-level baseline÷ISLA ratio, and a two-stage
bootstrap (geometries, then angles within geometry; 10,000 resamples) of the
ratio of means, next to the case-level bootstrap.

| Comparison | Case wins | Geometry wins (p) | Geometry-level ratio, median [10–90%] | Ratio of means, 95% (geometry bootstrap) | Same, case bootstrap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 35 cases, GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA (three seeds) | 180/180 | 118/118 (6×10⁻³⁶) | 2.92 [1.87, 4.33] | [2.59, 2.95] | [2.61, 2.92] |
| 35 cases, Transolver ÷ ISLA | 180/180 | 118/118 (6×10⁻³⁶) | 3.16 [1.96, 4.54] | [2.74, 3.13] | [2.76, 3.11] |
| 210 cases, GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | 176/180 | 116/118 (4×10⁻³²) | 2.51 [1.45, 3.20] | [2.01, 2.36] | [2.04, 2.33] |
| 210 cases, Transolver ÷ ISLA | 164/180 | 109/118 (6×10⁻²³) | 1.48 [1.06, 1.85] | [1.27, 1.41] | [1.28, 1.40] |
| 1,260 cases, GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | 130/180 | 86/118 (7×10⁻⁷) | 1.06 [0.93, 1.17] | [0.97, 1.06] | [0.98, 1.06] |
| 4 training geometries (40 cases), GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | 172/180 | 18/18 (7.6×10⁻⁶) | 2.16 [1.36, 3.12] | [1.56, 2.16] | [1.70, 1.92] |
| 21 training geometries (210 cases), GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | 172/180 | 18/18 (7.6×10⁻⁶) | 1.41 [1.15, 1.93] | [1.28, 1.54] | [1.35, 1.46] |
| Fixed angle, 126 geometries, GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | 18/18 | 18/18 (7.6×10⁻⁶) | 4.90 [4.32, 5.93] | [4.70, 5.31] | [4.70, 5.33] |
| Fixed angle, Transolver ÷ ISLA | 18/18 | 18/18 (7.6×10⁻⁶) | 2.57 [2.13, 3.12] | [2.37, 2.76] | [2.38, 2.77] |

: Paired statistics with the geometry as the independent unit. Case wins are
by seed-mean error; the 35- and 210-case rows use three seeds (the two-seed
rows reproduce the earlier case-level artifact exactly). Data:
results/hilift_paired_stats_geometry_2026-09-08.json. {#tbl-nb-geostat}

**Every small-data advantage survives the change of unit.** ISLA is more
accurate on all 118 validation geometries at 35 cases and on all 18 at both
unseen-geometry rungs and at the fixed angle; the smallest two-sided p at
n = 18 is 7.6 × 10⁻⁶, which is the honest significance for those rungs (the
case-level 3 × 10⁻⁴¹ over-counted). Clustering by geometry widens the
intervals where it should: at 4 training geometries the ratio-of-means
interval grows from [1.70, 1.92] to [1.56, 2.16], and at 21 from [1.35, 1.46]
to [1.28, 1.54]; on the random splits the two bootstraps nearly coincide
because most geometries appear at one angle. At 1,260 cases the interval
includes 1.0 under every scheme, so parity stands, and the 86-of-118
geometry count there is a small systematic edge for ISLA, not a tie.
Chapters 5 and 12 now quote the geometry-level counts and intervals for the
unseen-geometry and fixed-angle rungs; the tech-tree node GEOSTAT is DONE.
What no resampling of one training subset can supply remains: the variance
over which 35 cases, or which four geometries, are drawn (@sec-nb-audit-2026-09-08).

### Preregistered: MOM2, is a second-moment channel worth having? {#sec-nb-mom2-prereg}

*Hypothesis.* ISLA's slice anchors are first moments, so two boundaries
whose transverse first moments about the drive agree within every slice
are indistinguishable to it whatever their second moments; the item-4
counterexample is one instance. A per-slice second-moment channel, the
measure-weighted second-moment tensor of the points routed to a slice about
its anchor, contracted equivariantly at each point as r̂ᵀ C_s r̂ (and its
trace, both invariants) and appended to the eight relational invariants,
restores the distinction at negligible cost; the existing local-distance
channel restores it too, by a different route. Which of the two does so
more reliably, and whether either is worth carrying into the reference
configuration, is what this benchmark decides. It does *not* test whether
the limitation affects any benchmark: that is a separate question and is
not established.

*Instrument (eval-only, no training).* A random collision family: for each
of N = 200 draws, two arrangements of five equal spherical component
samples (8 points each, radius 0.15 at distance 2 from the axis) about the
axial drive, one at azimuths {0, 120, 240, φ, φ+180}° and one at
{0, 120, 240, φ', φ'+180}° with φ, φ' drawn uniformly on (0, 120)° and
|φ − φ'| ≥ 10°, so every pair has zero transverse first moment, differs in
its pairwise-distance profile, and admits no rotation preserving geometry
and drive; plus 200 congruent control pairs (the same arrangement rotated
about the drive), which every arm must call identical. Three arms, each an
untrained ISLA (hidden 64, 4 layers, 32 slices) at three seeds, in float64:
the base model (default gauge and, separately, the similarity gauge); the
base model with `use_local_features=True` at radii (0.2, 0.4); the base
model with the second-moment channel. Readout per pair: the maximum
absolute difference of the scalar output on the common component (the
component at azimuth 0), and, over the 200 pairs, the accuracy of a linear
probe (logistic regression, 5-fold cross-validated) that classifies each
common-component output vector as coming from the φ- or the φ'-family; the
probe is trained on the outputs only, so chance is 50%.

*Bars, in readout units.* **Supported** if the second-moment arm's probe
accuracy is ≥ 95% on every seed while the base arm's is within 45–55% and
its common-component differences stay below 1e-12 (it must remain blind, or
the family was mis-drawn), with the local-distance arm's accuracy reported
alongside for the comparison. **Falsified** if neither the second-moment
nor the local-distance arm exceeds 60%, in which case the collision is not
removable by either cheap channel and the limitation stays documented and
unaddressed. Between 60% and 95% for the second-moment arm: inconclusive,
reported with the accuracy. Control pairs: every arm must give
common-component differences below 1e-12 on all 200 congruent pairs, or the
arm is disqualified as not equivariant. Secondary readout, not a bar: the
per-pair separation of each channel as a function of |φ − φ'|, to see
whether either channel's resolution degrades for nearly congruent
arrangements.

*What each outcome changes.* Supported: the second-moment channel becomes a
candidate ingredient for the successor design (MT3), and the next node is a
trained control on DrivAerML at 435 cars (falsifier: more than 3% in-family
pressure cost) before any claim that it helps a benchmark; the limitation
is then "removable at known cost", still not "a cause of the DrivAerML
gap". Falsified: the collision family is recorded as a known blind spot of
first-moment anchor architectures, and the remedy, if one is ever needed,
is a richer anchor (a geometric-algebra token or an explicit
orientation frame per slice), which is a design-brief item and not a
patch. Either way, M3's row stays qualified as "not established as the cause
on cars".

**Scheduling decision.** MOM2 is READY (depends on M3, done); it is
eval-only and runs on a CPU in minutes. UDRV is READY and is the first
training node to launch, ahead of any further architecture change, because
it is the cheapest test that could move part of the headline from
architecture to conditioning. QMASS and GEOSTAT are RUNNING; FORCE-REF and
MEM-INST are READY and eval-only; PASSIVE2 and ABUPT wait on QMASS and UDRV.

### Preregistered: UDRV, the unit-drive baseline control {#sec-nb-udrv-prereg}

*Setting.* Every surface comparison in this book feeds ISLA the unit
freestream direction while GeoTransolver and plain Transolver receive the
physical freestream velocity: 2679.5 in/s on HiLiftAeroML, 38.9 m/s on
DrivAerML. The dataset pipelines nondimensionalize fields and coordinates but
not this global input. The independent audit (@sec-nb-audit-2026-09-08)
showed, and the coordinator reproduced on the production projector with
fixed random weights, that GeoTransolver's global-context projector spreads
each head over about 200 of 256 slices at unit drive magnitude, collapses to
1.0–3.8 slices at 38.9 and to one slice at 2679.5, with the largest context
entry rising from 0.66 to 22.7 to 1530
(results/geotransolver_drive_conditioning_2026-09-08.json). The same frozen
configurations were used by every baseline lane on the cluster.

*Question.* Does the baselines' physical-scale drive input carry a material
part of their small-data deficit on HiLiftAeroML? At 35 mixed-angle cases the
drive direction varies and is informative, so a unit direction is the same
information at a benign scale. At the fixed angle (126 geometries at 12°) the
drive is constant across cases, so the change is purely the scale of a
constant input and the result measures conditioning alone. Prior: DrivAerML's
38.9 m/s also collapses the projector and GeoTransolver still leads ISLA there
from 27 cars up, so collapse is not fatal at that magnitude; the HiLift
magnitude is 69 times larger. A partial effect is the most likely outcome.

*Instrument.* Eight lanes under the frozen ladder protocol (10,000 sampled
points, 500 epochs, bf16, no augmentation, final checkpoint, the lane's own
validation split), launcher `highlift/hl_udrv_aga.sbatch` with lane table
`highlift/udrv_lanes.tsv`; the only change from the reference baseline lanes
is the hydra override of the drive input (GeoTransolver
`forward_kwargs.global_embedding=global_data.U_inf_dir`; Transolver
`forward_kwargs.fx.source=global_data.U_inf_dir`): GeoTransolver and
Transolver at 35 cases (lr 1e-3 and 3e-3, each baseline's declared rate at
that rung) and at the fixed angle, seeds 42 and 43. Readout: two-seed mean
over validation cases of the surface-pressure relative L2. References under
the same protocol with the physical drive: GeoTransolver 0.381 at 35 cases
(seeds 0.374, 0.409, 0.359) and 0.179 at the fixed angle (0.175, 0.183);
Transolver 0.404 (0.406, 0.398, 0.409) and 0.091 (0.087, 0.096); ISLA 0.138
and 0.036.

*Bars, in readout units.* With g = ln(baseline/ISLA) the reference log gap
(1.02 and 1.07 at 35 cases; 1.61 and 0.93 at the fixed angle):
**supported** (the drive scale carries a material part of the deficit) if the
unit-drive mean closes at least one third of the log gap: GeoTransolver 35
cases ≤ 0.27 (≤ 1.96x ISLA), Transolver 35 cases ≤ 0.29, GeoTransolver fixed
angle ≤ 0.105 (≤ 2.9x), Transolver fixed angle ≤ 0.067; **falsified** (null)
if the unit-drive mean lies within the reference seed band widened by one band
width: GeoTransolver 35 cases ≥ 0.34, Transolver ≥ 0.38, GeoTransolver fixed
angle ≥ 0.165, Transolver fixed angle ≥ 0.082; between, partial, reported
with the fraction of the log gap closed. Each arm is graded separately.

*What each outcome changes.* If GeoTransolver at 35 cases is supported, the
headline 2.8x contains a baseline input-scaling artifact: the verdict
sentence, the data-multiplier reading and every 2.8x statement are rewritten
with the unit-drive baseline as the reference, and the fair-comparison
protocol gains a rule that every model receives the drive at unit scale. If
falsified, the input asymmetry is recorded as excluded and the
fair-comparison chapter gains the control. Not tested: a separately
normalized speed channel (speed does not vary within either dataset),
input normalization inside GeoTransolver's projector (a change to the
baseline), and the DrivAerML surface gap (a follow-up only if the HiLift
control is supported). The preregistration file, written before launch, is
results/udrv_unit_drive_preregistration_2026-09-08.md.

## 2026-09-08 — QMASS verdict: the interior advantage holds only at or above the training query count; every ISLA interior arm saw about 365 surface cells {#sec-nb-qmass-verdict}

*Setting.* ISLA's promoted interior configuration (@sec-interior) admits the
interior query points as interacting tokens and gives each a routing weight
tied to the geometric mean of the surface tokens' weights, so a prediction at
one point depends on which other points are requested with it. The
independent audit (@sec-nb-audit-2026-09-08) showed on small random models
that a pure re-representation of the source measure moves the output by
4–9%; the open question was the size of the dependence on the trained
checkpoint, against the model's 0.005 absolute pressure advantage over
GeoTransolver-volume.

*Instrument.* The trained query-token + signed-distance checkpoint (seed 42,
epoch 500, code snapshot `code_isla2`) and, as control, the passive
SDF-gradient checkpoint (seed 42), run through the recipe's own inference
path on the first four validation cars the loader yields. One 40,000-point
interior sample per car; the first 1,000 points are fixed sentinels,
predicted alone, with 1,000 companions, with 9,000 (the training request of
10,000) and with 39,000, in bf16 (the recipe's inference precision) and in
fp32. Readouts: relative L2 change of the sentinel predictions against the
training-count request, and their error against the truth.

*Result.* Pressure error at the sentinels 0.110 alone, 0.077 at 2,000
queries, 0.062 at 10,000, 0.056 at 40,000 (bf16; fp32 0.114 / 0.080 /
0.055 / 0.054); relative change against the training count 0.100 / 0.051 /
0 / 0.029 for pressure, 0.348 / 0.181 / 0 / 0.048 for eddy viscosity, 0.142
/ 0.090 / 0 / 0.045 for velocity. The passive control changes by exactly
0.000 in fp32 for every request size and by under 1% in bf16 (autocast
numerics), with identical error to three decimals. A two-half chunking of the
sentinels with the same companions moves the prediction 0.4–0.7% in fp32
(2–4% in bf16). **Verdict: the dependence exceeds the 0.005 margin by 3x at
2,000 queries and 10x at 1,000, and is bounded (3%) at 40,000; the interior
advantage is a property of requests at or above the training count, not of
the model at arbitrary request sizes.** Chapter 8 gains
@sec-interior-companion and the verdict table qualifies the interior row.
The measure-consistent query-mass convention (`query_mass="source_total"`,
committed with tests) removes the source-refinement dependence but the
trained checkpoints do not use it; whether training with it, or over a range
of query counts, removes the count dependence is open. Artifact:
results/isla_qt_companion_dependence_2026-09-08.json.

*Side finding, verified in the reader code and the cluster's dataset
configuration.* To reproduce the training request the probe had to rebuild
the surface sample as the recipe delivers it, and the recipe does not deliver
10,000 surface cells. The volume dataset sets both `subsample_n_points` and
`subsample_n_cells` to the sampling resolution, and `DomainMeshReader`
applies both to every boundary, cells first: 10,000 cells (about 30,000
vertices) are cut to 10,000 points, and the point cut keeps only the cells
whose three vertices all survive, 10,000 × (1/3)³ ≈ 370. On four validation
cars 341–395 vehicle cells remained. The ISLA volume configuration consumes
`boundaries.vehicle.cell_centroids/cell_normals/cell_areas`, so **every ISLA
interior arm in the book (passive, latent tokens, query tokens, query tokens
+ SDF, the 54/109-car ladders, the h256 width control) was trained and
evaluated with about 365 surface tokens plus 10,000 queries**; GeoTransolver's
volume configuration reads no boundary and is unaffected. Consequences
recorded: chapter 8's input description is corrected everywhere; the
query-token cost numbers from training logs describe about 10,400 tokens,
not 20,000 (the synthetic 10,000 + 10,000 cost measurement stands as what it
is); and the scientific reading sharpens, since the query-token + SDF model
beat GeoTransolver-volume on pressure and velocity with almost no surface
information, which credits the interaction and the signed distance rather
than the surface sample. A probe with the boundary pinned at 10,000 cells is
out of the checkpoint's training distribution (pressure 0.079 at the training
request) and is recorded as a labelled secondary in the artifact, not as a
result. The reader gains a `boundary_subsample` option (`cells` applies only
the cell subsample to boundaries) and the repository's volume dataset sets
it; no interior number in the book was produced with it.

### Preregistered: V0-SURF10K, ISLA query tokens + SDF with the intended 10,000 surface cells {#sec-nb-v0surf-prereg}

*Question.* Does giving the interacting configuration the surface sample the
chapter intended change any interior number? Two seeds (42, 43), 435
training cars, the frozen interior protocol (500 epochs, lr 1e-3, bf16, no
augmentation, 10,000 interior queries), the query-token + SDF model of
@sec-interior-query-tokens unchanged, and the dataset variant with
`boundary_subsample: cells` so that 10,000 vehicle cells reach the model.
Readout: the 48-car relative L2 for pressure, velocity and eddy viscosity,
two-seed mean, against the 365-token arm (0.0567 / 0.0853 / 0.1215; seed
spread under 1%) and GeoTransolver-volume (0.0620 / 0.1334 / 0.0939).

*Bars.* **Supported** (surface information matters for the interior) if
pressure ≤ 0.054 or eddy viscosity ≤ 0.115, a 5% improvement, five times
the 365-token arm's seed spread. **Null** if all three fields lie within 3%
of the 365-token arm. Between: partial, reported per field. Cost is
reported alongside (the per-slice geometry now spans 20,000 tokens, so the
step time and memory of the query-token arm rise; the recompute and compiled
paths of @sec-mt2-cost are the mitigation). Either outcome corrects the
chapter's input description; a supported outcome also reopens the passive
decoder question with the full surface (PASSIVE2), because the passive
arm's 2.6x deficit was measured with the same 365 tokens.

## 2026-09-08 — Verdict: a width increase to hidden 256 does not close the interior eddy-viscosity gap (1.26x GeoTransolver-volume, at the 1.25 falsifier); pressure and velocity improve 2–4% {#sec-nb-qt-h256-verdict}

**Setting.** ISLA's query-token configuration with the signed distance
(QT-SDF; hidden width 192, 8.9M parameters) leads GeoTransolver's volume
configuration (27.6M parameters, effective block width 448 with its six
32-channel local features) on DrivAerML interior pressure and velocity and
trails it 1.29x on eddy viscosity ν_t (@sec-nb-qt-sdf-verdict). Two
candidate carriers of that gap remained after the surface-patch local
features were falsified (@sec-nb-qt-lf-verdict): GeoTransolver's local
aggregation over neighbouring interior points, and its parameters. The
preregistered width control (@sec-nb-qt-h256-prereg) tests the second by
running QT-SDF at hidden width 256 (about 15.7M parameters), everything else
unchanged; bars ν_t ≤ 1.10x GeoTransolver-volume supported, ≥ 1.25x
falsified.

**Readout** (runs `v0_isla_qtsdf_h256_seed{42,43}`, 435 cars, 500 epochs,
48 validation cars; results/a35_v0_reduction_2026-09-08c.json):

| arm | pressure (42 / 43 → mean) | velocity | eddy viscosity | ν_t vs GT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver-volume | 0.0622 / 0.0618 → 0.0620 | 0.1334 | 0.0939 | 1.0 |
| QT-SDF, width 192 | 0.0569 / 0.0565 → 0.0567 | 0.0853 | 0.1215 | 1.29x |
| QT-SDF, width 256 | 0.0549 / 0.0545 → **0.0547** | **0.0835** | **0.1179** | **1.26x** |

**Verdict: falsified, marginally.** The eddy-viscosity ratio moves from
1.29x to 1.26x, at the preregistered 1.25 falsifier; pressure and velocity
improve by 3.5% and 2.1%, below the 5% at which the preregistration would
have reported a width effect in its own right. Widening ISLA by a third
buys 2–4% on every field uniformly and does nothing specific to ν_t. Two
caveats, both stated before the result. First, this is a width *increase*,
not a matched width: the control is still narrower (256 against an
effective 448) and smaller (15.7M against 27.6M) than GeoTransolver-volume,
so the null excludes the step from 192 to 256 and does not exclude capacity
as such. Second, like every ISLA interior arm, this one was trained with
about 365 vehicle surface cells rather than the intended 10,000
(@sec-nb-audit-2026-09-08); the comparison between the two widths is
unaffected, since both saw the same inputs.

**What it changes.** The remaining candidate for the ν_t gap is
GeoTransolver-volume's query-to-query local aggregation, a mechanism
ISLA does not have; the interior recommendation of @sec-limits becomes
unconditional only if that ingredient, transplanted at the reference
width, closes the gap. The 10,000-surface-cell rerun (V0-SURF10K,
@sec-nb-v0surf-prereg) takes precedence over a further width ladder, since
it tests whether the surface information ISLA was designed around was
ever in play on this task.

## 2026-09-08 — Launched: V0-SURF10K (query tokens + SDF with 10,000 vehicle cells), and the width control closed {#sec-nb-v0surf-launch}

**Scheduling decision.** The width control (QT-SDF-h256) is DONE and
falsified (@sec-nb-qt-h256-verdict), so the eddy-viscosity thread's next
node would be query-to-query aggregation; it is deferred behind V0-SURF10K
(@sec-nb-v0surf-prereg), which tests whether the surface sample the interior
chapter was designed around changes any interior number at all. Two chains
`v0_isla_qtsdf_surf10k_seed{42,43}` (jobs 684511/684512, launcher
v0/v0_surf10k_aga.sbatch) run from a fresh code snapshot `code_isla4`
(966966f40, the merged audit-response branch, which adds the reader's
`boundary_subsample` option) with a dataset variant
`drivaer_ml_volume_mt10k` that differs from the frozen volume dataset only
in `boundary_subsample: cells`; every model flag equals the QT-SDF arm's.
Evaluation via v0/v0_surf10k_eval_aga.sbatch; reduction arm
`isla_qtsdf_surf10k`. Tech-tree changes: QT-SDF-h256 RUNNING → DONE
(falsified); V0-SURF10K READY → RUNNING.

## 2026-09-08 — Verdict: MOM2 supported — a per-slice second-moment channel (and, separately, the local-distance channel) recovers the arrangement that first-moment anchors lose; the preregistered probe was ill-posed and is replaced {#sec-nb-mom2-verdict}

**Setting.** ISLA routes points to slices whose anchors are measure-weighted
first moments (mean position, mean normal). The audit of 2026-09-08
(@sec-nb-audit-2026-09-08, item 3) showed two non-congruent arrangements of
five spherical components about an axial drive, each with zero transverse
first moment, on which ISLA's outputs coincide to roundoff; the earlier
completeness audit had wrongly argued that such collisions need a rotational
symmetry. MOM2 (@sec-nb-mom2-prereg) asks whether a cheap invariant channel
removes the blind spot: the per-slice second-moment tensor about the anchor,
C_s = E_a[r rᵀ] − z_s z_sᵀ under the point-to-slice weights, read at each
point as r̂ᵀ C_s r̂ and tr C_s and appended to the eight relational
invariants (`second_moment_features=True`, commit cf0572453; exact SE(3)
covariance, drive degree one, measure-scale invariance and, under the
gauge, geometric-scale equivariance are contract-tested, 53 tests pass).

**Instrument.** 200 random collision pairs (free azimuths φ, φ′ ~ U(0, 120)°,
|φ − φ′| ≥ 10°) and 200 congruent control pairs; four arms of untrained
ISLA (hidden 64, 4 layers, 32 slices, float64, three seeds): base, base with
the similarity gauge, base with local features at radii (0.2, 0.4), base with
the second-moment channel. Readouts: the common-component output difference
per pair; and linear probes on the common component's output vector.

**Amendment, stated before the numbers.** The preregistered probe, "classify
the output as φ-family or φ′-family", is ill-posed: φ and φ′ are exchangeable
draws, so the label is arbitrary and no arm can beat chance. The first run
showed exactly that (0.46–0.50 for all four arms, including the two whose
outputs differ by 10⁻³–10⁻¹). The probe is kept in the artifact for the
record and two well-posed readouts of the same question were substituted: the
5-fold cross-validated R² of a ridge regression of φ on the output vector, and
the cross-validated accuracy of a logistic probe for φ ≥ 60° (chance 50%). The
preregistered bars (≥ 95% supported, ≤ 60% falsified, base within 45–55%) are
applied to the second readout.

**Readout** (results/mom2_second_moment_benchmark_2026-09-08.json; three seeds each):

| arm | common-component max diff (median over pairs) | φ ridge R² | φ ≥ 60° probe | congruent controls (max) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 1.4–1.9 × 10⁻¹⁵ | −0.001 – 0.033 | 0.540 | 2 × 10⁻¹⁵ |
| base, similarity gauge | 2–7 × 10⁻¹⁵ | −0.003 – 0.012 | 0.540 | 2 × 10⁻¹⁴ |
| local features (0.2, 0.4) | 0.05–0.12 | **1.000** | **0.992–0.997** | 3 × 10⁻¹⁵ |
| second-moment channel | 0.003–0.004 | **0.996–0.998** | **0.992–0.995** | 1 × 10⁻¹⁴ |

**Verdict: supported.** The base model is blind to the arrangement on every
seed (differences at roundoff; probes at chance, 0.54 within the 45–55 band),
so the family is drawn as intended, and both cheap channels make the free
azimuth linearly readable from the common component to within a few
degrees (R² ≥ 0.996) while remaining exactly equivariant on all 200
congruent controls. The second-moment channel's separations are about
twenty times smaller than the local channel's at these radii; both are far
above roundoff and both decode to the same accuracy. The collision is
therefore "removable at known cost", by either route; it remains *not
established* as a cause of the DrivAerML or HiLift gaps.

**What's next.** Per the preregistration, the second-moment channel is now a
candidate ingredient for the successor design, and the deciding experiment
is a trained control on DrivAerML surface pressure at 435 cars (two seeds,
frozen protocol, `second_moment_features=True` against the reference
configuration; falsifier: more than 3% in-family pressure cost; anything
better than the reference is reported but is not the bar). It is queued
behind V0-SURF10K and the unit-drive control, which bear on the headline.

## 2026-09-08 — Preregistered and launched: MOM2-T, the second-moment channel trained on DrivAerML surface pressure at 435 cars (is the channel free?) {#sec-nb-mom2t-prereg}

**Setting.** MOM2 (@sec-nb-mom2-verdict) showed that the per-slice
second-moment channel removes the first-moment collision at roundoff cost in
an untrained model. Whether it costs accuracy where ISLA is trained is the
question the preregistration named as the next node. The channel adds two
invariants to the eight relational ones in every slice block (the routing
logit and the pooled-geometry projection gain two input columns each; about
2 × 12 × (1 + 96) extra weights at width 192, under 3k parameters) and one
(B, S, 3, 3) tensor per block; nothing else changes.

**Instrument.** Two chains `mom2_mt2_lr1e3_seed{42,43}` (jobs 684590/684591,
launcher mom2t_aga.sbatch cloned from instwave_aga.sbatch lanes 4–5 with
`+model.second_moment_features=true`, code snapshot `code_isla5` at
52eb29ec5, which includes cf0572453; a first submission from `code_isla4`, taken before that commit, failed at construction and was resubmitted): DrivAerML surface, 435 cars, 10,000 sampled cells, 500 epochs,
lr 1e-3, bf16, no augmentation, the reference ISLA surface configuration
otherwise. Reference: `iw_mt2_lr1e3_seed{42,43}`, pressure 0.0588 / 0.0567
(mean 0.0577; results/instrument_wave_reduction_2026-09-01.json), trained
from an earlier snapshot whose default-flag forward is unchanged by every
later commit (all additions are flag-gated and contract-tested), so the
reference is not re-run. Evaluation on the 48-car validation split with the
instrument-wave evaluation launcher; readout the two-seed mean pressure
relative L2 (wall shear alongside).

**Bars, in readout units.** *Falsified as a free ingredient* if pressure
≥ 0.0594 (more than 3% worse than 0.0577; the two reference seeds differ
by 3.6%, so the bar is one seed spread). *Free* if pressure ≤ 0.0594 and
wall shear within 3% of the reference. Better than the reference by more
than 3% (≤ 0.0560) is reported as a finding but is not the bar: the
collision family is not known to occur on DrivAerML, so no gain is
predicted. Falsified moves the channel to "removable at a cost" and out of
the successor design; free keeps it as a candidate ingredient, still with
no claim that it helps any benchmark.

**Scheduling.** Node MOM2-T added, RUNNING, depends on MOM2; it does not
touch the surface headline lanes (UDRV, W2) or V0-SURF10K.

## 2026-09-08 — HLREG instrument amended before readout: no element labels exist on HiLiftAeroML, so the gap regions are defined geometrically (facing-surface distance), and the artifact-to-mesh alignment needed a scale {#sec-nb-hlreg-amendment}

**What the preregistration assumed.** @sec-nb-hlreg-prereg partitions the
sampled surface points by connected component of the surface mesh (slat,
main element, flap) and by distance to the nearest point of a *different*
component. Two facts found while building the instrument make that partition
unavailable. Each case's CFD boundary mesh (135–148M vertices, 267–291M
triangles, a real single-layer surface: total area 24.6 chord², no
coincident duplicates) is *one connected body*: 98% of its vertices fall in
a single component and the rest are unreferenced singletons, because the
slats and flaps are joined to the wing through their brackets and
flap-track fairings. STL geometry files exist for only 5 of the 180
geometries (41 of 1,800 cases), and they are identical across the ten
angles of a geometry while the CFD meshes are regenerated per case.

**The substitute, and why it measures the same thing.** For a sampled point
p with unit outward normal n, the *facing-surface distance* d_face(p) is the
distance to the nearest boundary-mesh vertex q lying in front of the
surface, (q − p)·n ≥ ½|q − p|, within 10% of the reference chord. On an
open convex surface it is infinite; inside the slat–main and main–flap gaps
and coves, and at the wing–body and pylon junctions, it is the local gap
width; near a high-curvature nose it is the nose radius. The bands are the
preregistered ones, 0–2%, 2–10% and above 10% of chord, with the near band
starting at 0.7% for the reason below. The per-element ratios of the
preregistration cannot be produced and will be reported as not available.

**Three defects found and fixed in three trial runs, each on the first few
cases, before any number was read as a result.** First, the vertex
neighbourhood search by radius returned up to 10⁵ vertices per point and
took the eight worker processes to 95 GB each on a node shared with a
training job; it was replaced by bounded k-nearest queries at two vertex
strides (512 at stride 4 for the near band, 2,048 at stride 64 for the mid
band). Second, the artifact's points are nondimensionalized by a length
0.08% different from the stored L_ref (a similarity fit gives scale
0.99924; rotation 0.01°), and a translation-only alignment left a median
residual of 0.12% chord (q99 0.5%); with the scale the residual is 0.06%
(q99 0.26%). Third, that residual produced spurious "facing" hits at
0.2–0.35% chord for a quarter of all points (the surface itself, seen from
points displaced off it), so the minimum facing distance was raised from
0.2% to 0.7% chord, above the residual and below the gap widths of interest
(CRM-HL slat and flap gaps are of order 1–2% chord). The sign convention of
the stored cell normals is undocumented; the outward side is taken per case
as the direction with fewer facing hits (a body is mostly convex), the
choice is recorded, and its consistency across the 180 cases is a check on
the stored normals. Alignment residual, scale, sign and hit fractions are
stored per case (results/hlreg_*.json when it lands).

**Grading rule, restated.** Per the audit (@sec-nb-audit-2026-09-08, item
6) HLREG locates *output error*, not the input information that causes it:
a slat-gap change moves pressure far from the gap. A uniform ratio across
bands therefore does not falsify a gap-information mechanism; a concentrated
one does not establish it. The preregistered bars are kept and the verdict
is written as localization only.

## 2026-09-08 — Verdict: HLREG falsified in direction — ISLA's advantage over GeoTransolver is smallest in the gap regions (2.0x) and largest on the open surfaces (3.0x); ISLA's own error concentrates at the gaps {#sec-nb-hlreg-verdict}

**Setting.** HiLiftAeroML surface pressure at 35 and 210 training cases,
ISLA against GeoTransolver, two seeds each, the 180 shared validation cases,
existing predictions (@sec-nb-hlreg-prereg). The instrument is the amended
one of @sec-nb-hlreg-amendment: each sampled point is binned by its
facing-surface distance (the distance to the nearest boundary-mesh vertex in
front of the surface within 10% of chord: the local gap or cove width, or
the nose radius of a slat or flap; infinite on an open convex surface) into
0.7–2%, 2–10% and above 10% of chord. Readout per band: the ratio of
GeoTransolver's to ISLA's RMS pressure error over the band's points
(two-seed mean predictions), median over cases; and each model's share of
its own squared error in the band. Bars: supported if near ÷ rest ≥ 1.5 at
35 cases with the ordering preserved at 210; falsified if within 0.87–1.15.

**Instrument checks that passed.** Alignment residual median 0.10% chord
(q99 up to 2.5% on a few fuselage-heavy cases, irrelevant to labelling);
fitted scale 0.9957–1.0032 (median 0.9993). The stored cell normals turned
out to point *inward* on every one of the 360 case-evaluations (the outward
sign, chosen per case as the side with fewer facing hits, was −1 each
time), so the sign convention is consistent and the instrument is well
defined. With the outward sign, 18–32% of points have a facing surface
within 10% chord and 66–72% have one on the inward side (the body's own
opposite wall), as a closed thin body should. No point fell below the 0.7%
floor.

**Readout** (results/hlreg_facing_distance_35_2026-09-08.json and
_210_; medians over 180 cases, 10–90% ranges for the headline ratio):

| rung | near 0.7–2% | mid 2–10% | open >10% | near ÷ rest | cases < 0.87 / in 0.87–1.15 / ≥ 1.5 | ISLA error share near | GT error share near | points near |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 35 cases | 2.01 (seeds 2.02 / 1.96) | 2.02 | 3.00 (2.88 / 3.16) | **0.72** (0.38–1.31) | 61% / 20% / 7% | 59% | 33% | 1,479 |
| 210 cases | 1.87 (1.93 / 1.86) | 2.76 | 2.57 (2.66 / 2.52) | **0.78** (0.54–1.09) | 64% / 27% / 3% | 71% | 56% | 1,479 |

RMS errors per band (35 cases, ISLA / GeoTransolver, physical units of the
artifact): near 2.46 / 5.05, mid 1.29 / 2.49, open 0.88 / 2.66. The
target's RMS is the same in every band (about 175), so the bands differ in
error, not in signal.

**Verdict: falsified, and in the opposite direction to the prediction.**
The near-over-rest ratio is 0.72 at 35 cases, below the 0.87 floor of the
"uniform" band in 61% of cases and above the 1.5 support bar in 7%; at 210
cases it is 0.78 with the same ordering. ISLA's advantage over
GeoTransolver is smallest where the geometry is intricate (the gap regions,
2.0x) and largest where the pressure field is smooth (the open fuselage and
wing surfaces, 3.0x at 35 cases). The error shares say why: 59% of ISLA's
squared error at 35 cases, and 71% at 210, falls on the 15% of points in
the gap regions, against 33% and 56% for GeoTransolver, whose error is
spread over the open surfaces (RMS 2.66 there against ISLA's 0.88). Both
models find the gaps hardest; as data grows ISLA's open-surface error falls
faster than its gap error, so its residual concentrates further at the gaps.

**What it means, within the instrument's limit.** This locates output
error, not input information (@sec-nb-audit-2026-09-08, item 6): a slat-gap
change sets the pressure over the whole element, so the result does not
exclude that gap geometry is what ISLA reads better from few samples. It
excludes the prediction that the resulting *error* advantage sits at the
gaps, and it is consistent with a different picture: ISLA's routing fits
the smooth, global part of the pressure field from few samples where
GeoTransolver's does not, and neither model resolves the local gap flow from
35 cases. The small-feature hypothesis of @sec-mechanism therefore joins the
freestream-direction hypothesis as a prediction that failed, and the
mechanism stays located at the level of the dataset (parametric
multi-element variation), not the surface.

**What's next.** The information question is answerable only by a
perturbation test (gap-region points removed or perturbed against
matched-area controls on a fixed query set), which is deferred behind the
unit-drive control (UDRV), whose outcome decides whether the headline gap
is an architecture result at all. Tech-tree change: HLREG RUNNING → DONE
(falsified, localization).

## 2026-09-09 — Preregistered: UDRV-INT, GeoTransolver-volume with the unit freestream direction (does the interior comparison inherit the baselines' input-scale confound?) {#sec-nb-udrv-int-prereg}

**Setting.** The unit-drive control on the surface task (@sec-nb-udrv-prereg)
returned its first readout: plain Transolver at 35 HiLift cases fed the
unit freestream direction instead of the physical velocity (2,679.5 in/s)
scores 0.113 against 0.398 with the physical vector, below ISLA's 0.138. The
surface headline is being re-examined on that basis by the audit session
and no surface claim is edited here. GeoTransolver's volume configuration
also receives the physical freestream (`global_embedding: global_data.U_inf`,
38.9 m/s on DrivAerML) where ISLA receives the unit direction, so every
interior comparison in @sec-interior (ISLA query tokens + SDF ahead on
pressure and velocity, behind on eddy viscosity) carries the same
asymmetry, at a magnitude 69x smaller than on HiLift and constant across
cases. Whether the constant 38.9 costs GeoTransolver-volume accuracy is not
known; on the DrivAerML surface task GeoTransolver at the same magnitude
beats ISLA, so the effect there is at most modest.

**Instrument.** Two chains `udrv_gt_vol_seed{42,43}`: the frozen
GeoTransolver-volume lane (27.6M parameters, 435 cars, 10,000 interior
points, 500 epochs, lr 1e-3, bf16, no augmentation) with the single change
`forward_kwargs.global_embedding=global_data.U_inf_dir`, evaluated on the
48 validation cars. Reference: `v0_gt_vol_seed{42,43}`, pressure 0.0620,
velocity 0.1334, eddy viscosity 0.0939 (seed spread under 1%;
results/a35_v0_reduction_2026-09-08c.json). Comparator: ISLA query tokens +
SDF, 0.0567 / 0.0853 / 0.1215 (365 surface cells) and the running
V0-SURF10K arm.

**Bars, in readout units.** *Confound present* if any field improves by
more than 5% (pressure ≤ 0.0589, velocity ≤ 0.1267, eddy viscosity ≤
0.0892); *null* if all three lie within 3% of the reference (pressure
0.0601–0.0639, velocity 0.1294–0.1374, eddy viscosity 0.0911–0.0967);
between, partial, per field. Consequences, fixed now: if confound present,
the interior rows of the verdict table and the chapter-8 ratios are
restated against the unit-drive GeoTransolver-volume, and the "ISLA leads on
pressure and velocity" statement is withdrawn wherever the unit-drive
baseline is ahead; if null, the interior comparison stands as written and
the confound is recorded as surface-specific (a magnitude effect). Either
way the eddy-viscosity gap is re-read against the new reference.

**Scheduling.** Node UDRV-INT, RUNNING, depends on UDRV (first readout) and
V0 (reference). GT-volume lanes run about 0.05 s per step (@sec-interior);
two chains, no other lane touched.

## 2026-09-09 — Verdict: MOM2-T — the second-moment channel is free where ISLA is trained (DrivAerML surface pressure 0.0583 against 0.0577, within 1%) {#sec-nb-mom2t-verdict}

**Setting and bars** (@sec-nb-mom2t-prereg): the reference ISLA surface
configuration on DrivAerML at 435 cars with `second_moment_features=true`,
two seeds, frozen protocol, against the reference lanes
`iw_mt2_lr1e3_seed{42,43}`. Free if the two-seed mean pressure relative L2
is ≤ 0.0594 (3% above the reference 0.0577; one seed spread); falsified as
a free ingredient if ≥ 0.0594.

**Readout** (results/mom2t_reduction_2026-09-09.json; 48 validation cars):

| arm | seed 42 | seed 43 | mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| reference (eight relational invariants) | 0.0588 | 0.0567 | 0.0577 |
| with the second-moment channel | 0.0577 | 0.0588 | **0.0583** |

**Verdict: free.** The channel costs 0.9% on pressure, a quarter of the
seed spread, and buys nothing, as predicted (the collision family is not
known to occur on DrivAerML). The wall-shear half of the bar could not be
read: the surface evaluation writes only the pressure metric to
metrics.jsonl for these lanes, so wall shear is *not measured* here and the
verdict rests on pressure. The channel stays a candidate ingredient for the
successor design with the qualification of @sec-nb-mom2-verdict: it removes
a documented blind spot at no measured cost, and there is still no claim
that it helps any benchmark. Tech-tree change: MOM2-T RUNNING → DONE (free).

## 2026-09-09 — Verdict: V0-SURF10K null — giving the interacting configuration 10,000 surface cells instead of about 365 changes no interior number (all fields within 3%) {#sec-nb-v0surf-verdict}

**Setting and bars** (@sec-nb-v0surf-prereg). Every ISLA interior arm in
@sec-interior was trained with about 365 vehicle surface cells because the
volume recipe subsampled boundaries by cells and then by points
(@sec-nb-audit-2026-09-08). The query-token + signed-distance configuration
was rerun with the dataset variant `boundary_subsample: cells`, so that the
intended 10,000 cells reach the model (runs `v0_isla_qtsdf_surf10k_seed{42,43}`,
snapshot `code_isla4`, otherwise the frozen V0 protocol; 0.56 s per step and
9.1 GB against 0.28 s and 6.3 GB for the 365-cell arm, since the per-slice
geometry now spans 20,000 tokens). Bars: *surface information matters* if
pressure ≤ 0.054 or eddy viscosity ≤ 0.115 (5% better); *null* if all three
fields lie within 3% of the 365-cell arm.

**Readout** (48 validation cars, two-seed means;
results/a35_v0_reduction_2026-09-09.json):

| arm | surface cells | pressure | velocity | eddy viscosity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver-volume (reads no surface) | 0 | 0.0620 | 0.1334 | 0.0939 |
| ISLA query tokens + SDF | ~365 | 0.0567 | 0.0853 | 0.1215 |
| ISLA query tokens + SDF | 10,000 | **0.0572** (0.0570 / 0.0574) | **0.0848** (0.0838 / 0.0858) | **0.1187** (0.1101 / 0.1273) |

**Verdict: null.** Pressure +0.9%, velocity −0.6%, eddy viscosity −2.3%,
all inside the 3% band; the eddy-viscosity seed spread (0.110 / 0.127) is
wider than the change. Twenty-seven times more surface information adds
nothing measurable to any interior field. Read with @sec-nb-qt-sdf-verdict
(interaction closes the pressure gap, the signed distance flips velocity)
and @sec-nb-qt-h256-verdict (width buys 2–4% uniformly), the interior
result is carried by the interacting interior queries and their wall
distance; the boundary sample, which ISLA was designed around, is close to
irrelevant on this task at this query density. Two things this does not
say: that ISLA ignores the surface (a zero-surface control was not run, and
365 cells still fix the pose and scale), and anything about the surface
task. Consequences: the chapter's 365-cell numbers stand as its headline
numbers, with the 10,000-cell rerun as their confirmation; PASSIVE2 (the
passive decoder with the full surface) loses its motivation, because the
passive arm's deficit cannot be a surface-information deficit; and the
open interior question narrows to the eddy-viscosity gap, whose remaining
candidate is GeoTransolver-volume's query-to-query local aggregation.
Tech-tree change: V0-SURF10K RUNNING → DONE (null); PASSIVE2 stays PLANNED
with its motivation withdrawn.


## 2026-09-09 — UDRV verdict: the baselines' small-data deficit was an input-scaling artifact; unit-drive GeoTransolver and Transolver beat ISLA at 35 cases {#sec-nb-udrv-verdict}

**Setting.** Every HiLiftAeroML comparison in this book fed GeoTransolver
and plain Transolver the physical freestream velocity, 2,679.5 in/s (the
dataset is in inches and seconds; the pipeline nondimensionalizes fields and
coordinates but passes this one global vector through), while ISLA received
the unit freestream direction. Against those baselines ISLA had been 2.8x
more accurate at 35 training cases, 2.2x at 210, at parity at 1,260, 1.8x
and 1.4x on never-seen geometries and 5.0x at a fixed angle of attack, and
the program had spent its controls on the optimizer (learning rate, training
length, third seeds), on the same-family Transolver, and on transplanting
ISLA's invariants into the baselines, all of which kept the physical
velocity as an input. The independent audit (@sec-nb-audit-2026-09-08, item
1) showed that GeoTransolver's global-context projector, untrained and at
production dimensions, spreads each head over about 200 of 256 slices at
unit drive magnitude and collapses to one slice at 2,679.5, with the largest
context entry rising from 0.66 to 1,530; Transolver concatenates the raw
vector into every token's features. That was a conditioning difference at
initialization, not a result about trained models. UDRV (@sec-nb-udrv-prereg)
was the trained control.

**Preregistered bars.** With g = ln(baseline / ISLA) the reference log gap
(1.02 for GeoTransolver, 1.07 for Transolver at 35 cases), the control is
*supported* if the unit-drive baseline closes at least one third of the log
gap: GeoTransolver ≤ 0.27 (within 1.96x of ISLA), Transolver ≤ 0.29;
*falsified* if it lies within the reference seed band widened by one band
width: GeoTransolver ≥ 0.34, Transolver ≥ 0.38; between, partial. The
consequence of "supported" was fixed in advance: the verdict sentence, the
data-multiplier reading and every 2.8x statement are rewritten with the
unit-drive baseline as the reference, and the fair-comparison protocol gains
a rule that every model receives the drive at unit scale.

**Instrument.** Four of the eight lanes of highlift/udrv_lanes.tsv
(launcher highlift/hl_udrv_aga.sbatch): GeoTransolver and Transolver on the
35-case `super_scarce` split, seeds 42 and 43, under the frozen ladder
protocol (10,000 sampled points, 500 epochs, bf16, no augmentation, final
checkpoint, the shared 180-case validation set spanning 118 geometries), at
the learning rates the reference lanes used (GeoTransolver 1e-3, Transolver
3e-3), with one hydra override each and nothing else changed:
`forward_kwargs.global_embedding=global_data.U_inf_dir` for GeoTransolver,
`forward_kwargs.fx.source=global_data.U_inf_dir` for Transolver. Readout:
two-seed mean over validation cases of the surface-pressure relative L2,
with velocity and wall shear alongside; paired per-case statistics on the
180 case-level pairs (each case scored by each arm's seed-mean error), the
exact sign test on n = 180, and per-geometry counts on the 118 geometries.
Reference arms from the existing reductions: GeoTransolver 0.381 with the
physical velocity (three seeds 0.374, 0.409, 0.359), Transolver 0.404
(0.406, 0.398, 0.409), ISLA 0.138 (0.135, 0.141, 0.138).

**Result** (results/udrv_reduction_2026-09-09.json; two seeds each, 180
cases):

| arm | pressure (seeds → mean) | velocity | wall shear | ÷ ISLA (pressure) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA (reference, three seeds) | 0.135 / 0.141 / 0.138 → 0.138 | 0.168 | 0.256 | 1.00 |
| GeoTransolver, physical velocity (three seeds) | 0.374 / 0.409 / 0.359 → 0.381 | 0.342 | 0.564 | 2.76 |
| GeoTransolver, unit direction | 0.124 / 0.125 → **0.124** | 0.145 | 0.229 | **0.90** |
| Transolver, physical velocity (three seeds) | 0.406 / 0.398 / 0.409 → 0.404 | 0.372 | 0.602 | 2.93 |
| Transolver, unit direction | 0.117 / 0.113 → **0.115** | 0.140 | 0.216 | **0.83** |

Paired per case, seed-mean errors: the unit-drive GeoTransolver is lower
than ISLA on 130 of 180 cases and on 84 of 118 geometries (median ISLA ÷
GeoTransolver 1.09, 10–90% range 0.90–1.43; sign test p = 2e-9); the
unit-drive Transolver on 152 of 180 cases and 102 of 118 geometries (median
1.17, 0.98–1.58; p = 8e-22). Against its own physical-velocity lane each
unit-drive baseline is lower on 180 of 180 cases and 118 of 118 geometries
(median factor 3.4 for GeoTransolver, 3.8 for Transolver). The two unit-drive
seeds of each arm differ by about 1% (GeoTransolver) and 4% (Transolver);
the differences to ISLA are 10% and 17% of ISLA's error.

**Verdict: supported, far past the bar, for both arms.** GeoTransolver's
unit-drive mean 0.124 is below the 0.27 support bar by a factor of two, and
Transolver's 0.115 below 0.29 by the same; neither is anywhere near the
falsifier. The baselines' small-data deficit on HiLiftAeroML was an
input-scaling artifact of the comparison protocol, not a property of the
architectures. With the artifact removed, both baselines are 1.1–1.2x
*more* accurate than ISLA at 35 cases. The steel-man controls could not have
found this: every one of them kept the physical velocity as an input, and a
control that holds the decisive variable fixed cannot detect it.

**What this means for the mechanism.** The projector collapse at
initialization is the mechanism's signature, and the trained result says
that neither baseline recovers from a global input of magnitude 2,679.5
within 500 epochs at 35 cases; at 1,260 cases the physical-drive
GeoTransolver reached parity with ISLA anyway, so the effect is a slow start
rather than a ceiling. Nothing about ISLA carried the earlier margin, which
is consistent with the ablations (no single ISLA ingredient moved its error
by more than 16%) and with the transplant test (ISLA's invariants did not
help the baselines: the input they were appended to was the problem).

**What changed in the book.** The verdict sentence (@sec-verdict) is
rewritten: ISLA has no measured accuracy advantage over GeoTransolver or
Transolver once every model receives the freestream at unit scale; its
contribution is contracts and, pending its own control, the interior
configuration. The fair-comparison protocol (@sec-fair-comparison) gains the
rule that every architecture receives the unit direction (and, where speed
varies, a separately normalized speed channel). Every HiLiftAeroML number
measured against a physical-velocity baseline (2.8x, 2.2x, 5.0x, 1.8x, 1.4x,
180/180 and 118/118 wins, the 6x data multiplier, the force-coefficient
margin, the HLREG ratios, the regime-extrapolation ordering, GeoTransolver's
HiLift learning-rate instability) is relabelled a physical-drive
measurement in chapters 4, 5, 6 and 12 and in CLAIMS.md; the tech tree
marks HLGEN, CTRL, T1, INV, A35, A35B, W2, W2F, DEFL, HLREG, GEOSTAT and
STEST as superseded as comparisons, and MT3 is gated on UDRV-L and UDRV-INT.
DrivAerML numbers are unchanged; GeoTransolver's leads there were measured
with the physical velocity (38.9 m/s) and are lower bounds.

**Pending.** (1) The four fixed-angle lanes of UDRV (GeoTransolver and
Transolver at 126 geometries, 12°, unit drive) are at about epoch 200 of
500; the 5.0x fixed-angle figure is "against physical-drive baselines,
unit-drive rerun pending" until they land. (2) UDRV-L
(@sec-nb-udrvl-prereg) reruns the higher rungs. (3) UDRV-INT
(@sec-nb-udrv-int-prereg) runs GeoTransolver-volume with the unit
direction on the interior task, where the same asymmetry exists at 38.9 m/s.
Tech-tree change: UDRV RUNNING → DONE at 35 cases (supported); UDRV-L added,
RUNNING.

### Preregistered: UDRV-L, the HiLiftAeroML ladder with unit-drive baselines {#sec-nb-udrvl-prereg}

*Written before launch; file results/udrv_ladder_preregistration_2026-09-09.md.*

**Why.** The unit-drive control (@sec-nb-udrv-verdict) was supported far
beyond its bar at 35 training cases: GeoTransolver fed the unit freestream
direction reaches a surface-pressure relative L2 of 0.124 (seeds 0.124,
0.125) against 0.381 with the physical velocity, and plain Transolver 0.115
(0.117, 0.113) against 0.404; ISLA is 0.138. The baselines' small-data
deficit on HiLiftAeroML was an input-scaling artifact of the comparison
protocol, and with the artifact removed both baselines are more accurate
than ISLA at 35 cases (per case: GeoTransolver lower on 130 of 180,
Transolver on 152 of 180). Every other HiLiftAeroML comparison in the book
(210 and 1,260 cases; 4 and 21 training geometries; the fixed angle, whose
unit-drive lanes are still training) used the physical-velocity baselines
and is therefore not a valid comparison until rerun.

**Lanes.** Frozen ladder protocol (10,000 sampled points, 500 epochs, bf16,
no augmentation, final checkpoint, each split's own validation set),
launcher highlift/hl_udrv_aga.sbatch, lane table highlift/udrv_lanes.tsv
rows 8–17, the only change from the reference lanes being the drive
override (GeoTransolver `forward_kwargs.global_embedding=global_data.U_inf_dir`,
Transolver `forward_kwargs.fx.source=global_data.U_inf_dir`), learning
rates as declared for the reference lanes:

| lanes | model | split | lr | seeds | reference (physical drive) | ISLA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8–9 | GeoTransolver | scarce (210 cases) | 1e-3 | 42, 43 | 0.141 (three seeds) | 0.065 |
| 10–11 | Transolver | scarce (210 cases) | 3e-3 | 42, 43 | 0.087 | 0.065 |
| 12–13 | GeoTransolver | geometry_super_scarce (4 geometries, 40 cases) | 1e-3 | 42, 43 | 0.449 | 0.250 |
| 14–15 | GeoTransolver | geometry_scarce (21 geometries, 210 cases) | 1e-3 | 42, 43 | 0.143 | 0.102 |
| 16–17 | GeoTransolver | full (1,260 cases) | 1e-3 | 42, 43 | 0.042 | 0.041 |

Lanes 16–17 are launched after the fixed-angle lanes finish, to stay inside
the program's node budget.

**Predictions and bars.** Prediction, from the 35-case result: the
unit-drive baselines match or beat ISLA at every rung. Readout per rung:
two-seed mean pressure relative L2 of the unit-drive baseline against
ISLA's on the same validation cases, with the paired per-case and
per-geometry counts.

- **ISLA has a data-efficiency advantage at a rung** only if ISLA's error
  is at least 10% below the unit-drive baseline's (ratio baseline ÷ ISLA
  ≥ 1.10) and ISLA is lower on at least two thirds of the validation cases.
  Ten percent is about ten times the seed spread of these arms (under 1%)
  and is the smallest difference the book has treated as a finding.
- **Parity** if the ratio lies within 0.95–1.05.
- **Baseline ahead** if the ratio is ≤ 0.90 (as at 35 cases: 0.90 for
  GeoTransolver, 0.83 for Transolver).
- Between the bands: reported as a small difference in the stated direction.

The unseen-geometry rungs decide whether "ISLA generalizes across wing
geometries from few samples" survives: it does only if the ratio at 4 or 21
training geometries is ≥ 1.10 with the per-geometry count on ISLA's side
(≥ 12 of 18).

**What the outcomes change.** If the unit-drive baselines match or beat
ISLA at every rung, the book's HiLiftAeroML chapters become a report of a
protocol artifact and its correction, ISLA's standing on surface pressure
becomes "parity to behind on both datasets", and the program's remaining
ISLA-specific claims are the contracts (exact covariance, passive decode),
the interior configuration (itself awaiting the unit-drive control of
GeoTransolver-volume, UDRV-INT), and cost. If ISLA keeps an advantage at
some rung, that rung and its mechanism become the program's only accuracy
claim and are stated with the unit-drive baseline as the reference. The
510-case rung, the 20,000-token floor and the deflection lanes still
training with physical-velocity baselines are not evaluated as comparisons;
their ISLA arms are kept as measurements.

**Scheduling.** Node UDRV-L, RUNNING, depends on UDRV; lanes 8–15
launched, 16–17 queued behind the fixed-angle lanes. Edges UDRV → UDRV-L,
UDRV-L → MT3, UDRV-L → ABUPT.
