Every ratio agrees with its pool-frame value within 2%. The uniform errors
agree within 1.3% except the similarity-gauge corner at 10,000 cells, which
reads 5% lower in the sample frame (seeds 0.0680 / 0.0695 against 0.0742 /
0.0712; its per-seed ratios 1.56 / 1.55 against 1.40 / 1.66). That
difference is sampling variance, not a frame effect, shown two ways.
First, the two probe families drew *different cells*: of the 10,000
uniform cells per car the sample-frame and pool-frame evaluations share 0–4
(125–312 of 80,000), and the biased draws differ in count per car (Poisson
inclusion; e.g. 10,213 against 10,094), so the two evaluations are
independent random samples of each car, and the gauge corner at an eighth
of its training count is the configuration with the largest
sample-to-sample variance (its seed spread there is 4%). The frame shift
itself (pool centre minus sample centre) is 0.002–0.004 in nondimensional
units. Second, a direct test: the gauge corner's checkpoint evaluated on
three cars with every point translated by (0.37, −0.21, 0.11), about a
hundred times the frame shift, changes its output by 4.9–6.0 × 10⁻⁶
relative (float32 roundoff; `highlift/infer_translation_test.py`, a copy of
the recipe's `infer.py` with the check inserted; nothing in the recipe
modified). ISLA's forward receives points, normals, the drive and the
measure weights; the stored centre is not an input, so the frame in which
the dataset centres the mesh cannot reach the model. The ISLA rows of the
density-bias tables are therefore the same in either frame, and the
finding that motivated the canonical sample-frame datasets (the baselines
had been handed the pool's unbiased mean) is a baseline-only correction.

**HiLift density probes: sample frame from the start (program instruction,
ISLA Main, 2026-09-10).** Every HiLiftAeroML density probe of the SCALE
study, for all three architectures, runs on one canonical pair of
sample-frame datasets built by this track while the HiLift lanes train:
`highlift_probe_{biased3,unif2}_sf.yaml` (reader pool 40,000 cells, for
10,000-cell probes) and `highlift_probe_{biased3,unif2}_sf_80k.yaml`
(320,000-cell pool, for 80,000-cell probes), in `$T/recipe/datasets`. They
derive from `highlift_surface.yaml` (the dataset the lanes train on) exactly
as `drivaer_probe_*_sf{,_80k}.yaml` derive from `drivaer_ml_surface.yaml`:
the reader's cut becomes a fixed 4x pool; a sampler is inserted after the
field transforms (`PoissonBiasedSubsampleMesh`, bias 10 on centroid x below
the per-sample median with exact inverse-inclusion weights composed into the
measure, for the biased column; `SubsampleMesh` for the uniform control);
`CenterMesh` moves from its training position to directly after the
sampler; `DropDegenerateCells` follows it. Reader, pattern, manifest,
global-data merge, augmentations, freestream direction, normals,
nondimensionalization, normalization and targets are unchanged; each file's
header states the derivation. Smoke test on the ISLA HiLift reference
`mt2_hl_lr1_seed42` (legacy checkpoint, resolved by `code_eval`, float32,
10,000 cells, both columns, 180 validation cases): loads at epoch 500,
samples 9,994 (uniform, after degenerate-cell drops) and 10,030 (biased,
Poisson count) cells on the first case, writes per-sample rows and a summary
equal to their mean (range guard satisfied): pressure 0.0400 uniform against
0.542 biased, a 13.6x ratio for the constant-gauge reference at a single
seed, of the same size as its DrivAerML ratio (12x). HiLift probe results
enter the HiLift half of this entry when the lanes land.

## 2026-09-09 — Preregistered: QTDENS, does GeoTransolver-volume's eddy-viscosity lead come from reading the interior sample's density, and does an ISLA-native query-neighbour channel close the gap? {#sec-nb-qt-density-prereg}

**Setting.** On the DrivAerML interior task ISLA's query-token
configuration with the signed distance (the reference arm: about 365
surface cells, 10,000 interior queries) scores 0.0567 / 0.0853 / 0.1215 on
pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity ν_t against GeoTransolver-volume's
0.0620 / 0.1334 / 0.0939 (48 validation cars, two-seed means;
results/a35_v0_reduction_2026-09-09.json). The ν_t gap, 1.29x, survived
surface-patch local features (@sec-nb-qt-lf-verdict), a width increase to
256 (@sec-nb-qt-h256-verdict) and 27x more surface cells
(@sec-nb-v0surf-verdict). GeoTransolver-volume's one remaining
untransplanted ingredient is its local aggregation over *neighbouring
interior points* at six radii. Two readings of what that ingredient
supplies compete. The physical reading: near-wall flow structure that the
global slice routing cannot resolve. The instrumental reading, raised by the
audit (@sec-nb-audit-2026-09-08, item 7): DrivAerML's ν_t is a hybrid
RANS/LES modelled viscosity tied to the local grid scale, the interior
sample is drawn from the CFD volume mesh, so the local sampling density is a
proxy for mesh scale and hence for the closure's filter length; a model
that reads density reads the discretization, not the physics.

**Arms** (two seeds each, 42 and 43; the frozen interior protocol: 435
cars, 500 epochs, lr 1e-3, bf16, no augmentation, dataset
`drivaer_ml_volume_mt` so the surface sample matches the reference arm's
365 cells; code snapshot `code_qtdens` from branch isla-query-density;
launcher v0/v0_qtdens_aga.sbatch):

- *Density* (`v0_isla_qtsdf_dens_seed{42,43}`): the reference model plus
  `query_density_feature=true`: each query token receives the number of
  other queries within 0.05 gauge units (about 5% of the car's RMS radius),
  entered as [log(1+c), log(1+c) − log n_queries]. This channel carries no
  physics and no geometry beyond the sample's own spacing.
- *Neighbours* (`v0_isla_qtsdf_nbr_seed{42,43}`): the reference model plus
  `query_neighbor_features=true` (k = 16): the mean over the 16 nearest
  other queries of the pair invariants {|Δr|, log|Δr|, Δr̂·n_q, Δr̂·d,
  n_j·n_q, n_j·d, (s_j − s_q)/gauge} plus the 16th-neighbour distance and
  its log. This is the ISLA-native transplant of GeoTransolver-volume's
  query-to-query aggregation: relative geometry and wall-distance
  differences of the neighbours, exactly equivariant, and it contains the
  density information as well (the k-th neighbour distance).

Both channels are exact invariants of the gauge-normalized query cloud
(contract-tested: SE(3) covariance, drive degree one, measure-scale
invariance, gauge scale equivariance; 56 ISLA tests pass), and both make
the prediction depend on the query cloud, as the query-token mode already
does (@sec-nb-qmass-verdict).

**Bars, in readout units (ν_t, two-seed mean; GeoTransolver-volume
0.0939).** The ν_t seed spread of this configuration is wide (h256 seeds
0.1188 / 0.1169; 10,000-cell seeds 0.1101 / 0.1273), so the bars are the
ones the width control used. An arm *closes the gap* if ν_t ≤ 0.1033
(within 1.10x of GeoTransolver-volume); it *fails* if ν_t ≥ 0.1174 (at
least 1.25x, the reference arm's 1.29x within noise); between,
inconclusive. Pressure and velocity are reported alongside; a change of more
than 5% in either (pressure outside 0.0539–0.0595, velocity outside
0.0810–0.0896) is reported as an effect of the channel in its own right.

**What each outcome means.**
- Density closes the gap: GeoTransolver-volume's ν_t lead is, at least in
  large part, a reading of the mesh scale through the sample density, not
  of the flow; the book states the ν_t comparison as a discretization
  artefact of the benchmark, the density channel is *not* adopted as a model
  ingredient, and the interior ν_t metric is flagged as one that rewards
  reading the mesh.
- Neighbours close the gap and density does not: the missing ingredient is
  neighbouring-point relative geometry (the physical reading); the channel
  becomes a candidate for the successor configuration, with its query-cloud
  dependence measured next.
- Both close it: the two readings cannot be separated by this design; the
  density result takes precedence in the interpretation (the cheaper
  explanation), and a density-matched control (neighbour channel with the
  distance features removed) is the next node.
- Neither: the ν_t gap is not in the query-side inputs at this width and
  depth; the remaining candidates are GeoTransolver-volume's effective width
  448 and its multi-radius encoding, and the thread is deprioritized.

**Scheduling.** Node QTDENS added (RUNNING), depends on QT-SDF and
V0-SURF10K. Four GPU nodes at most; the density arm launches first, the
neighbour arm when the program is at or below 30 nodes.

**Amendment before readout (float32 instrument).** The program's reporting
instrument changed to float32 inference while these lanes trained
(@sec-nb-fp32-instrument): the same weights score differently under
different bf16 evaluation graphs by amounts comparable to the bars above.
The bars are therefore restated as ratios to the *float32* GeoTransolver-volume
reference, evaluated with the same launcher: an arm closes the gap if its
float32 ν_t ≤ 1.10x that reference, fails if ≥ 1.25x; pressure and velocity
changes above 5% relative to the float32 ISLA query-token + SDF reference
are reported as channel effects. Both passes are run (bf16 into the usual
directory, float32 into `v0_evals_fp32/`); the verdict is graded on float32
and states the precision in every table. The float32 references landed
(same checkpoints, identical points, `v0_evals_fp32/`): GeoTransolver-volume
0.0515 / 0.1088 / 0.0879 and ISLA query tokens + SDF 0.0547 / 0.0796 / 0.1116
(pressure / velocity / ν_t), so bf16 had inflated GeoTransolver-volume by
20–23% and ISLA by 4–8%, and in float32 GeoTransolver-volume leads on
pressure (ISLA ÷ GT 1.06) while ISLA leads on velocity (0.73). In readout
units the ν_t bars are: **closes the gap if ν_t ≤ 0.0967**, **fails if
ν_t ≥ 0.1099**; the reference arm sits at 0.1116 (1.27x). Pressure effects
are reported against 0.0547 (ISLA) and 0.0515 (GeoTransolver-volume), with
the 5% channel-effect band on pressure 0.0520–0.0574 and on velocity
0.0756–0.0836.

## 2026-09-09 — Ops: the DrivAerML interior stall is a hang inside `pin_memory` in the reader's prefetch thread, not a Lustre read; diagnosed from in-process stack dumps {#sec-nb-interior-stall-diagnosis}

**Symptom.** From about 12:14 on 2026-09-09 every interior (DrivAerML
volume) training lane across three sessions stopped advancing within one
to twenty epochs of starting or resuming (the four QTDENS lanes at epochs
312 / 302 / 292 / 302, a coordinator lane at epoch 1, a transfer-session
lane at 22), while every HiLiftAeroML lane kept stepping. Each stalled link
died an hour later on the NCCL watchdog's collective timeout inside the
recipe's per-step failure barrier and its chain resumed from the last
checkpoint, only to stall again within an epoch or two, so each lane
burned an hour of four idle GPUs per cycle. The wall-clock coincidence had
suggested the known hourly DrivAerML Lustre stall.

**What was excluded, and how.** (1) A hung read: a thread-state dump of a
stalled link (highlift/qtdens_thread_dump.sh) showed no thread in
uninterruptible I/O wait on any rank and no dataset file open; three ranks
spun at 100% CPU (the all-reduce busy-wait) and one slept on a futex at 7%.
(2) Bad files or stripes: from a healthy allocation the first 4 MB of all
11,616 training files and 1 MB at each of the 8 stripes of all 2,420
interior memmaps read in under 5 s each (highlift/qtdens_probe_files.sh,
qtdens_probe_stripes.sh); no OST inactive. (3) The new model code: both
QTDENS channels run forward and backward at production shape on CPU,
including duplicated query positions, and the coordinator's lane without
them stalled too. (4) A resume-specific bug: the first stalls followed a
resume, but the epoch-1 stall did not.

**Instrument.** py-spy cannot attach (ptrace scope), so a diagnostic
`sitecustomize.py` was placed first on PYTHONPATH in the QTDENS code
snapshot: when `FAULT_DIR` is set it arms `faulthandler.dump_traceback_later`
to write every thread's Python stack to
`$FAULT_DIR/fault_rank<RANK>_<pid>.log` every ten minutes. The probe lane
(dens seed 42, resuming from epoch 310, collective timeout 20 min) stalled
again at epoch 311 step 103 and dumped.

**Finding.** On the stuck rank the main thread waits in
`concurrent.futures.Future.result()` (physicsnemo/datapipes/protocols.py:366
← datapipes/dataloader.py:459, 499, 306 ← recipe train.py:548), the prefetch
hand-off, which has no timeout; the prefetch worker it waits for is inside
`TensorDict.pin_memory` (tensordict/base.py:6069 → `_apply_nest` →
`pin_memory`) called from `DomainMeshReader.__getitem__`
(physicsnemo/datapipes/readers/mesh.py:690, `dm = dm.pin_memory()`) via
mesh_dataset.py:224. A second thread waits normally on the I/O pump's
backpressure semaphore (datapipes/io_pump.py:152). The other three ranks
are in train.py:342 `_step_failure_barrier`, the collective the watchdog
then names. The stall is therefore a hang inside CUDA host-memory pinning
of the just-loaded sample, in the reader's prefetch thread. Why pinning
began hanging on DrivAerML interior lanes on every node from 12:14, and not
on HiLift lanes, is not established (host pinned memory or driver level; the
interior sample pins the 10,000-point interior fields plus boundary fields
per step).

**Workaround and test.** The recipe exposes `dataloader.pin_memory`
(base.yaml sets it true). The probe lane was relaunched with
`dataloader.pin_memory=false` (job 694119); the acceptance criterion is
fifteen minutes of normal stepping past epoch 312, after which the other
QTDENS lanes and the coordinator's held interior chains are released with
the same override. The cost of pageable host-to-device copies is read from
the probe's step time against the 0.287 s of the pinned run.

**Outcome.** The probe resumed from epoch 310, passed the stall point and
stepped normally for fifteen minutes (epoch 327 at the check), where four
pinned attempts had hung at epoch 311–312. Step time 0.388 s against
0.287 s pinned: the workaround costs 35% per step on the 10,000-query ISLA
lane. The other three QTDENS lanes and the coordinator's held interior
chains were released with the same override. Root cause (why host-memory
pinning began hanging on DrivAerML interior lanes on every node from
12:14) remains open; a bounded wait on the prefetch hand-off in
physicsnemo/datapipes/dataloader.py would turn this class of hang into a
logged failure instead of an hour of idle GPUs per link and is the
datapipe follow-up to file. Diagnostic tools left in the task directory:
highlift/qtdens_thread_dump.sh, qtdens_probe_files.sh,
qtdens_probe_stripes.sh, code_qtdens/sitecustomize.py, tools/pyspy.

**Correction, two hours later: pinning was the site, not the cause.** With
pinning off the probe lane advanced from epoch 310 to about 389 and stalled
twice more; the new dumps place the stuck rank (rank 2) inside
`TensorDict.to(device)` (physicsnemo/mesh/domain_mesh.py:1686 →
tensordict/base.py:16188), the host-to-device copy of the loaded sample, with
the other three ranks in the step barrier. One rank's CUDA context stops
completing host-side operations at a random point, first pinning and then
the copy: a device- or driver-level hang on the node, not the datapipe, the
model or Lustre. It affects every DrivAerML interior lane since 12:14 and no
HiLiftAeroML lane; the mechanism is not established from user space. What
holds: the chains progress between stalls, so the collective timeout on the
QTDENS lanes was cut to 600 s (a stalled link dies and resumes in ten
minutes instead of sixty) and links idle for more than fifteen minutes are
recycled; `pin_memory=false` is kept because it removes one hang site at a
35% step-time cost. Expected loss: one stall per thirty to sixty minutes
per lane, each costing ten minutes plus up to ten epochs of replay.

## 2026-09-10 — Verdict: QTDENS — neither a query-density scalar nor an ISLA-native query-neighbour channel closes the interior eddy-viscosity gap (float32 ν_t 1.32x and 1.30x GeoTransolver-volume against the reference arm's 1.28x) {#sec-nb-qt-density-verdict}

**Setting and bars** (@sec-nb-qt-density-prereg and its float32
amendment). ISLA query tokens + SDF trails GeoTransolver-volume on eddy
viscosity ν_t; two readings of GeoTransolver-volume's neighbouring-point
aggregation competed: it reads the local sampling density (mesh scale,
hence the hybrid RANS/LES closure's filter length) or it reads neighbouring
flow geometry. Two flag-gated ISLA channels on the reference arm, two seeds
each, frozen protocol, 365 surface cells: a density scalar (other queries
within 0.05 gauge units) and a k = 16 neighbour aggregation of pair
invariants including wall-distance differences. Graded on float32
(@sec-nb-fp32-instrument): closes the gap if ν_t ≤ 0.0967, fails if
ν_t ≥ 0.1099; pressure and velocity effects reported if outside 5% of the
float32 reference arm (0.0520–0.0574 and 0.0756–0.0836). Training: both
channels cost nothing at training time (0.28 s per step and 6.0 GB, identical
to the reference arm); the lanes were slowed by the interior stall of
@sec-nb-interior-stall-diagnosis, not by the channels.

**Readout** (48 validation cars, two-seed means; float32 in
`v0_evals_fp32/`, bf16 in `v0_evals/`; results/qtdens_reduction_2026-09-10.json):

| arm | precision | pressure | velocity | ν_t (seeds) | ν_t ÷ GeoTransolver-volume |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver-volume | float32 | 0.0515 | 0.1090 | 0.0877 (0.0869 / 0.0884) | 1.00 |
| ISLA query tokens + SDF (reference) | float32 | 0.0548 | 0.0801 | 0.1122 (0.1058 / 0.1187) | 1.28 |
| + query-density scalar | float32 | 0.0542 | 0.0779 | **0.1155** (0.1160 / 0.1150) | **1.32** |
| + query-neighbour channel (k = 16) | float32 | 0.0541 | 0.0795 | **0.1138** (0.1069 / 0.1207) | **1.30** |
| GeoTransolver-volume | bfloat16 | 0.0620 | 0.1334 | 0.0939 | 1.00 |
| ISLA query tokens + SDF (reference) | bfloat16 | 0.0567 | 0.0853 | 0.1215 | 1.29 |
| + query-density scalar | bfloat16 | 0.0564 | 0.0840 | 0.1252 | 1.33 |
| + query-neighbour channel | bfloat16 | 0.0563 | 0.0855 | 0.1239 | 1.32 |

**Verdict: neither closes the gap; both fail the bar.** In float32 the
density arm's ν_t is 0.1155 and the neighbour arm's 0.1138, both above the
0.1099 failure line and both within the reference arm's seed spread
(0.1058–0.1187); the neighbour arm's own seeds span 0.1069–0.1207. Pressure
(−1%) and velocity (−0.7% to −2.7%) stay inside the 5% band, so neither
channel is a channel effect in its own right. The bf16 pass tells the same
story with the expected offset (GeoTransolver-volume inflated 20–23%, ISLA
4–8%, as @sec-nb-fp32-instrument found).

**What it means.** The preregistration's fourth outcome: the ν_t gap is not
in the query-side inputs at this width and depth. The instrumental reading
is weakened rather than confirmed: a model given the sampling density
directly gained nothing on ν_t, so whatever GeoTransolver-volume's local
features supply, it is not recoverable from the density alone by this
architecture (with the usual caveat that an available input may go unused
in training). The physical reading is not supported either: relative
geometry and wall-distance differences of the sixteen nearest queries add
nothing. The remaining candidates for the gap are GeoTransolver-volume's
effective width of 448 and its multi-radius encoding taken together, and
the thread is deprioritized as the preregistration said it would be. The
channels stay in the code as flag-gated, default-off options with contract
tests; neither is adopted. Tech-tree change: QTDENS RUNNING → DONE (neither).

## 2026-09-10 — Verdict: measure weights off persists at the fixed angle (0.031 against 0.035 in float32, 17 of 18 geometries); third of six rungs {#sec-nb-now-single12-verdict}

The weights-off ladder (@sec-nb-wave3-prereg, bars from

## 2026-09-10 — Program redirect: accuracy by principled means only; measure weights off becomes an ablation and its reference-configuration rule is retired {#sec-nb-principle-redirect}

Peter's review of the weights-off ladder (@sec-nb-noweights-prereg,
@sec-nb-wave3-prereg) redirected the program. The physics does not depend
on how a surface was meshed, so a surrogate's answer must not either; a
model that gains accuracy by aggregating over whichever points the mesher
placed is reading the mesher's refinement pattern, a non-physical signal
that a uniformly generated point cloud or a different mesher would remove.
The goal is restated in @sec-principle: an accurate model reached by
physically principled means, because the principles are what generalize to
novel problems, while accuracy can be bought later with size.

Three consequences take effect now. First, the routing without measure
weights is an **ablation**, pricing the requirement (12% at 35 cases, 17%
at 4 geometries, 10.6% at the fixed angle, 2.9% on DrivAerML, in exchange
for a 19x loss of sampling-density robustness), and is never ISLA's
reference configuration; the preregistered rule that it would become the
reference at four or more of six rungs is retired, and every "best fair
configuration" phrase in the polished chapters now reads "weights-off
ablation (not adopted)". The remaining weights-off lanes keep running
because the price is worth knowing at every rung. Second, adoption of any
architecture change now requires a stated mechanism, a physical
justification and discretization-invariance tests before in-distribution
accuracy is even consulted. Third, the mechanism question behind the
weights-off gain stays open and is worth answering for its own sake:
whether the in-distribution price is estimator variance (the log-area term
spans orders of magnitude on a high-lift wing and concentrates each slice's
mass on a few large cells) or the loss of the density signal. The
discriminating experiment, sampling cells with probability proportional to
area and aggregating with uniform weights (an unbiased estimate of the
surface integral with the smooth attention of the weights-off model), is a
candidate for preregistration; it would be adopted only if it recovers
density robustness as well as accuracy.

## 2026-09-10 — Audit of the program's architecture changes against the principle: one shortcut (weights off), two channels retired in principle, one configuration question (constant gauge), baselines fail the invariance test {#sec-nb-principle-audit}

Each change to ISLA made or evaluated in this program, graded on the three
questions of @sec-principle (mechanism; physical soundness; discretization
invariance), with the standing decision.

| change | mechanism | physically principled? | discretization test | decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| measure-weighted routing (`use_measure_weights`) | slice aggregate = integral over the surface measure | yes: quadrature | 1.20x under 10:1 bias with the similarity gauge | keep; requirement |
| measure weights off | aggregate = mean over sampled points; reads mesher density or reduces estimator variance (open) | no | 19x under 10:1 bias | **ablation only; never adopted** |
| similarity gauge (scale-normalized geometry, reference length as input) | scale equivariance with absolute size re-entered explicitly | yes | 1.20x under bias | keep; **should be the reference configuration** (see below) |
| constant gauge (configuration behind every accuracy number) | fixed length scale | yes in mechanism | **13–14.5x under bias**, worse than GeoTransolver's 3.6x | fails the test; proposal: move the reference to the similarity gauge at its 8% in-distribution cost |
| unit-direction freestream (all architectures) | dimensionless drive input | yes; discards speed magnitude, so a Reynolds-dependent dataset needs Re as a physical scalar input | n/a | keep; note the Re caveat |
| second-moment channel (`second_moment_features`) | per-slice covariance of point positions under the routing weights (measure-weighted) | yes: geometric invariant of the slice | inherits the routing's measure | keep as option (free on DrivAerML) |
| query tokens + signed distance (interior) | SDF is a physical geometric field | yes | query-count contract exact after `query_mass="source_total"` | keep |
| query mass = source total (QMASS repair) | query weight tied to the source measure, not the query count | yes: removes a query-discretization dependence | exact (roundoff) | keep |
| local surface features (patch integrals at three radii) | measure-weighted integrals in gauge-normalized units | yes if the radii scale with the reference length (they are applied after the gauge) | inherits the routing's measure | keep as option; verify the radius units in the constant gauge |
| query-density scalar, query-neighbour channel (QTDENS) | read the interior sample density / neighbour layout | **no**: discretization features | not tested; falsified on accuracy anyway | **retired in principle** |
| anchor top-k sparse routing | approximation of the full routing | neutral (exact at k = N) | neutral | not adopted (not worth it) |
| fast point-softmax kernel | summation order | neutral | neutral (float32 identical to 1e-6) | default |
| support tokens / passive readout (companion) | query-independent decode | yes | exact query independence | keep as option |
| raw-coordinate channel, raw seeds | break or bypass the invariants | no | n/a | ablations only |
| learned virtual tokens with learned log-weight | virtual routing targets | neutral | neutral | keep |
| **baselines**: GeoTransolver's radius ball queries; GeoTransolver-volume's local features over interior samples | aggregate over neighbouring sampled points | read sample density | 9.5x (GeoTransolver), 3.9x (Transolver) under 10:1 bias | state beside every accuracy comparison |

Two findings change practice. The reference ISLA configuration behind the
accuracy results is the constant gauge, which fails the discretization test
by a wide margin; under the principle the similarity gauge, which passes it
at an 8% in-distribution cost at 35 cases, is the configuration the program
should stand on, and that switch is proposed for Peter's decision rather
than made here. And the baselines' density dependence, measured but
reported as a side column, becomes a first-class axis: an accuracy lead that
disappears under resampling is a lead over this mesher, not over the
problem. Everything else in the table is principled or already an
ablation.

**Redirect (2026-09-10, program-wide, binding).** The program's goal is an
accurate model reached by physically principled means, because those are
what generalize to novel problems; accuracy can be bought later with size,
generalization cannot. For this study: width and token scaling are capacity
and stand; the weights-off arms are ablations, never references; and the
512 × 80,000-cell arm of every architecture, and each reference arm, is
additionally evaluated on the program's sampling-density probe (DrivAerML
10:1 biased density against a uniform control, float32), so that the cost
frontier of bar 4 is stated with each configuration's discretization
invariance beside its accuracy. An architecture change is adopted only if
its physical rationale is stated and it passes such invariance tests;
in-distribution accuracy alone never justifies it.

## 2026-09-10 — Preregistered: BENCH, the consistency benchmark (evaluation only): three samplers × five counts on every reference checkpoint {#sec-nb-bench-prereg}

The principle of @sec-principle asks that a surrogate converge to a single
field under refinement of the sampling and to the same field under two
samplings of the same surface. No number in the book measures that
directly; the density-robustness column (10:1 front/back bias at 10,000
cells, @sec-robustness-density) measures one distribution shift at one
count. This benchmark measures the property itself, for all three
architectures, at no training cost.

**Instrument.** Every validation surface (48 DrivAerML cars; the 180
35-case and 18 fixed-angle HiLiftAeroML validation cases) is sampled from a
320,000-cell pool by three samplers, at n ∈ {2,500, 5,000, 10,000, 20,000,
40,000} cells: `unif`, uniform over cells (the training convention, which
inherits the mesher's refinement pattern); `area`, independent inclusion
with probability proportional to cell area (what a uniform point-cloud
generator would produce; a new `weight_mode="area"` of the recipe's Poisson
sampler); `biased`, the existing 10:1 front/back Poisson bias. All three
fold exact Horvitz–Thompson weights into the measure, so a measure-consistent
model sees the same integral under each. Float32 inference, each
checkpoint under its own training snapshot (legacy ISLA checkpoints load
only under `code`; an identical error from two checkpoints is a load
failure, never a value). Arms: ISLA constant gauge (iw_mt2_lr1e3,
lad_hl_mt2_super_scarce, mech_hl_mt2_single_aoa_12), ISLA similarity gauge
(iw_mt2_gauge; a35_hl_mt2_gauge), the weights-off ablation (now_*),
unit-drive GeoTransolver (uw_gt_unit_lr1e3, udrv_hl_gt_*) and unit-drive
Transolver (uw_transolver_unit_lr3e3, udrv_hl_transolver_*), two seeds each.

**Readouts and bars (pressure rel-L2, seed means).** D_area(n) =
err(area, n) ÷ err(unif, n) − 1 and D_biased(n) likewise, headline at n =
40,000: |D| ≤ 3% is *consistent across sampling distributions*, |D| ≥ 10%
*reads the sampling distribution*, between inconclusive. Convergence:
err(unif, n) and err(area, n) against n, the ratio err(2,500) ÷ err(40,000),
monotonicity within the two-seed spread, and the fine-mesh gap |err(area,
40k) − err(unif, 40k)|. Paired per-case counts with sign tests.

**Predictions.** ISLA with measure weights, either gauge: |D_area| ≤ 3% at
every count on both datasets; the similarity gauge has D_biased ≤ 30% at
every count; the constant gauge fails D_biased (12x at 10,000 is known).
Whether the constant gauge is also count-dependent is open: a 28x reading of
the reference at 40,000 cells reported during the scaling study carries the
signature of an unloaded checkpoint (1.567, the seeded-init error) and is
being rerun under the training snapshot, so this benchmark's same-snapshot
refinement curve is the deciding measurement; the prediction is that the
constant gauge passes refinement (its measure weights are exact) and fails
only the distribution shift. GeoTransolver and Transolver: |D_area| ≥ 10% on
HiLiftAeroML, whose multi-element meshes are strongly refined in the gaps,
and smaller on DrivAerML; D_biased ≥ 200% (9.5x and 3.9x known at 10,000).
The weights-off ablation fails D_area on HiLiftAeroML. A result where the
baselines pass D_area on both datasets would mean the mesher's refinement
pattern is not what they read, and the density-bias failure is a different
mechanism (extrapolation in local point density rather than a learned
prior); that reading would be recorded as such.

reducer results/consistency_bench/reduce_consistency_bench.py; cluster
$T/bench/, $T/bench_evals/, recipe copy $T/recipe_bench.

## 2026-09-10 — Preregistered: MW, measure-weighted slice pooling for GeoTransolver and Transolver (the principled steel-man) {#sec-nb-mw-prereg}

Both baselines pool points into slices with a token-count-normalized
softmax (physics_attention.py: slice weights summed over tokens and
divided out), so every sampled point counts equally and the slice
aggregate is a mean over the mesher's sample rather than an integral over
the surface. On the surface recipe GeoTransolver's radius ball queries are
off (`include_local_features=false`), so this pooling is its only point
aggregation; the same routine serves Transolver and GeoTransolver's GALE
blocks. The principled repair is the one ISLA carries: weight each point's
contribution by its quadrature measure, slice_s = Σ_i m_i a_is f_i ÷ Σ_i
m_i a_is, with m_i the cell area times the Horvitz–Thompson weight,
normalized per sample to mean one so the existing floor keeps its meaning.
Flag `measure_weighted_slices` (default off, bitwise-unchanged), forward
argument `measure_weights` fed from the same tensor ISLA consumes. Contract
tests: uniform weights reproduce the unweighted model; duplicating every
token at half measure leaves the output unchanged in float64 (the test the
unweighted model must fail).

**Question.** Is the baselines' accuracy lead over ISLA carried by reading
the sampling distribution, and does giving them measure semantics remove
their density-bias failure? **Lanes** (unit drive, frozen protocol,
snapshot code_mw): HiLift 35 cases, GeoTransolver 3e-3 and Transolver 3e-3,
seeds 42/43/44; DrivAerML 435 cars, GeoTransolver 1e-3 and Transolver
3e-3, seeds 42/43. Float32 evaluation on the arm's own split plus the
10:1 density probe and the BENCH samplers.

**Bars (float32 pressure rel-L2).** HiLift 35: references GeoTransolver
0.1102, Transolver 0.1142, ISLA 0.1377. *Lead survives* if the weighted
baseline is ≤ 0.131 (5% ahead of ISLA); *lead was the density read* if ≥
0.1336 (within 3% of ISLA or behind); between inconclusive. DrivAerML:
references 0.0503 / 0.0517 / 0.0558; *survives* ≤ 0.0530; *was the read* ≥
0.0541. Density: biased ÷ uniform ≤ 1.5 *measure-consistent* (the
similarity-gauge ISLA is 1.21); ≥ 3 *fails*. **Predictions.** The lead
survives on DrivAerML (near-uniform meshes; the read has little to carry)
and shrinks on HiLift; the density factor falls below 1.5 for both. If the
lead survives on both datasets with the factor below 1.5, the baselines'
advantage is inductive bias and the book says so.

## 2026-09-10 — Preregistered: WAVE-4, the similarity-gauge ISLA on every HiLiftAeroML rung, toward moving the reference configuration {#sec-nb-wave4-prereg}

ISLA's reference configuration behind every accuracy number is the constant
gauge (a fixed reference length of 8.0 in nondimensional coordinates), which
degrades 12x under the 10:1 density bias. The similarity gauge (centroid and
reference length from the measure-weighted point set) degrades 1.21x under
the bias at an 8% in-distribution cost at 35 cases and a 10% cost on
DrivAerML (0.0616 against 0.0558). Under @sec-principle the configuration
that passes the consistency tests is the one the program should stand on.
It exists at 35 HiLift cases and on DrivAerML; this wave trains it on the
six other rungs (210 cases, 1,260 cases, 4 and 21 training geometries,
fixed angle, deflection; two seeds) plus a third seed at 35 cases, thirteen
lanes, snapshot code (reference kernel, same as the constant-gauge lanes),
`+model.similarity_gauge=true` the only change. Launcher
highlift/hl_wave4_aga.sbatch, lane table wave4_lanes.tsv, run ids
w4_hl_mt2_gauge_<split>_seed<seed>.

**Readouts.** Float32 pressure rel-L2 per rung against the constant-gauge
ISLA lanes and the unit-drive baselines; the BENCH samplers at 40,000 cells
on the 35-case and fixed-angle checkpoints. **Bars.** The gauge's
in-distribution cost per rung: ≤ 5% "cheap", 5–15% "the known price",
> 15% "expensive at this rung" (stated per rung; the 35-case value is 8%).
**Decision rule.** The reference configuration moves to the similarity
gauge if it passes the BENCH consistency bars where the constant gauge
fails them, regardless of the in-distribution price; the price is then
stated beside every number, and the constant-gauge results are kept as the
prior configuration's record. If the similarity gauge fails the BENCH bars
too, the switch is not made and the failure becomes the next mechanism
question.

*Amended 2026-09-10 (@sec-nb-gauge-lr-confound):* the "10% cost on
DrivAerML" quoted above compares the similarity gauge trained at learning
rate 3e-3 with the constant gauge trained at 1e-3; at matched rate the two
are at parity, so the DrivAerML price of the gauge is not established and
the per-rung bars apply to the HiLift lanes, which are rate-matched. The
centering probe (@sec-nb-center-probe-verdict) adds a second candidate
reference, constant length with measure-weighted centering; the switch is
decided between the two once the four centering lanes and this wave read
out.

## 2026-09-10 — Preregistered: XFAM, why ISLA's DrivAerML representation transfers to a new vehicle family worse than GeoTransolver's {#sec-nb-xfam-prereg}

Zero-shot on the SHIFT-SUV fastback family (99 cases, float32, under
snapshot code) the reference ISLA scores 0.788 against the unit-drive
GeoTransolver's 0.612; fine-tuned on 20 fastback cases both start 1.6–2.5x
better than random and end 6% (ISLA) and 31% (GeoTransolver) better than
training from scratch (#sec-nb-campc-t3-verdict and its addendum). The
question is which ISLA ingredient carries the deficit. Rival hypotheses,
each with a discriminating arm evaluated zero-shot on the fastback in
float32:

- **H1, absolute scale (constant gauge).** The similarity-gauge reference
  (iw_mt2_gauge_seed{42,43}); the transfer session is evaluating it.
- **H2, the slice bottleneck.** 256 anchors learned on one family's shape
  distribution. Arms: n_slices 128 and 512 at fixed everything else, two
  seeds each, DrivAerML 435, unit drive, snapshot code (run ids
  xf_dr_mt2_s128_seed{42,43}, xf_dr_mt2_s512_seed{42,43}); the existing
  v5a4 (2,560 query-independent anchors) is a two-factor variant and is
  reported but not used to decide.
- **H3, drive-relative invariants coupling geometry to the freestream.**
  Arm: seed_mode=raw (raw [r, n, d] seeds, GeoTransolver-style inputs) on
  DrivAerML, two seeds (xf_dr_mt2_rawseed_seed{42,43}).
- **H4, measure weights.** The weights-off ablation (now_mt2_lr1e3); being
  evaluated by the transfer session.
- **H5, optimization rather than representation.** Decided by the existing
  first-batch decomposition: both models start well and diverge during
  adaptation, so H5 predicts no single-ingredient arm moves the zero-shot
  number.

**Bars (zero-shot fastback pressure rel-L2; reference ISLA 0.788, unit
GeoTransolver 0.612).** An arm *carries the deficit* if it scores ≤ 0.70
(halfway to GeoTransolver); *contributes* if 0.70–0.76; *does not* if ≥
0.76 (within seed spread; the two reference seeds are 0.782 and 0.794).
In-family DrivAerML error is reported beside each arm so a transfer gain
bought with in-family loss is visible. **Prediction.** H1 contributes (the
fastback cars differ in size from DrivAerML) but does not carry; H2 and H3
do not; the deficit is distributed, consistent with H5, in which case the
follow-up is a training-diversity study rather than an architecture change,
matching @sec-principle. Artifact: results/xfam_zeroshot_2026-09-10.json.

## 2026-09-10 — Preregistered: MIX, training across meshing conventions (uniform-over-cells and area-proportional samplings of the same surfaces) {#sec-nb-mix-prereg}

The long-run advantage of a measure-consistent surrogate is that it can be
trained on data from several meshers and deployed on another, because its
aggregate is an integral over the surface rather than a mean over the
sample. This study tests that claim in its cleanest form, with the physics
held fixed: the same DrivAerML training cases are presented under two
meshing conventions, the native cell-uniform sampling (`unif`, 10,000
cells; what every checkpoint in the book saw) and the area-proportional
sampling of the same cells (`area`, expected 10,000 cells; the convention a
uniform point-cloud generator or a different mesher would produce), using
the `weight_mode="area"` Poisson sampler of @sec-nb-bench-prereg with exact
Horvitz–Thompson weights. Three training conditions per architecture:
`unif` only (the existing reference lanes), `area` only, and `mixed`
(both conventions as two datasets through the recipe's `extra_datasets`
multi-dataset path, each case seen under both). Architectures: ISLA with
the similarity gauge, unit-drive GeoTransolver (1e-3), unit-drive
Transolver (3e-3); two seeds; 500 epochs; float32 evaluation on the 48
validation cars under both conventions.

**Readouts (pressure rel-L2).** For each architecture: the *swap penalty*
S = err(train unif, eval area) ÷ err(train unif, eval unif) and its mirror;
the *mixing cost* C = err(mixed, eval unif) ÷ err(train unif, eval unif)
and err(mixed, eval area) ÷ err(train area, eval area). **Bars.** S ≤ 1.03
*convention-independent*; S ≥ 1.10 *pays for the swap*; C ≤ 1.03 *mixes
for free*; C ≥ 1.10 *pays for mixing*. **Predictions.** The
similarity-gauge ISLA is convention-independent and mixes for free (S and
C within 3%). GeoTransolver and Transolver pay for the swap in at least one
direction (S ≥ 1.10) and pay for mixing (C ≥ 1.05), because their slice
pooling reads the sampling density; if the measure-weighted baselines of
@sec-nb-mw-prereg are trained by then, they enter as a fourth and fifth
architecture with the prediction that the penalty disappears. A result
where the baselines are convention-independent here would mean DrivAerML's
meshes are too uniform for the convention to matter, and the study moves to
HiLiftAeroML, whose gap refinement makes the two conventions differ by
orders of magnitude in local density. Lanes: 2 conventions × 3
architectures × 2 seeds = 12 new DrivAerML lanes (the unif-only condition
exists), snapshot `code` for the baselines and ISLA, recipe copy
recipe_bench; run ids mix_dr_<arch>_<area|mixed>_seed<seed>. Artifact:
results/mix_conventions_2026-09-10.json.

## 2026-09-10 — Verdict, centering probe: the constant gauge's density collapse is the unweighted centroid (12.1x → 1.12x with measure-weighted centering, no retraining) {#sec-nb-center-probe-verdict}

The main session derived from the model code that the only
sampling-distribution-dependent quantity in the reference ISLA's forward
pass is the plain mean used to center the point cloud in the constant-gauge
branch (#sec-nb-centroid-derivation): the routing softmax carries exact
log-weights, the slice moments are attention-normalized, and the reference
configuration has no local features, so under a 10:1 sampling bias toward
one half of the car the unweighted centroid moves by a large fraction of
the body length and every relational invariant leaves its trained range.
The prediction was that centering by the measure-weighted mean, the
similarity gauge's own centroid formula, would recover most of the 12x
collapse on the *trained* reference checkpoints without retraining, with a
falsifier at a residual ratio of 6x or more.

**Instrument.** A flag-gated `center_mode="measure"` in the constant-gauge
branch (default `"plain"`, bitwise unchanged; contracts: uniform weights
reproduce the plain mean to 10⁻¹², translation invariance in both modes, and
a 10:1 Horvitz–Thompson biased subsample of a 100,000-point cloud moves the
plain centroid by more than 0.3 cloud radii while the weighted centroid
stays within 0.15). The reference checkpoints iw_mt2_lr1e3_seed{42,43} and
the weights-off control now_mt2_lr1e3_seed42 were evaluated in float32 on
the 48 DrivAerML validation cars under the uniform and 10:1-biased probe
samplers in both centering modes (snapshot code_center, the training
snapshot plus the patch; every log shows the checkpoint loaded and the
plain cells reproduce campaign E to four digits).

| checkpoint | plain: uniform / biased / ratio | measure: uniform / biased / ratio | frame cost (measure ÷ plain, uniform) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA reference, seed 42 | 0.0566 / 0.7053 / 12.5x | 0.0950 / 0.1093 / **1.15x** | 1.68 |
| ISLA reference, seed 43 | 0.0550 / 0.6439 / 11.7x | 0.3295 / 0.3609 / **1.10x** | 5.99 |
| weights-off ablation, seed 42 | 0.0549 / 1.2670 / 23.1x | 0.0864 / 0.2784 / 3.22x | 1.57 |

**The centering is the collapse.** The reference's biased-over-uniform
ratio falls from 12.1x to 1.12x, inside the 1.5x recovery bar and far from
the 6x falsifier, on both seeds. The weights-off control falls from 23x to
3.2x: centering explains most of its collapse and the residual is the loss
of the Horvitz–Thompson weighting in the attention, the second prediction
of the derivation. What the probe does not establish is accuracy: on these
plain-trained checkpoints the frame swap is not neutral on the uniform draw
either (1.7x and 6.0x), because the area-weighted centroid differs from the
plain mean even under uniform-over-cells sampling, so a network trained in
one frame is being read in another. The four trained lanes with measure
centering (cg_dr_mt2_mcenter_seed{42,43} on DrivAerML,
cg_hl_mt2_mcenter_super_scarce_seed{42,43} at 35 HiLift cases; bars: density
ratio ≤ 1.5x and within 3% of the constant gauge's accuracy) decide whether
the reference configuration becomes "constant length with measure
centering" rather than the similarity gauge, which buys the same robustness
at an 8–10% price that may sit in its scale normalization rather than its
centering.

**The frame-swap cost is a finding in its own right.** A network trained in
the plain-mean frame loses 1.7x (seed 42) and 6.0x (seed 43) of its accuracy
on the *uniform* draw when read in the area-weighted frame, so the constant
gauge's accuracy rides on an exact frame to a degree that a centroid shift
of the size the area weighting produces on an ordinary sample is enough to
break it, and the two seeds differ fourfold in that sensitivity. The
displacement is small: on the uniform draw the area-weighted and plain
centroids differ by 0.031 nondimensional units, 0.16 m, **3.4% of the body
length** (48 cars: 2.4–4.7%), entirely from the area weighting (with bare
Horvitz–Thompson weights and no area the two coincide exactly). On the
biased draw the plain centroid moves 0.23 body lengths (1.08 m) from its
uniform position while the measure-weighted centroid moves 0.010 body
lengths (0.05 m; 0.2–2.8%), which is the whole mechanism in two numbers
(`$T/center/centroid_displacement.py`; table in the artifact).

**Preregistered bars for the four trained lanes** (before they read out):
joint pass if the density ratio is ≤ 1.5x *and* the float32 pressure
error is within 3% of the constant gauge's (0.0557 on DrivAerML; 0.138 at
35 HiLift cases), in which case "constant length + measure centering"
becomes the candidate reference configuration. Failure readings: invariant
but costly (ratio ≤ 1.5x, error > 3% worse) means the price of robustness
is the centering itself and the similarity gauge stands; accurate but not
invariant (within 3%, ratio > 1.5x) means a second sampling-dependent path
exists that the probe's frozen weights did not expose. Either way the mechanism question of @sec-nb-principle-audit
(why does the reference fail the density test) is answered: an unweighted
sample statistic in the frame construction, not the measure semantics of the
routing. Artifact: results/center_probe_2026-09-10.json (cluster
$T/center/probe_fp32, reducer center/reduce_center_probe.py).

## 2026-09-10 — Note: the similarity gauge's "10% price on DrivAerML" is a learning-rate confound; at matched rate the two gauges are at parity {#sec-nb-gauge-lr-confound}

While matching the MIX lanes to their reference checkpoints, the launch
record showed that the similarity-gauge DrivAerML reference
(iw_mt2_gauge_seed{42,43}) was trained at learning rate 3e-3 (the
instrument-wave launcher's default; `resolved_config.yaml` confirms it),
while the constant-gauge reference iw_mt2_lr1e3 was trained at 1e-3. The
book's statement that the gauge costs about 10% on DrivAerML (0.0616 against
0.0558 in float32) therefore compares two learning rates as well as two
gauges. The rate-matched comparison uses the constant-gauge checkpoint
trained at 3e-3, mt2_v3c_seed42, whose float32 error on the same 48 cars
under the same snapshot is 0.0620 (transfer session, snapshot `code`):
**0.0616 (gauge, two seeds 0.0623 / 0.0609) against 0.0620 (constant gauge,
one seed at 3e-3), parity within the seed spread.** The 35-case HiLift
comparison (1.08x, @sec-mechanism) is rate-matched and stands. Consequences:
the DrivAerML price of the similarity gauge is not established and is not
quoted; the accuracy × consistency matrix labels the gauge row with its
rate; a rate-matched pair at 1e-3 (similarity gauge, two seeds, DrivAerML)
is the missing measurement and is added to the WAVE-4 lane set as
w4_dr_mt2_gauge_lr1e3_seed{42,43}; and the MIX study's ISLA lanes run at
3e-3 to match their reference. This is also a reminder that the
recipe's per-architecture rate rule (@sec-protocol) must be checked per
lane record, not assumed.

## 2026-09-10 — Derivation: the constant gauge's sampling-density collapse is the unweighted centroid, not the length scale; prediction and bars for the reference-configuration switch {#sec-nb-centroid-derivation}

The density-robustness probe (@sec-robustness-density; `drivaer_probe_biased3`)
hands the model importance-corrected measure weights: `PoissonBiasedSubsampleMesh`
computes each cell's inclusion probability and composes 1/π into the measure,
so the sparse half of a 10:1 biased sample carries 10x weights and the total
measure is preserved within the Poisson count noise (about 3%). A
measure-consistent aggregate is therefore invariant under the probe up to
Monte Carlo variance, and the degradation ratios are properties of the
models, not of the quadrature. That makes the reference ISLA configuration's
12–14x collapse (against 1.2x for the similarity-gauge configuration) a
question about a specific path in the forward pass.

Reading the artifact rather than its description: in
`physicsnemo/experimental/nn/isla/model.py` the constant-gauge branch
centers the point cloud by the *plain mean of the sampled points* and
divides by the constant `reference_length`; the similarity-gauge branch
centers by the *measure-weighted mean* and scales by the weighted RMS
radius. The routing softmax adds the raw log-weights and is invariant to a
uniform rescale of the measure; the slice moments are attention-normalized;
the reference configuration (hidden 192, 12 layers, 256 slices,
reference length 8.0, no local features, no virtual tokens, no anchors)
has no other path in which the sampling distribution enters except through
the weights. **The only sampling-distribution-dependent quantity in the
reference forward pass is the unweighted centroid.** Under a 10:1 bias
toward one half of the car the plain mean moves by a large fraction of the
body length; every relative vector r shifts with it, and all eight
relational invariants (|r|/L, r̂·d, r̂·n, the anchor positions) leave the
range the model was trained on. On a uniform sample the plain and
measure-weighted centroids nearly coincide, which is why the same model is
accurate in distribution.

**Prediction (falsifiable).** (a) The trained reference checkpoint,
evaluated on the biased probe with measure-weighted centering in place of
the plain mean (a flag-gated option in the constant-gauge branch; the
default stays bitwise), recovers most of the collapse without retraining:
biased ÷ uniform falls from 12.1x to below 2x. Falsifier: it stays at or
above 6x. (b) A constant-length model *trained* with weighted centering
passes the probe at ≤ 1.5x while keeping the constant gauge's accuracy
within 3% at 35 HiLift cases and on DrivAerML, so the reference switch can
avoid the similarity gauge's 8% in-distribution cost if that cost sits in
the scale normalization rather than the centering. If (a) recovers but (b)
still costs about 8%, the price is the centering itself and the similarity
gauge stands as the reference. (a) is evaluation-only; (b) is two lanes per
dataset. Owner: the generalization-plan session (item 4), which holds the
model file for this work; this entry is the derivation it cites.

**Additions (same day, transfer session, checked against the snapshot that
trained the reference, `code/.../mt2/model.py`).** The plain-mean centroid
enters through the per-point seed features (r̂·d̂, r̂·n̂, |r|) and the anchor
directions; the relational terms r − z are translation-invariant and
unaffected. A residual second path remains even with weighted centering:
the attention is an unbiased Horvitz–Thompson weighting, but its effective
sample size in the sparse half falls about 10x under the bias, so a
variance term stays and is most of what the similarity-gauge arm's 1.21x
is; the falsifier (≥ 6x) sits safely above it. Test-design caveat: with
per-cell area weights the weighted centroid differs from the plain mean on
the *uniform* draw too, so the clean comparison is uniform-with-weighted
centering against biased-with-weighted centering, both under the new flag,
with the uniform-plain number reported beside as the cost of the frame
change. Second prediction, with a sign: the weights-off configuration's 19x
combines the same centroid shift with the loss of the Horvitz–Thompson
weighting in the attention (log-weights zero), so weighted centering alone
must *not* recover it; if it does, the derivation is wrong about where the
weights matter.

## 2026-09-10 — One guarded evaluation snapshot for the program: code_eval reproduces the original-snapshot float32 numbers per case for all three architectures {#sec-nb-code-eval-adopted}

The checkpoint-loading hazard (companion notebook, research/transfer_program, entry #sec-nb-snapshot-hazard; a renamed model
class made the loader skip the weights file and evaluate the seeded
initialization, silently) has two structural fixes in the repository: the
loader refuses to continue when a training checkpoint exists but the
model's weights file is missing, and it searches a model's declared legacy
class names first, so ISLA loads its MeshTransformer2 checkpoints with a
warning naming both files. The frozen training snapshots on the cluster
predate both fixes, so the scaling session exported an evaluation-only
snapshot, `code_eval`, from the fixed package (fast kernel opt-in, so the
default forward is bitwise the reference), and the question was whether it
computes the same function as the snapshots that trained the reported
checkpoints.

Identity check, float32, 48 DrivAerML validation cars, per-case pressure
relative L2 against the existing `code` evaluations: **ISLA
(iw_mt2_lr1e3_seed42) 0.056818 under both, mean relative difference 1.3 ×
10⁻⁶ and largest per-case difference 6 × 10⁻⁵ (summation-order roundoff;
loaded through the legacy-name path, one warning, no skip); GeoTransolver
(uw_gt_unit_lr1e3_seed42) 0.050043 and Transolver
(uw_transolver_unit_lr3e3_seed42) 0.05158 bitwise identical.** All float32
evaluation launchers now import `code_eval`; the training snapshots remain
for training and bfloat16 reproduction. An evaluation log containing
"skipping load" voids the run (CLAIMS).

## 2026-09-10 — Verdict: 21-geometry rung with the unit drive — GeoTransolver 0.92x of ISLA in float32, lower on 136 of 180 cases; the 1.4x "unseen-geometry advantage" was the input scale {#sec-nb-udrvl-geo210-verdict}

The unit-drive ladder (@sec-nb-udrvl-prereg) reruns GeoTransolver on each

receives, and nothing else changed. The 21-geometry rung trains on 210
cases from 21 wing geometries at all ten angles and validates on 180 cases
from 18 geometries never seen; against the physical-drive GeoTransolver
this rung had read as a 1.40x ISLA advantage on 172 of 180 cases. Two seeds

## 2026-09-10 — Kernel check for the 80,000-cell cliff: the middle-dimension softmax has no defect above 2^16 points on the GB300, so the cliff is not the bare kernel; the reference kernel is 1,000x less precise than the fast one in float32 {#sec-nb-softmax-dim1-test}

**Setting.** The ISLA scaling track found (@sec-nb-scale-isla-launch, count
curve) that both 10,000-cell-trained ISLA references improve monotonically
when evaluated at 20,000, 40,000 and 60,000 cells and then collapse to a
near-constant prediction at 80,000 (relative pressure error 0.81 and 0.89,
biased ÷ uniform ≈ 1). The one healthy 80,000-cell evaluation, the
80k-trained corner at 0.0427, ran on the fast point-softmax kernel, while
both references ran on the reference kernel, `torch.softmax(x, dim=1)` over
the middle (point) dimension of a (batch, points, slices) tensor. Since
65,536 = 2^16 lies between 60,000 and 80,000, a kernel defect above 2^16
points was a live hypothesis with a preregistered discriminator (the
track's 65k/70k brackets and an 80k kernel swap). This entry isolates the
kernel from the model with a one-minute micro-test so the brackets can be
read against a known kernel.

**Instrument.** One GB300, the evaluation snapshot's environment
(`code_eval`), random logits with standard deviation 3 in a (1, N, 256)
tensor for N in {40,000, 60,000, 65,535, 65,536, 65,537, 70,000, 80,000,
100,000}, float32 and bfloat16. Three quantities per N: the reference
kernel's and the fast kernel's (transpose, softmax over the last dimension,
transpose back) maximum absolute deviation from a float64 log-sum-exp
softmax, and each kernel's column sums over points (exactly one for a
correct softmax). The same check runs through the model's own
`_softmax_over_points` helper imported from `code_eval` at 60,000 and
80,000 points. Script and artifact:
results/scaling/softmax_dim1_test.py,
results/scaling/softmax_dim1_test_2026-09-10.json (job 700392).

**Result.** No cliff. In float32 the reference kernel deviates from exact
by 4.5e-5 to 1.2e-4 at *every* N, including 65,535 and 65,537, with column
sums between 1.00002 and 1.00021; the fast kernel deviates by 0.5e-7 to
2.3e-7 with column sums within 3.5e-7 of one. In bfloat16 the two kernels
give identical outputs at every N (0.9e-3 to 1.9e-3 from exact, the
bfloat16 rounding of the weights themselves). Through the model's helper at
80,000 points: reference 1.0e-4, fast 1.4e-7.

| N (points) | reference kernel, float32, max |Δ| | fast kernel, float32, max |Δ| | bfloat16 (both kernels) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 40,000 | 9.7e-5 | 1.3e-7 | 1.3e-3 |
| 60,000 | 7.1e-5 | 1.3e-7 | 1.9e-3 |
| 65,535 | 1.0e-4 | 1.4e-7 | 1.8e-3 |
| 65,536 | 4.5e-5 | 1.0e-7 | 1.8e-3 |
| 65,537 | 1.2e-4 | 2.3e-7 | 1.8e-3 |
| 70,000 | 6.7e-5 | 0.5e-7 | 1.0e-3 |
| 80,000 | 6.9e-5 | 0.9e-7 | 0.9e-3 |
| 100,000 | 8.7e-5 | 0.9e-7 | 1.1e-3 |

**Two readings.** (1) A bare-kernel defect above 2^16 points is excluded on
this device and PyTorch build: if the 65k/70k brackets are healthy and
80,000 still collapses, the cause sits elsewhere in the 80,000-cell
evaluation path of the *reference* checkpoints, something the corner's
evaluation did not share (snapshot, which kernel a legacy checkpoint
instantiates under `code_eval` — checkpoints written before the
`fast_point_softmax` argument existed take the current default unless the
loader pins it, so the kernel actually used must be read from the
evaluation log, not the lane table — or a per-count datapipe behaviour).
The track's kernel-swap probe remains the decisive discriminator and its
readout supersedes this entry's bracketing of causes. (2) A finding in its
own right: the middle-dimension softmax kernel is about a thousand times
less precise than the last-dimension kernel in float32 (1e-4 against 1e-7
on weights of order 0.5), the same at every N. The model's docstring
statement that the two kernels "agree to 1e-6 in float32" describes the
model-level comparison, where the logits' range is narrower than this
test's; on raw softmax weights the reference kernel carries a 1e-4 floor.
No verdict changes: every float32 headline in the book compares
checkpoints evaluated under one kernel each, and the 1e-4 floor is three
orders below the smallest difference the book reports. It is recorded here
because it is the kind of instrument property that would otherwise be
rediscovered.

**What this does not say.** Nothing about why the references collapse at
80,000 cells (open, the track's probes are running), and nothing about
training numerics: the reference kernel's 1e-4 floor was present in every
pre-2026-09-10 ISLA training run and is part of what the kernel-neutrality
control (@sec-nb-fast-kernel-default) measured as +1.8%.

**Resolution (same day).** The ISLA track's brackets closed the question
within two hours: under the program's evaluation snapshot `code_eval` the
10k-trained constant-gauge reference scores 0.0545 / 0.0530 / 0.0529 /
0.0529 / 0.0529 / 0.0528 at 20k / 40k / 60k / 65k / 70k / 80k cells, and
the 80k-trained corner scores its native 0.0427 at 80,000 cells on the
reference kernel as well. The two collapsed readings (0.814 / 0.892, job
700105) were evaluations of the same checkpoints on the same datasets under
the *legacy* `code` snapshot, which that launcher still imported for the
`iw_*` lanes at the time; they are struck in the track's entry as a defect
of the legacy snapshot's evaluation path at 80,000 cells (mechanism not
pursued: nothing evaluates under `code` any more, and the program-wide
rule since @sec-nb-code-eval-adopted is that every evaluation imports
`code_eval`). Reading (1) above therefore resolves to "the snapshot", and
the kernel attribution the hypothesis rested on was itself wrong: infer.py
instantiates the model from the recipe's model config, not from the
checkpoint's stored arguments, so every `code_eval` evaluation of a legacy
checkpoint runs the class default, the fast kernel; a checkpoint written
before the `fast_point_softmax` argument existed carries no record of its
training kernel. Evaluation logs now state the instantiated kernel, and the
lane tables' "numerics" column is a training label only. Reading (2), the
1e-4 float32 floor of the middle-dimension kernel, stands and is noted in
the helper's docstring.

## 2026-09-10 — SCALE synthesis, DrivAerML half: at 512 wide × 80,000 cells all three architectures land within 3% in float32 (GeoTransolver 0.0419, ISLA 0.0428 constant gauge / 0.0431 similarity gauge, Transolver 0.0431); scale narrows the baselines' lead by 0.08 in ratio, past the 0.05 bar; only ISLA's similarity-gauge corner is density-invariant (1.09x against 10.5x / 16.6x / 14.9x in the sample frame) at equal cost; the baselines reach that error at 0.3–0.6x ISLA's GPU-hours {#sec-nb-scale-drivaer-synthesis}

**Setting.** The scaling study (@sec-nb-scale-prereg) asked whether the
accuracy ordering the book reports at the frozen protocol's operating point
(about 9M parameters, 10,000 sampled surface cells per case) survives when
the three architectures are given the memory a 288 GB device offers. Three
tracks ran the arms (ISLA @sec-nb-scale-isla-launch, GeoTransolver
@sec-nb-scale-gt-verdict, Transolver @sec-nb-scale-transolver-verdict) on
DrivAerML at full data (435 cars, 48 validation cars), two seeds per arm,
the frozen 500-epoch protocol, the unit-drive freestream for the baselines,
and the corner 512 wide × 80,000 cells added for all three after ISLA's
pilot. This entry answers bars 3 and 4 of the preregistration (does scale
change the ordering; which architecture reaches a given error cheapest) and
adds the program redirect's requirement (@sec-nb-principle-audit): every
accuracy is reported beside its discretization-invariance reading, the
biased ÷ uniform pressure error under a 10:1 sampling-density bias. The
HiLift half is training under the reader contention described in
@sec-nb-hilift-io (25–68 epochs per day; one to two weeks at full protocol,
no epoch cut) and is not in this entry.

**Instrument.** Float32 inference is the headline for every number
(@sec-nb-fp32-instrument); bfloat16 is shown where the offset matters. All
evaluations of the corner arms and every density probe ran under the
program-wide guarded evaluation snapshot `code_eval`
(@sec-nb-code-eval-adopted); the earlier single-knob arms were evaluated
under their training snapshots and their float32 numbers were reproduced per
case by `code_eval` in the identity check. Every reducer refuses a run whose
evaluation log shows a skipped checkpoint load, an unnamed snapshot, or a
tripped inference summary guard (zero hits across the 44 GeoTransolver,
44 Transolver and all ISLA logs). Pressure relative L2, 48 cars, two-seed
means; seed spreads are under 1.5% on every accuracy row.

**The corner, 512 wide × 80,000 cells** (GPU-hours = 500 epochs × 108 steps
× median step × 4 GPUs; ISLA's rows state the routing measure weights and
the point-softmax kernel because both are configuration choices; the
baselines have neither knob):

| Transolver, unit drive | 512 wide | 23.9M | **0.0431** (0.0434 / 0.0428) | 0.833 | 0.0471 | 0.111 s | 27.6 GB | 6.6 | **14.9** (13.0 / 16.8) (pool 4.6: 4.2 / 5.1) | 13.7 (12.2 / 15.3) (pool 4.4) |
| ISLA, similarity gauge, measure weights on, fast kernel (`g512x80k`) | 512 wide, exact recompute | 60.2M | **0.0431** (0.0425 / 0.0437) | 0.700 (÷ gauge reference 0.0616); 0.774 ÷ constant-gauge reference | 0.0441 | 0.281 s | 22.9 GB | 20.2 | **1.09** (pool 1.08) | 1.56 (pool 1.53) |

GeoTransolver's seed-42 probe is the resubmitted copy (the first output was
displaced by another track's directory move and restored bit-identical;
both copies read 0.2738 biased / 0.0419 uniform). Cost columns are each
track's reduction (results/scaling/*_scale_reduction_2026-09-09.json).

**The references and the single-knob arms, for the same readers** (the
reference row of each architecture is the book's operating point; ratios are
÷ that architecture's own reference):

| ISLA, constant gauge, weights on | 192 × 10k, 8.9M | 0.0557 | 0.0577 | 0.273 s | 9.8 GB | 21.3 | **12.0** (pool 12.1: 12.5 / 11.7) | 0.926 | 0.912 | 0.883 (reference kernel, 1.28 s/step) | 0.840 (fast kernel) | 0.811 (reference kernel) |
| Transolver, unit drive, lr 3e-3 | 256 × 10k, 6.0M | 0.0517 | 0.0563 | 0.097 s | 3.2 GB | 5.8 | **11.6** (10.2 / 13.0) (pool 3.9: 2.2 / 5.5) | 0.928 | 0.913 | 0.932 | 0.921 | 0.880 |
