Width scales for all three (bar 1: 9–11% at 512 wide, met everywhere;
ISLA's 384 → 512 step is 1.6%, inside seed spread, so its width gain is
flattening by 512) and all three are resolution-limited (bar 2: 8% for the
baselines at 80,000 cells, 16% for ISLA, with 12% already at 40,000). The
two knobs compose nearly independently for every architecture (ISLA:
0.912 × 0.840 = 0.766 against the measured corner 0.768), so the corner is
each architecture's best DrivAerML configuration in this study, with no
sign of saturation at 80,000 cells. Two ISLA cost caveats from its track:
the two 40k arms trained on the reference kernel before the fast kernel was
adopted (1.28 s per step, 86 GPU-hours against 21–23 for every other arm),
and peak memory is not comparable across training snapshots (the reference
reads 9.8 GB under the legacy snapshot and the same configuration 3.9 GB
under `code_perf`), so memory is ordered within a snapshot only.

**Bar 3, does scale change the ordering.** With r = baseline ÷ ISLA at the
matched arm, in float32:

| pair | r at the reference (10k, reference widths) | r at the corner (512 × 80k) | shift | bar (±0.05) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | 0.0503 / 0.0557 = **0.903** | 0.0419 / 0.0428 = **0.979** | **+0.076** | scale favours ISLA |
| Transolver ÷ ISLA | 0.0517 / 0.0557 = **0.928** | 0.0431 / 0.0428 = **1.007** | **+0.079** | scale favours ISLA |

Both shifts exceed the preregistered 0.05 bar in ISLA's favour: at the
operating point the unit-drive baselines lead ISLA by 7–10% on DrivAerML
(@sec-nb-fp32-drivaer-regrade); at the corner the three architectures sit
within 3% of each other, GeoTransolver 2% ahead of ISLA and Transolver 1%
behind. The mechanism is the token knob, not width: ISLA gains 16% from
80,000 cells at the reference width against 8% for either baseline, while
the width gains are the same 9–11% for all three. The book's DrivAerML
accuracy ordering is therefore an ordering at 9M parameters and 10,000
cells, and the recommendation section gains the scale clause the
preregistration anticipated. Under bfloat16 the same corner would read
ISLA 0.0441 ahead of GeoTransolver 0.0460 and Transolver 0.0471: the
instrument, not the models, decides a 4–6% "lead" there, which is why the
float32 rule exists.

**The redirect's reading: accuracy × invariance.** None of the three
constant-configuration corners is discretization-invariant. ISLA's
constant-gauge corner degrades 16.6x under the 10:1 bias at its own
80,000 cells (10.8x at 10,000), the same class as its reference's 12.0x, and
its 80k-cell token gain does not transfer down: queried at 10,000 cells it
scores 0.0663, worse than the 10k-trained reference's 0.0558 there. The
baselines, probed in the sample frame (the frame a biased mesher delivers;
see the frame-convention paragraph below), degrade 10–15x at the corner as
at their references (GeoTransolver 10.5x at 80k and 10.2x at 10k against
12.1x for its reference; Transolver 14.9x and 13.7x against 11.6x), and both
corners pay +8% when queried at 10,000 cells (GeoTransolver's uniform error
rises 8%; Transolver 0.0465 against 0.0430). Scale buys
capacity and resolution for every architecture and invariance for none of
the constant configurations. **The similarity-gauge corner is the exception
and the study's principled result.** ISLA with the similarity gauge (the
program's one nearly density-invariant configuration: 1.21x at 10k and
1.01x at 80k for its reference, with monotone count generalization
0.0616 → 0.0574 from 10k to 80k cells) scaled to 512 wide × 80,000 cells
scores **0.0431 in float32 (seeds 0.0425 / 0.0437) with biased ÷ uniform
1.08 at its own 80,000 cells**, meeting both preregistered bars (≤ 0.0449,
within 5% of the constant-gauge corner, and ≤ 1.5; neither failure bar
fires) at the same cost as the constant-gauge corner (60.2M parameters,
22.9 against 22.8 GB, 0.281 against 0.285 s, 20.2 against 22.5 GPU-hours).
The gauge's 10% accuracy cost at the reference (0.0616 against 0.0558)
vanishes at the corner (+0.7%), so the choice between the constant and the
similarity gauge is no longer accuracy against invariance: at scale it is
invariance for free. The one property the gauge does not buy is
down-transfer: queried at 10,000 cells the gauge corner scores 0.0727
(ratio 1.53), 1.69x its native error, as the constant corner's 0.0663 is
1.55x its own; a model trained at 80,000 cells should be deployed at
80,000. The frontier statement the redirect asks for now reads: *at
512 × 80k on DrivAerML, GeoTransolver, ISLA and Transolver reach
0.042–0.043 in float32; GeoTransolver and Transolver do so at density
sensitivities of 10.5x and 14.9x, ISLA's constant gauge at 16.6x, and ISLA's
similarity gauge at 1.09x (sample frame; pool frame 4.2x / 4.6x / 16.7x /
1.08x) — the only configuration in the study whose
accuracy would survive a mesher that put ten times the cells on the front
of the car.* The 16.7x is not an ISLA property but a constant-gauge
property (@sec-nb-centroid-derivation); the redirect makes the constant
gauge inadmissible as a scaling result on its own, so ISLA's constant-gauge
row in the bar-3 table is a capacity measurement, and the gauge row is the
configuration the program can adopt. Bar 3 read with the gauge row instead
gives r = 0.0419 / 0.0431 = 0.972 (GeoTransolver) and 0.0431 / 0.0431 =
1.000 (Transolver), shifts +0.069 and +0.072 from the constant-gauge
reference, still past the 0.05 bar.

**Frame convention (added the same day, when the sample-frame probes
landed).** The density probes the tracks first ran (`drivaer_probe_{biased3,unif2}{,_80k}`)
centre the mesh by the plain mean of the reader's uniform pool *before* the
biased draw, so GeoTransolver and Transolver, which consume absolute centred
coordinates, were handed an unbiased frame the pipeline computed for them;
a biased mesher would deliver the mean of the cells it produced. ISLA
centres inside the model on the sample it receives, so its frame was
already the sample's. The generalization session found this and the
program adopted the sample-frame probes
(`drivaer_probe_{biased3,unif2}_sf{,_80k}`: the same files with the
CenterMesh block moved to directly after the sampler, in both columns;
generator transfer/make_postcenter_probes.py) as canonical; every ratio in
this entry is now stated as *sample frame (pool frame)*, sample frame the
headline. All three tracks re-probed their corners and references under
`code_eval`, two seeds, float32, with each reference as the launcher
control. The controls reproduce the generalization session's readings
(GeoTransolver reference 12.0 / 11.9 / 12.5, Transolver 10.2 / 13.0; ISLA's
11.99 and 1.21 equal to its pool-frame values within 2%, and a direct
translation test on the gauge corner checkpoint moves its output by
5–6 × 10⁻⁶ relative, results/scaling/isla_translation_check_2026-09-10.json).
What changes: the pool-frame probe had under-reported the baselines'
sensitivity by 2.5–3x (Transolver 3.9x → 11.6x at the reference;
GeoTransolver 9.5x → 12.1x) and had manufactured the GeoTransolver corner's
apparent improvement and seed asymmetry (6.5 / 1.9 → 9.3 / 11.6); in the
honest frame no baseline configuration in the study is less sensitive than
its reference, Transolver's corner is more so (14.9x against 11.6x), and
the uniform errors are unchanged by the frame (the uniform draw's mean is
the pool's). ISLA's rows move by under 2%. The redirect's reading above is
unchanged in kind and sharpened in degree: at 512 × 80k the similarity
gauge's 1.09x stands against 10.5x, 14.9x and 16.6x.

**Bar 4, the cost frontier.** Read at matched error rather than at the
endpoint: Transolver reaches 0.0431 for 6.6 GPU-hours (27.6 GB),
GeoTransolver 0.0419 for 12.7 GPU-hours (41.5 GB), ISLA 0.0428 for 22.5
GPU-hours (22.8 GB, with the exact recompute). The baselines reach the
corner error at 0.3–0.6x of ISLA's GPU-hours because their attention runs
over 256 slices and widening is nearly free in step time (GeoTransolver
0.15 → 0.211 s, Transolver 0.097 → 0.111 s from reference to corner), while
ISLA's per-point relational geometry makes its step 0.285 s at the corner
(1.3x GeoTransolver, 2.6x Transolver) even with the fast point-softmax
kernel, which is what made the 80k arms affordable at all (3.4 s per step
before it, @sec-nb-isla-perf-verdict). ISLA is the most memory-efficient of
the three at the corner (22.8 against 27.6 and 41.5 GB) because of the exact
activation recompute, and every corner uses under 15% of the device; the
binding cost on this hardware is step time, not memory, for all three. At
matched GPU-hours the frontier reads: for about 6–7 GPU-hours Transolver
gives 0.043; for 13 GeoTransolver gives 0.042; ISLA's cheapest
configuration in the study, the reference at 21 GPU-hours, gives 0.056, and
its corner at 22.5 gives 0.043. The cost-matched comparison of
@sec-nb-cost-matched-fast (ISLA 1.09x GeoTransolver's step at the operating
point) holds at 10,000 cells; at 80,000 the gap widens to 1.3x because the
relational-geometry cost is per point.

**The bfloat16 offset, one sentence.** Across the six DrivAerML reference
and corner rows the bfloat16 − float32 offset is an additive floor per
architecture rather than a percentage: GeoTransolver +0.0041 to +0.0053,
Transolver +0.0040 to +0.0046, ISLA +0.0013 to +0.0020 (per-case up to
+0.011 for the baselines), so as errors fall from 0.05 to 0.042 the relative
offset grows from 8–10% to 10–11% for the baselines and stays 3–4% for
ISLA; every close comparison in this study moved toward the baselines when
read in float32, and the corner ordering inverted (above).

**Struck and pending, stated.** Two 80,000-cell readings of the 10k-trained
ISLA references (0.814 / 0.892) produced under the legacy `code` snapshot are
struck: the same checkpoints on the same datasets read 0.0528 and 0.0574
under `code_eval`, the saved predictions of the struck runs are identical to
the healthy ones per car, and the defect was in the legacy snapshot's
metric aggregation (@sec-nb-softmax-dim1-test; the ISLA track's entry lists
every 80k reading with its snapshot and job). No number in any chapter was
produced by an evaluation under a pre-`code_eval` snapshot at 65,536 points
or more. The structural guards now in force: every evaluation imports
`code_eval` and writes its snapshot beside its output; reducers refuse
unnamed snapshots and skipped loads; infer.py refuses to write a summary
outside the range of its own per-sample values (commit f9330f317). Every DrivAerML
arm of the preregistration is now in this entry; pending: the sample-frame
density probes at the corner (below, when they land) and the HiLift half. Every ISLA evaluation and probe
now names its snapshot per instrument (reference `code`; width arms
`code_isla5`; token, constant-gauge corner and kernel control `code_perf`;
gauge corner `code_eval`) and no evaluation tripped the summary guard.

**What this does not say.** Nothing about HiLift (1,260 cases; training,
I/O-bound, weeks), where the 35-case and 210-case rungs have ISLA ahead and
the scale question is different; nothing about learning-rate retuning
(every arm at the protocol rate, none diverged); nothing about the interior.
The bar-3 result says the DrivAerML surface ordering at 9M parameters and
10,000 cells does not persist at 60M parameters and 80,000 cells; it does
not say ISLA leads there (it does not, by 2% against GeoTransolver in
float32), and under the redirect the constant-gauge corner that produced
ISLA's row is a measurement of capacity, not a configuration the program
adopts.

## 2026-09-10 — Verdict: 210-case rung with the unit drive — GeoTransolver 0.83x of ISLA (lower on 162 of 180), Transolver 0.91x; the 2.2x was the input scale; prediction held at five of six rungs {#sec-nb-udrvl-210-verdict}

The unit-drive ladder (@sec-nb-udrvl-prereg) reran GeoTransolver and
Transolver on the 210-case HiLiftAeroML rung (a random 210 of the 1,260
cases, about 126 geometries) with the freestream as a unit direction and
nothing else changed. Against the physical-drive GeoTransolver this rung had
read as a 2.2x ISLA advantage on 177 of 180 cases, the ladder's second
headline after the 2.8x at 35 cases. Two seeds of each unit-drive baseline
were evaluated in float32 (training and evaluation snapshots matched, zero
skipped loads) with the bfloat16 pass alongside; the ISLA reference is the
three-seed float32 mean. Artifact: `results/udrvl_210_reduction_2026-09-10.json`.

**GeoTransolver fed the unit direction scores 0.0533 (seeds 0.0532 /
0.0535) against ISLA's 0.0643 (0.0617 / 0.0661 / 0.0652): 0.83x, lower on
162 of 180 validation cases (median GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA 0.775), inside the
preregistered "baseline ahead" band (0.0579 or below).** Transolver at its
better rate scores 0.0582 on both seeds (the seed means coincide to four
digits; the per-case values differ by up to 115%, and the checkpoints and
seeds were verified distinct), 0.91x of ISLA and lower on 145 of 180 cases,
between parity and "baseline ahead" on the baseline's side. Velocity and
wall shear follow (GeoTransolver 0.080 / 0.123, Transolver 0.085 / 0.130,
ISLA 0.094 / 0.144). The physical-drive GeoTransolver on the same cases
scores 0.141 on three seeds (0.159 / 0.157 / 0.107; 2.2x behind ISLA by the
mean, 2.7x by the median case) and is 3.4x worse than its unit-drive self on
178 of 180 cases; the physical-drive Transolver, 0.077, is 1.5x worse than
its unit-drive self on 170 of 180. Bfloat16 gives the same ordering (0.0542,
0.0588, 0.0648).

The prediction written before any rerun, that the unit-drive baselines match
or beat ISLA at every rung, has now held at five of six: 35 cases (0.80–0.90x
by the best rates), 210 cases (0.83x / 0.91x), 4 geometries (0.76x / 0.77x),
21 geometries (0.92x, between) and the fixed angle (0.78x / 0.86x). The
1,260-case rerun (epochs 80–90 of 500, I/O-throttled) is the last; the
physical-drive result there was parity, so the prediction is that it lands
at parity or on the baselines' side. The 2.2x at 210 cases is retired as an
ISLA advantage; chapter 5, chapter 12, the index and the status chapter are
updated. What the ladder now says about ISLA is unchanged in kind from the
35-case verdict: the small-data advantage on HiLiftAeroML was the baselines'
input scale, and with it removed ISLA is 1.1–1.3x behind at every small-data
rung on this dataset.

## 2026-09-10 — Preregistered: QCOUNT, query-count augmentation for the interior query-token configuration (does training over a range of request sizes remove the count dependence?) {#sec-nb-qcount-prereg}

*Setting.* ISLA's interior configuration admits the interior query points as
interacting tokens (@sec-interior-query-tokens). Its prediction at a point
therefore depends on how many other points are requested with it: on the
trained reference checkpoint the sentinel pressure error is 0.114 when a
point is predicted alone, 0.080 with 2,000 companions, 0.055 at the training
request of 10,000 and 0.054 at 40,000 (float32, four cars,
@sec-nb-qmass-verdict). The passive alternative, which is exactly
count-independent, was tested at matched depth and inputs and lost 1.43x on
pressure and 2.41x on eddy viscosity (companion D1, @sec-interior-query-independence),
so the interacting queries are the configuration and the count dependence
is what remains to remove. Under @sec-principle the target is consistency:
the same field at every request size, with error that falls, not rises,
as the count grows.

*Mechanism (why this should work).* The dependence is a training-distribution
artifact, not an architectural necessity: every interior lane has trained
at exactly 10,000 queries, so the routing weights, the query mass and the
query-query interactions have only ever been seen at one count. Training
with the count drawn per sample over a range asks the same network to
produce the same field at 2,000 and at 20,000 requests, which the
measure-consistent routing (Horvitz–Thompson weights on the surface, query
mass a fraction of the surface measure) already permits; what the
augmentation supplies is the gradient signal that penalizes count-specific
solutions. It changes no input, adds no non-physical signal and leaves the
architecture unchanged; it is a statement about the training distribution
over discretizations, which is the principled lever for a consistency
property.

*Instrument.* `DomainMeshReader` gains `interior_n_points_range=(lo, hi)`:
the interior point count is drawn per sample, uniformly on the closed
integer range, from the sample's own generator (reproducible per epoch and
index), overriding the fixed count for the interior only; boundaries keep
their fixed sizes and the default `None` is bitwise the old behaviour
(reader tests, 33 passing). Arm: the reference query-token + signed-distance
configuration (hidden 192, 12 layers, 256 slices, similarity gauge; training
snapshot `code_isla2` plus this reader change, otherwise frozen protocol,
`dataloader.pin_memory=false`) trained on DrivAerML volume with
`interior_n_points_range=[2000, 20000]`, two seeds
(v0_isla_qtsdfval_qcount_seed{42,43}). Evaluation in float32 under the
guarded snapshot at three request sizes on all 48 validation cars: 2,000,
10,000 and 20,000 interior points per car. Controls: the reference
checkpoints (v0_isla_qtsdfval_seed{42,43}) evaluated at the same three
sizes (10,000 already: 0.0547 / 0.0796 / 0.1116 deduplicated two-seed means;
2,000 and 20,000 running now, jobs 702010 and 702011).

*Bars (readout units, float32, two-seed means, 48 cars).* (1) *Accuracy kept
at the training count:* pressure at 10,000 within 3% of the reference
(≤ 0.0563), otherwise "augmentation costs accuracy". (2) *Count dependence
removed:* pressure at 2,000 requests within 10% of the arm's own 10,000
value (the reference's 2,000-request penalty on all 48 cars, float32,
deduplicated two-seed means, is +38% on pressure, 0.0753 against 0.0547,
+59% on velocity, 0.1266 against 0.0796, and +49% on eddy viscosity, 0.1663
against 0.1116; at 20,000 requests the reference improves to 0.0531 / 0.0771
/ 0.1097, so it converges upward and fails only downward; control jobs
702010 / 702011, zero skipped loads);
"supported" if the 2,000-to-10,000 ratio is ≤ 1.10 for pressure and ≤ 1.15
for eddy viscosity, "falsified" if pressure ≥ 1.25 (no better than half the
reference's penalty), between otherwise. (3) *Consistency upward:* the
20,000-request error is at or below the 10,000 value for all three fields.
(4) *No regression against GeoTransolver-volume at the training count:*
pressure ratio ISLA ÷ GeoTransolver-volume stays within 0.03 of the
reference's 1.08. Falsifiers stated in advance: (2) failing means the count
dependence is not a training-distribution artifact and the interacting
decode carries an intrinsic request-size dependence, which would make
query-count consistency an architectural question after all; (1) failing
means the price of consistency is paid in accuracy and the trade is
reported, not adopted. Cost is recorded (mean count 11,000, about 1.1x the
reference step). Owner: this session; launch after the two control jobs
report.
not say ISLA leads there (it does not, by 2–3% against GeoTransolver in
float32 in either gauge), and under the redirect the constant-gauge corner
is a measurement of capacity while the similarity-gauge corner is the
configuration the program can adopt: matched accuracy, an order of
magnitude less density sensitivity than every other corner (1.09x against
10–17x in the sample frame), equal cost.
Whether the same holds on HiLift, where the two datasets' surface
resolutions and case counts differ, is the pending half.

## 2026-09-10 — Verdict, measure-centering lanes: free and density-robust on DrivAerML (0.98x, 1.17x under the bias), a 10% price at 35 HiLift cases; the frame estimate, not the length scale, is what heterogeneous meshes charge for {#sec-nb-center-lanes-verdict}

The centering probe (@sec-nb-center-probe-verdict) showed that the
constant-gauge ISLA's density collapse is its plain-mean centroid; the
open question was whether a model *trained* with the measure-weighted
centroid keeps the constant gauge's accuracy. Four lanes answered it
(constant gauge, `center_mode="measure"`, unit drive, learning rate 1e-3,
500 epochs, snapshot code_center; float32 evaluation; bars preregistered in
the probe verdict as a joint pass of density ratio ≤ 1.5x and error within
3% of the constant gauge's 0.0557 on DrivAerML and 0.138 at 35 HiLift
cases). Artifact: results/center_lanes_2026-09-10.json.

| dataset | measure-centered ISLA (seeds) | constant gauge, plain centering | ratio | density 10:1 (seeds) | similarity gauge, rate-matched |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DrivAerML, 48 cars | 0.0550 / 0.0545 → **0.0548** | 0.0557 | **0.98x** | 1.17x / 1.18x → **1.17x** | 0.0616 at 3e-3 (parity with 0.0620 at 3e-3) |
| HiLift, 35 cases (180 val) | 0.1519 / 0.1521 → **0.1520** | 0.1377 | **1.10x** | not measured | 0.1482 (three seeds), 1.076x |

**DrivAerML: joint pass.** Measure centering costs nothing (1.6% better,
inside seed spread) and takes the density-bias ratio from 12.1x to 1.17x,
inside the 1.5x bar; the residual 1.17x is the estimator-variance floor the
similarity gauge also shows (1.21x). On this dataset "constant length plus
measure-weighted centering" is a configuration that is both as accurate as
the reference and consistent under resampling, and it does it without the
similarity gauge's scale normalization.

**HiLift 35 cases: the accuracy bar fails** (0.1520 against 0.1377, a 10.4%
price), landing in the preregistered "invariant but costly" reading: the
price of robustness here is the frame estimate itself. The similarity
gauge, which also builds its frame from the measure-weighted sample, pays
7.6% on the same rung (three seeds, rate-matched), and the two prices
coincide within the seed spread, so the common cause is the frame
statistic, not the length scale. The mechanism is the one already named
for the weights-off ablation: on a multi-element wing the cell areas span
orders of magnitude, so a centroid (or RMS extent) estimated from 10,000
area-weighted samples is a high-variance statistic, and a frame that
jitters between draws of the same surface is a handicap in training; the
plain mean of a uniform-over-cells draw is a low-variance statistic that
happens to read the mesher. DrivAerML's near-uniform meshes make the two
estimates nearly equivalent, which is why the price vanishes there.

**What follows.** The principled repair does not need the sample at all: the
frame (centroid, extent) of a surface is a property of the geometry and can
be computed once from the full mesh at data-preparation time and passed as
global data, exactly as the freestream direction is; it is then
sampling-independent by construction, has no estimator variance, and costs
nothing at inference. That configuration ("full-geometry frame", FRAME-FULL)
is the next preregistration: prediction, constant-gauge accuracy recovered
at 35 HiLift cases (within 3% of 0.1377) with the density ratio ≤ 1.2x on
DrivAerML. The reference-configuration decision therefore reads: on
DrivAerML the measure-centered constant gauge is adopted as the reference
(accuracy kept, consistency gained). On HiLiftAeroML the constant gauge is
the configuration behind every number to date and fails the consistency
test; keeping it as the flagship because it is 10% more accurate in
distribution would be the trade @sec-principle rules out, so the HiLift
reference is *under decision*, not settled: the chapters present the two
consistent configurations (measure centering at a 10% price, the similarity
gauge at 7.6%) beside the constant gauge's numbers, and the FRAME-FULL
prediction. A dataset-dependent reference would itself be a warning sign,
which is a second reason to let FRAME-FULL decide. The HiLift density ratio
of the measure-centered checkpoints is being measured under the BENCH
samplers and will complete their row (the density column above is empty for
that reason, not because the test was skipped). *Ruling applied
2026-09-11:* at equal accuracy the frame-free construction is preferred
(@sec-nb-relframe-verdict), so the measure-centred frame is not adopted;
the reference is RELFRAME with the total-measure scale unless FRAME-FULL
passes its joint bar.

## 2026-09-10 — Preregistered: FRAME-FULL, the frame from the full geometry as global data (sampling-independent by construction) {#sec-nb-frame-full-prereg}

The centering results (@sec-nb-center-probe-verdict,
@sec-nb-center-lanes-verdict) leave one mechanism standing for why the
sampling-consistent frames cost 7–10% at 35 HiLift cases and nothing on
DrivAerML: on a multi-element wing the cell areas span orders of magnitude,
so a centroid or an RMS extent estimated from 10,000 area-weighted samples
is a high-variance statistic, and a frame that jitters between draws of
the same surface handicaps training; the plain mean of a uniform-over-cells
draw is low-variance and reads the mesher. The frame of a surface is a
property of the geometry, not of the sample. FRAME-FULL computes the
area-weighted centroid and RMS radius once per case from the full surface
mesh, at data-preparation time, and passes them as global data (as the
freestream direction is), so the frame is sampling-independent by
construction, has no estimator variance, and costs nothing at inference. It
is well posed under @sec-principle: the quantities are available for any
geometry at inference and depend on no sampling.

**Arms** (ISLA, unit drive, learning rate 1e-3, 500 epochs, snapshot
code_frame): A, "center only": constant reference length 8.0 with the
full-geometry centroid (`center_mode="global"`); B, "center and scale": the
full-geometry centroid and RMS radius (the similarity gauge's statistics,
computed exactly). Datasets: DrivAerML 435 cars and HiLift 35 cases, two
seeds each, eight lanes (ff_dr_mt2_{center,frame}_seed{42,43},
ff_hl_mt2_{center,frame}_super_scarce_seed{42,43}). Frame table:
$T/frame/frame_table_{drivaer,hilift}.json, verified on two cars against an
independent full-mesh computation to 10⁻⁶.

**Bars (float32 pressure rel-L2; joint pass).** Accuracy within 3% of the
constant gauge's plain-centred reference (0.1377 at 35 HiLift cases, three
seeds; 0.0557 on DrivAerML) *and* density biased ÷ uniform ≤ 1.2x on
DrivAerML (the measure-centred lanes' 1.17x is the sample-estimate floor
this should undercut; the BENCH samplers supply the HiLift consistency
readout). **Predictions.** Arm A passes jointly on both datasets, recovering
the 10% lost by sample-based measure centering at 35 HiLift cases; arm B
passes as well, and if B is within seed spread of A the similarity gauge's
7.6% price is confirmed as frame-estimate variance rather than scale
normalization. **Falsifier.** If arm A still pays ≥ 7% at 35 HiLift cases,
the variance hypothesis is wrong and the price of a sampling-consistent
frame lies in the centring itself (a plain-mean frame carries information
about the mesher that helps in distribution), which would be recorded as a
genuine in-distribution advantage of a non-physical input and would not
change the decision against it. **Decision.** If A passes jointly on both
datasets it becomes the reference configuration on both, ending the
dataset-dependent reference; if only DrivAerML passes, the HiLift reference
stays under decision with the FRAME-FULL numbers stated. Artifact:
results/frame_full_2026-09-10.json.

## 2026-09-10 — Verdict, BENCH: no configuration is consistent across sampling distributions at 10,000 cells; only the similarity-gauge ISLA converges toward consistency (D_area +122% → +18%, D_biased +20% → +2.8% from 10k to 40k), every other arm is flat {#sec-nb-bench-verdict}

The consistency benchmark of @sec-nb-bench-prereg evaluated every reference
checkpoint of the three architectures on the same validation surfaces under
three samplers (uniform over cells, area-proportional, 10:1 front/back
biased; exact Horvitz–Thompson weights in every case) at 2,500 to 40,000
cells, in float32 under each checkpoint's training snapshot (390 lanes, 0
loader warnings, seeds distinct in every cell, the 10,000-cell uniform
numbers reproduce campaign E to 0.0004). Artifact:
results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json; reducer beside
it; cluster $T/bench, $T/bench_evals, recipe copy $T/recipe_bench.

**Pressure rel-L2, seed means, at 10,000 and 40,000 cells** (unif / area /
biased):

| arm | dataset | 10k: unif / area / biased | 40k: unif / area / biased | D_area 40k | D_biased 40k |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA constant gauge | DrivAerML | 0.0561 / 0.1832 / 0.6740 | 0.0530 / 0.1008 / 0.6693 | +90% | +1162% |
| ISLA similarity gauge | DrivAerML | 0.0618 / 0.1370 / 0.0742 | 0.0579 / 0.0683 / 0.0595 | +18% | **+2.8%** |
| ISLA weights off (ablation) | DrivAerML | 0.0544 / 0.7319 / 1.044 | 0.0518 / 0.6602 / 1.033 | +1176% | +1895% |
| GeoTransolver, unit drive | DrivAerML | 0.0509 / 0.3623 / 0.4957 | 0.0506 / 0.3351 / 0.5210 | +562% | +930% |
| Transolver, unit drive | DrivAerML | 0.0520 / 0.1869 / 0.2014 | 0.0518 / 0.1617 / 0.1995 | +213% | +286% |
| ISLA constant gauge | HiLift 35 | 0.1390 / 0.4317 / 0.4576 | 0.1362 / 0.3938 / 0.4599 | +189% | +238% |
| ISLA weights off (ablation) | HiLift 35 | 0.1226 / 0.9254 / 0.5914 | 0.1201 / 0.9145 / 0.5933 | +662% | +394% |
| GeoTransolver, unit drive | HiLift 35 | 0.1104 / 0.2931 / 0.3615 | 0.1100 / 0.2716 / 0.3628 | +147% | +230% |
| Transolver, unit drive | HiLift 35 | 0.1148 / 0.3607 / 0.4078 | 0.1145 / 0.3212 / 0.4090 | +181% | +257% |
| ISLA constant gauge | HiLift fixed angle | 0.0361 / 0.4850 / 0.5018 | 0.0338 / 0.3583 / 0.5020 | +960% | +1385% |
| ISLA weights off (ablation) | HiLift fixed angle | 0.0313 / 1.293 / 0.5282 | 0.0293 / 1.236 / 0.5210 | +4119% | +1679% |
| GeoTransolver, unit drive | HiLift fixed angle | 0.0274 / 0.4084 / 0.3322 | 0.0270 / 0.2734 / 0.3310 | +912% | +1125% |
| Transolver, unit drive | HiLift fixed angle | 0.0308 / 0.3031 / 0.2669 | 0.0304 / 0.3343 / 0.2643 | +1001% | +770% |

**Against the bars.** At the headline count of 40,000 cells only one cell
of the whole benchmark passes the ≤ 3% consistency bar: the similarity-gauge
ISLA under the 10:1 bias on DrivAerML (+2.8%, worse than uniform on 36 of 48
cars). Every other arm × sampler reads the sampling distribution by the ≥
10% bar, most by an order of magnitude. Prediction 1 (measure-weighted ISLA
consistent under the area sampler at every count) is falsified for both
gauges on both datasets; prediction 4 held in direction (the baselines read
the distribution everywhere) but not in the DrivAerML-versus-HiLift
contrast; prediction 5 (weights-off fails) held on both datasets.

**What the area sampler is.** The area-proportional draw is a far harsher
change of discretization than the 10:1 bias. DrivAerML and HiLiftAeroML
cell areas span three to four decades, so an inclusion probability
proportional to area gives Horvitz–Thompson weights whose max/min ratio is
about 1,000–3,000 on the cars and 8,000–37,000 on the wings (the bias
probe's is exactly 10), and at 40,000 cells the largest 21% (cars) to 33%
(wings) of kept cells sit at the clamp. The refined regions, mirrors, slat
and flap gaps, are nearly unsampled: an area-uniform point cloud of 10,000
points does not resolve them at all. The measure-consistent estimator is
unbiased under this draw, but its variance is enormous where the geometry
is fine, so the failure of the measure-weighted ISLA arms under `area` at
fixed count is an information and variance statement, not a shortcut
statement: no method with a 10,000-point budget can read a slat gap from a
sample that contains none of it. That is why Peter's definition of the
property matters (@sec-principle): consistency is convergence in the
fine-mesh limit, and the discriminating readout is the *trend* with count.

**Convergence.** Under uniform sampling every arm's error falls
monotonically with count (ISLA 1.50x from 2,500 to 40,000 cells on
DrivAerML, GeoTransolver 1.17x, Transolver 1.12x; the measure-weighted
integral estimator gains most from refinement). Under the area sampler
only the two measure-weighted ISLA arms on DrivAerML converge toward the
uniform answer: the constant gauge's area error falls 2.63x from 2,500 to
40,000 cells and the similarity gauge's 3.50x (fine-mesh gaps 0.048 and
0.010), while every other area curve is flat (ratios 0.9–1.6): the
baselines' and the weights-off ablation's answers under a different
sampling distribution do not approach their uniform-sampling answers as the
sample grows, which is the operational meaning of "reads the sampling
distribution". The similarity gauge on DrivAerML is the one configuration
on a path to consistency: D_area +226% → +18% and D_biased +20% → +2.8% from
10k to 40k, with the curve still falling. The ordering by
sampling-distribution dependence on DrivAerML at 40k is clean: similarity
gauge (+18%) < constant gauge (+90%) < Transolver (+213%) < GeoTransolver
(+562%) < weights-off ablation (+1176%).

**HiLift.** No arm converges under the area sampler on either HiLift rung
within 40,000 cells (the constant-gauge ISLA's fixed-angle area error does
fall, 0.51 → 0.36, but from ten times its uniform error); the wings'
refinement spans more decades than the cars', so the fine-mesh limit is
further away than the benchmark's largest count. The similarity gauge and
the measure-centred checkpoints on the HiLift rungs are being added (24
lanes, job 703803, snapshot code_center for the latter) to complete the
HiLift picture.

**Reading for the program.** (1) The density-bias probe at 10,000 cells,
the number the book has been quoting, understates how far every
configuration is from consistency: the bias probe changes the distribution
by a factor of ten; a different mesher changes it by thousands. (2) The
similarity gauge is the only existing configuration that converges toward
the same field under both distribution changes, and it does so slowly; the
frame work (@sec-nb-center-lanes-verdict, RELFRAME) addresses the frame
part of the remaining dependence, while the variance of the
measure-weighted estimator under extreme weights is a second, separate
limit that a count budget alone cannot fix. (3) A "mesher-transfer" claim
for any of the three architectures at 10,000 cells would be false; the
honest statement is a convergence rate, and only ISLA with measure weights
has one. Chapter 6 gains the curves.


## 2026-09-10 — Peter's ruling on the frame, and RELFRAME preregistered: translation invariance from relative positions only, a length scale from the geometry's measure, no sample statistic anywhere {#sec-nb-relframe-prereg}

Peter ruled on the reference-configuration question raised by
@sec-nb-center-lanes-verdict: there will be no dataset-dependent reference
configuration, and centering by a sample statistic (plain or measure-weighted
mean) or scaling by one (RMS radius) injects the point distribution, a
non-physical input, into the model, so both are out. Translation invariance
is to come from relative positions alone, and the length scale from the
physics or from an integral property of the geometry. FRAME-FULL
(@sec-nb-frame-full-prereg) is kept as the *diagnostic* of the
variance mechanism, not as a candidate reference.

**Where the centroid enters ISLA.** In the constant-gauge forward pass the
center c enters exactly six scalars. Seed features per point (four):
|r| and log|r| (distance from the center; carry the point's position in the
body, front/rear/top/bottom, in a rotation-invariant way), r̂·d̂ (whether the
point lies upstream or downstream of the center along the freestream) and
r̂·n̂ (whether the surface faces toward or away from the center: convexity
sense). Relational invariants per point–anchor pair (two of eight): z_mag
(the anchor's radius from the center) and ẑ·d̂ (the anchor's upstream /
downstream position). The other six relational invariants (point–anchor
distance and its log, the unit relative vector dotted with the drive, the
point normal and the anchor normal, the point normal dotted with the anchor
normal) and both second-moment terms are anchor-relative and translation
invariant with no frame at all; the anchor's own orientation information
survives through m̂_s·d̂. **RELFRAME** drops the six center-dependent terms
(`frame_mode="relative"`: seeds reduce to n̂·d̂ plus the measure; the
relational set to its six frame-free members) and sets the length scale to
either the constant reference length (a stated problem parameter) or the
square root of the total surface measure Σ w_i (an integral of the geometry,
sampling-consistent under the Horvitz–Thompson weights; `scale_mode`).

**Arms** (ISLA, unit drive, lr 1e-3, 500 epochs): relative + reference
length, and relative + √(total measure); DrivAerML 435 cars and HiLift 35
cases; two seeds; eight lanes (rf_dr_mt2_{ref,meas}_seed{42,43},
rf_hl_mt2_{ref,meas}_super_scarce_seed{42,43}). **Bars (joint, float32).**
Within 3% of the constant gauge's 0.1377 / 0.0557 and biased ÷ uniform ≤
1.2x on DrivAerML; the BENCH samplers on the trained checkpoints give the
area-sampler trend. **Prediction.** The A35B ablation showed the invariant
seed set is not load-bearing (raw seeds 0.99x), so dropping the centroid
seeds costs little: constant-gauge accuracy at ≤ 1.2x on both datasets, which
would make RELFRAME the single flagship. **Falsifier.** A price ≥ 7% at 35
HiLift cases with the density bar passed means the center-dependent terms
carry in-distribution information the anchor-relative set does not (which
of the six is answered by adding them back one at a time), and the price is
then a stated cost of the principle, not a reason to reinstate a sample
statistic. The reference stays "under decision" in every chapter until
RELFRAME reads out.
**Ruling received after this entry (2026-09-10, Peter via the main
session).** Three decisions bear on the reading above. (1) The HiLift reader
contention is accepted for now and fixed later, so the HiLift half keeps its
full protocol and its one-to-two-week projection. (2) No dataset-dependent
reference configurations: one flagship configuration across datasets, so
the gauge corner's DrivAerML result cannot by itself make the similarity
gauge the reference while it costs 8% at 35 HiLift cases; that decision
belongs to the centering lanes and to Peter. (3) Sample-statistic frames,
which is what the similarity gauge is (centering by the sampled cloud's
measure-weighted mean, scaling by its measure-weighted RMS radius), are to
be replaced by translation invariance from relative positions with a length
scale taken from an integral of the geometry (for example the total surface
measure) or a stated physical reference length. The gauge corner's numbers
stand as measured, and the mechanism they demonstrate stands: at scale, a
frame that does not read the sampling density costs nothing in accuracy and
removes the density sensitivity. What changes is the configuration that
carries that mechanism into the program: when the relative-position arm
exists, the same 512 × 80,000 corner is run with it and its row replaces the
gauge row as the adoptable one; until then "the configuration the program
can adopt" above should be read as "the frame class the program adopts,
measured here through its similarity-gauge instance".

## 2026-09-10 — Verdict, MW: with measure-weighted slice pooling the baselines keep their lead over ISLA (0.0498 / 0.0522 on DrivAerML, 0.1173 / 0.1217 at 35 HiLift cases) and become the most density-consistent configurations measured (1.02x under the 10:1 bias) {#sec-nb-mw-verdict}

The MW study (@sec-nb-mw-prereg) gave GeoTransolver and Transolver the same
quadrature measure ISLA carries, in their slice softmax (each point's
contribution weighted by its cell area times the Horvitz–Thompson weight;
flag `measure_weighted_slices`, contract-tested: duplicating half the tokens
at half measure leaves the output unchanged, which the unweighted models
fail). Ten lanes trained under the frozen protocol with the unit drive
(HiLift 35 cases, three seeds each at 3e-3; DrivAerML 435 cars, two seeds,
GeoTransolver 1e-3 and Transolver 3e-3), snapshot code_mw; float32
evaluation and the 10:1 density probe under the same snapshot (no loader
warnings). Artifact: `results/mw_w4dr_xfam_reduction_2026-09-10.json` (block `mw`).

| architecture, measure-weighted pooling | DrivAerML (seeds → mean) | unweighted reference | density 10:1 (seeds → mean) | HiLift 35 (seeds → mean) | unweighted reference | ÷ ISLA 0.1377 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver, unit drive | 0.0492 / 0.0505 → **0.0498** | 0.0503 | 1.03 / 1.01 → **1.02x** | 0.1127 / 0.1220 / 0.1173 → **0.1173** | 0.1102 | 0.85x |
| Transolver, unit drive | 0.0519 / 0.0525 → **0.0522** | 0.0517 | 1.02 / 1.03 → **1.025x** | 0.1211 / 0.1207 / 0.1234 → **0.1217** | 0.1142 | 0.88x |

**Against the bars.** DrivAerML: both weighted baselines are within seed
spread of their unweighted selves and far below the 0.0530 "lead survives"
bar; the density factor falls from 9.5x (GeoTransolver) and 3.9x
(Transolver) to 1.02x, under the 1.5x "measure-consistent" bar and below
every ISLA configuration measured (similarity gauge 1.21x, measure centering
1.17x). HiLift 35: the weighted baselines pay 6.5% (GeoTransolver 0.1102 →
0.1173) and 6.6% (Transolver 0.1142 → 0.1217) but stay under the 0.131 bar,
so the lead over ISLA survives at 0.85x and 0.88x; part of the baselines'
HiLift lead was the density read (about a third of it), most was not. The
prediction held on both counts: on the cars the read had nothing to carry;
on the wings it carried some.

**Reading, stated plainly.** Unweighted slice pooling is a removable hack.
With measure semantics GeoTransolver and Transolver keep their
in-distribution lead over ISLA on both datasets (free on the cars, 6.5% on
the wings) and become the most density-consistent configurations measured,
so at the reference size ISLA's contracts buy neither accuracy nor
consistency; what ISLA retains is exact equivariance under arbitrary poses
(6–19%, @sec-pose-contract; companion #sec-nb-campb-verdict), the interior velocity and near-wall lead at
matched parameters (@sec-interior), and the memory footprint at scale.
Measure-weighted pooling is the recommended repair for the Transolver family:
a principled, general fix of exactly the kind this program should ship, and
it lands in the repository flag-gated and default-off with its contract
tests. Two qualifications belong beside that sentence. First, a structural asymmetry in the probe: the datapipe
centres every architecture's coordinates by the plain mean of the reader's
40,000-cell uniform pool (`CenterMesh`, before the biased second-stage draw),
so the baselines see an unbiased frame from the pipeline while ISLA
re-centres inside the model on the biased 10,000-cell sample; the baselines'
1.02x therefore measures the slice pooling with the frame held fixed, and the
pool-mean centring is itself a sample statistic of the kind Peter's ruling
removes from the flagship (@sec-nb-relframe-prereg). ISLA's residual 1.17–1.21x
is that in-model frame estimate, which RELFRAME removes; a like-for-like
probe with the pipeline's centring moved after the biased draw (the frame a
biased mesher would deliver) is being run on the weighted and unweighted
baselines so that both numbers sit side by side. Second, the HiLift
consistency of the weighted baselines is not yet measured (no HiLift density
probe; the BENCH samplers are being run on these checkpoints), and the
BENCH area sampler (@sec-nb-bench-verdict) is the harder test: whether the
weighted baselines converge under it, as the measure-weighted ISLA arms do
and the unweighted baselines do not, is the readout that decides whether
"measure semantics" has been transferred or only the bias probe passed.
Chapter 5's 35-case table and chapter 6's matrix gain these rows; the code
is flag-gated and default-off in the repository.

## 2026-09-10 — Verdict, XFAM: no single ISLA ingredient carries the cross-family deficit; anchors and seeds are null, the gauge points the wrong way at both rates, the deficit is distributed {#sec-nb-xfam-verdict}

The XFAM study (@sec-nb-xfam-prereg) trained the rival-hypothesis arms on
DrivAerML (435 cars, unit drive, lr 1e-3, three seeds each, snapshot code)
and evaluated them zero-shot on the 99 SHIFT-SUV fastback cases in float32
under the same snapshot (no loader warnings). Reference ISLA 0.788 (0.782 /
0.794), unit-drive GeoTransolver 0.612; bars: ≤ 0.70 carries the deficit,
0.70–0.76 contributes, ≥ 0.76 does not. Artifact `results/mw_w4dr_xfam_reduction_2026-09-10.json` (block
`xfam`) and the transfer session's variant evaluations
($T/transfer/fastback_zeroshot_fp32).

| hypothesis | arm | zero-shot fastback (seeds → mean) | in-family DrivAerML (mean) | reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H2 slice bottleneck | n_slices 128 | 0.827 / 1.084 / 1.034 → 0.98 | 0.0553 | worse; does not carry |
| H2 slice bottleneck | n_slices 512 | 0.829 / 0.779 / 1.001 → 0.87 | 0.0545 | worse; does not carry |
| H3 drive-relative invariants | raw seeds (seed_mode=raw) | 0.822 / 0.825 / 0.654 → 0.767 | 0.0534 | ≥ 0.76: does not carry (one seed at 0.65, spread 0.17) |
| H1 absolute scale | similarity gauge (lr 3e-3) | 1.038 / 0.851 → 0.945 | 0.0616 | wrong way |
| H1 absolute scale | similarity gauge (lr 1e-3, rate-matched) | 1.068 / 0.768 → 0.918 | 0.0543 | wrong way; seed spread 0.30, the widest measured |
| H4 measure weights | weights off | 0.802 / 0.811 → 0.806 | 0.0544 | null |
| (partial H2) | 2,560 query-independent anchors | 0.800 / 0.900 → 0.850 | — | worse; two-factor variant |

**No arm reaches the 0.70 bar, and no arm's seed mean falls below 0.76.** The
anchor count moves the zero-shot error the wrong way at both 128 and 512;
the raw seeds are within seed spread of the reference (and 4% better
in-family, consistent with A35B's finding that the invariant seed set is
not load-bearing); the gauge is worse; the measure weights are null. The
seed spreads on this readout are large (0.17–0.26 across three seeds for
the anchor arms), which the preregistration anticipated by requiring three
seeds and which itself says the zero-shot fastback number is dominated by
what the optimizer happens to find, not by the ingredient. The deficit is
therefore distributed, the H5 reading: ISLA's DrivAerML representation
transfers worse than GeoTransolver's for no single architectural reason
that these arms can name, and the campaign C closure (mixing cost grows
with foreign share for ISLA only; coverage of the sibling family, not a
family flag, is what transfers) points to training diversity as the lever.
The rate-matched gauge pair closes H1: 1.068 / 0.768 (mean 0.918), the
widest seed spread of any arm, so absolute scale is not the carrier either.
Follow-up under @sec-principle: no architecture change is proposed from
this study; the cross-family question moves to data (which families, how
many, mixed how) and to RELFRAME's zero-shot numbers once trained, since a
frame-free model is the first ISLA whose fastback error is not tied to a
DrivAerML-fitted centroid.

## 2026-09-10 — Addendum to the MW verdict: the weighted baselines' 1.02x was the pipeline's frame, not the pooling; with the frame taken from the biased sample they collapse 14–16x, worse than their unweighted twins {#sec-nb-mw-postcenter}

**With like-for-like frames every configuration that centres on a sample
statistic collapses 10–17x under the 10:1 bias (unweighted baselines
10–13x, measure-weighted baselines 14–16x, constant-gauge ISLA 12–17x), and
only the frames that do not read the sample survive (ISLA's similarity gauge
and measure-weighted centring at about 1.2x, RELFRAME by construction):
measure weighting repairs the aggregation, the frame is a separate defect,
and both must be fixed.** The MW verdict (@sec-nb-mw-verdict) flagged a
structural asymmetry in the density probe: the datapipe centres every architecture's coordinates by the
plain mean of the reader's 40,000-cell uniform pool before the 10:1 biased
draw, so GeoTransolver and Transolver, which consume absolute centred
coordinates, received an unbiased frame from the pipeline while ISLA
re-centres inside the model on the biased sample. The like-for-like probe
moves the centring after the sampler (the frame a biased mesher would
deliver; the biased draw itself splits on the median of centroid x and is
translation-invariant, so only the input frame changes), evaluated in
float32 at 10,000 cells on the weighted and unweighted baselines (no loader
warnings; $T/transfer/mw_postcenter_density.json; variants
recipe_mw/datasets/drivaer_probe_{unif2,biased3}_postcenter.yaml).

| run | frame from the pool (pre): unif / biased / factor | frame from the sample (post): unif / biased / factor |
|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver, measure-weighted, seed 42 | 0.0493 / 0.0508 / 1.03 | 0.0493 / 0.7024 / **14.3** |
| GeoTransolver, measure-weighted, seed 43 | 0.0506 / 0.0512 / 1.01 | 0.0506 / 0.7371 / **14.6** |
| Transolver, measure-weighted, seed 42 | 0.0519 / 0.0531 / 1.02 | 0.0517 / 0.8194 / **15.9** |
| Transolver, measure-weighted, seed 43 | 0.0524 / 0.0538 / 1.03 | 0.0526 / 0.8083 / **15.4** |
| GeoTransolver, unweighted, seed 42 | 0.0503 / 0.5919 / 11.8 | 0.0502 / 0.6027 / 12.0 |
| GeoTransolver, unweighted, seed 43 | 0.0510 / 0.4010 / 7.9 | 0.0506 / 0.6035 / 11.9 |
| Transolver, unweighted, seed 42 | 0.0515 / 0.1143 / 2.2 | 0.0518 / 0.5278 / 10.2 |
| Transolver, unweighted, seed 43 | 0.0519 / 0.2848 / 5.5 | 0.0517 / 0.6743 / 13.0 |

**The 1.02x was the frame.** With the centre estimated from the biased
sample the measure-weighted baselines degrade 14.4x (GeoTransolver) and
15.6x (Transolver), as much as or slightly more than their unweighted
twins (12.0x and 11.6x under the same frame). Measure weighting fixed the
*aggregation*, which is what the contract test checks, but both baselines
consume absolute centred coordinates as their positional input, and a plain
mean over a 10:1 front/back sample moves that frame by roughly a fifth of a
body length toward the dense half, an input-distribution shift that no
pooling rule can undo. The uniform-draw errors are unchanged pre and post
(the uniform sample's mean equals the pool's), so the accuracy half of the
MW verdict stands: the lead survives on both datasets. The consistency half
is retracted: the measure-weighted baselines are *not* the most
density-consistent configurations measured; under a like-for-like frame the
ordering under the 10:1 bias is ISLA similarity gauge 1.20–1.21x, ISLA with
measure-weighted centring 1.17x, then everything that centres on a plain
sample mean (ISLA constant gauge 12.1x, unweighted baselines 11.6–12.0x,
weighted baselines 14.4–15.6x), then the weights-off ablation (19x).

**What this means for the frame question.** The frame is the whole of the
density story at 10,000 cells, for every architecture: the baselines'
published density collapse (9.5x and 3.9x, @sec-robustness-density) was
measured with an unbiased frame handed to them by the pipeline and is
therefore an *under*-estimate of what a biased mesher would do to them
(12x); ISLA's constant-gauge collapse is the same mechanism inside the
model; ISLA's measure-weighted frames are the only ones that survive, at
the 1.2x variance floor of a frame estimated from a sample; and Peter's
ruling that the flagship carry no sample-statistic frame at all (RELFRAME,
@sec-nb-relframe-prereg) applies with equal force to the baselines, whose
raw-coordinate inputs need *some* frame: a measure-weighted baseline with a
relative-position encoding, or one fed the RELFRAME-style geometry-integral
scale, is the principled baseline this program has not yet built. The
matrix rows, chapter 6 and chapter 12 are corrected accordingly; the
"recommended repair" sentence narrows to "fixes the aggregation, not the
frame".

## 2026-09-10 — BENCH addendum: the measure-centred constant-gauge ISLA is the first configuration consistent across all three samplers (DrivAerML +3% / +3% at 40k; HiLift 35 cases −2% / +4% at 10k) {#sec-nb-bench-mcenter}

The four measure-centring checkpoints of @sec-nb-center-lanes-verdict were
run through the consistency benchmark's three samplers at 10,000 and 40,000
cells (snapshot code_center, float32, no loader warnings; artifact
results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_mcenter_2026-09-10.json).

| arm | 10k: unif / area / biased | 40k: unif / area / biased | D_area 10k → 40k | D_biased 10k → 40k |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA constant gauge, measure-weighted centring, DrivAerML | 0.0553 / 0.0650 / 0.0652 | 0.0523 / 0.0538 / 0.0537 | +18% → **+3%** | +18% → **+3%** |
| ISLA constant gauge, measure-weighted centring, HiLift 35 | 0.1553 / 0.1526 / 0.1611 | 0.1513 / 0.1509 / 0.1523 | **-2%** → **-0%** | **+4%** → **+1%** |

**Against the bars.** On DrivAerML both samplers pass the 3% consistency
bar at 40,000 cells (+3% / +3%), the first arm in the benchmark to do so
under the area sampler, converging from +18% at 10,000 cells. On the HiLift
35-case rung, where every other configuration reads the sampling
distribution by 150% to 4,000% (@sec-nb-bench-verdict), the measure-centred
ISLA is consistent already at 10,000 cells (area −2%, bias +4%) and at
40,000 (0%, +1%). The whole of the constant-gauge ISLA's sampler dependence
on both datasets (+90% / +189% under area at 40k) was therefore its
plain-mean centroid; with the centroid estimated from the measure, the
measure-weighted routing integral gives the same field under a
uniform-over-cells, an area-proportional and a 10:1-biased draw of the same
wing, at fixed count and at the count the book's accuracy numbers use.

**Two readings and one caution.** First, this is the consistency the
principle asks for, measured: a model whose answer does not depend on how
the surface was sampled, at 10,000 cells, on the hardest meshes in the
program, at a 10% in-distribution price on those meshes and none on the
cars. Second, on the frame question: the measure-weighted centroid is the
Horvitz–Thompson estimate of the surface's geometric centroid ∫x dA / ∫dA,
an integral property of the geometry, and the benchmark shows its estimate
from the sample converging to the same value under three sampling laws; it
is a *sample statistic* only in the sense that every quadrature is one,
which is a different case from the plain mean that reads the distribution
and from the RMS-radius scale. Whether Peter's ruling excludes it is a
question for him, not for this entry; RELFRAME (no frame at all) remains the
cleanest construction and is training. The caution: the benchmark's error
is evaluated on the sampled points themselves, so the area and biased
samplers also move the *metric's* point distribution (toward large cells
and toward the dense half); that shift is common to every arm in a row and
cannot produce a −2% by itself, but it means the HiLift number is
consistency of the predicted field on the points drawn, not a claim about
the unsampled gaps.

## 2026-09-10 — Verdict: the weights-off ablation persists at 210 HiLift cases (0.0589 against 0.0643 in float32, 150 of 180 cases); the measure semantics cost 8% here, and the ablation stays an ablation {#sec-nb-nowl-210-verdict}

The NOW-L rung (@sec-nb-noweights-prereg, amended 2026-09-10: ablation only,
the reference-configuration consequence retired) asks what ISLA's routing
measure weights cost in distribution at 210 random HiLiftAeroML training
cases. Two seeds of ISLA with the weights off (a35_hl_mt2_noweights_scarce),
otherwise the frozen protocol, evaluated in float32 (zero skipped loads) with
the bfloat16 pass alongside; the weighted reference is the three-seed float32
mean. Artifact: `results/nowl_210_reduction_2026-09-10.json`.

**Weights off scores 0.0589 (seeds 0.0581 / 0.0598) against 0.0643 for the
weighted model: 0.916x, an 8.4% gain, lower on 150 of 180 validation cases
(median weighted ÷ off 1.075).** The preregistered bars were 0.0611 or below
to persist and 0.0624 or above to fade; the ablation persists. Velocity
(0.0873 against 0.0937) and wall shear (0.1329 against 0.1441) move by the
same 7–8%. Bfloat16 agrees (0.0593 against 0.0648). Against the unit-drive
baselines of @sec-nb-udrvl-210-verdict the ablation remains behind
GeoTransolver (0.0533, 0.905x of the weights-off model, GeoTransolver lower on
149 of 180) and reaches parity with Transolver (0.0582, 0.988x, Transolver
lower on 128 of 180).

The ablation tally is now: persists at 35 cases (12%), 210 cases (8.4%), 4
geometries (17%) and the fixed angle (10.6%); fades on DrivAerML (2.9%);
pending at 21 geometries, 1,260 cases and the deflection split. Under
@sec-principle these numbers price the measure semantics and decide nothing
about the configuration: the weights stay on, because removing them makes
the aggregate depend on the mesher's sampling density (19x under a 10:1
bias, and flat rather than convergent under the area-proportional sampler in
@sec-consistency-bench). The open mechanistic question, whether the price is
estimator variance or the loss of a density signal, is the area-proportional
sampling arm the generalization session is running. NOW-L closes as a node;
its 21-geometry, 1,260-case and deflection lanes report under WAVE-3.

## 2026-09-11 — Verdict, MIX: every architecture pays to swap sampling conventions (ISLA 1.5–1.9x, the baselines 3–7x), and every architecture absorbs both conventions for free when trained on both {#sec-nb-mix-verdict}

The MIX study (@sec-nb-mix-prereg) trained the three architectures on the
same 435 DrivAerML cars presented under two meshing conventions of the same
surfaces, uniform over cells (`unif`, the training convention of every
checkpoint in the book) and area-proportional (`area`, the law a uniform
point-cloud generator or a different mesher would produce, with exact
Horvitz–Thompson weights), in three conditions: `unif` only (the existing
reference lanes), `area` only, and `mixed` (both, each case seen under each
convention per epoch, 500 epochs, so twice the optimizer steps). Twelve new
lanes, two seeds, unit drive, learning rates matched to the references (ISLA
similarity gauge at 3e-3 to match iw_mt2_gauge, GeoTransolver 1e-3,
Transolver 3e-3), snapshot code, recipe copy recipe_bench; float32
evaluation of every model on the 48 validation cars under both conventions
at 10,000 cells (snapshot code_eval; no loader warnings). Artifact: `results/mix_conventions_2026-09-10.json`.

| architecture | trained on | evaluated on unif | evaluated on area |
|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA, similarity gauge (3e-3) | unif | 0.0616 | 0.1186 |
| ISLA, similarity gauge (3e-3) | area | 0.0868 | 0.0594 |
| ISLA, similarity gauge (3e-3) | mixed | 0.0569 | 0.0541 |
| GeoTransolver, unit drive | unif | 0.0505 | 0.3247 |
| GeoTransolver, unit drive | area | 0.3786 | 0.0518 |
| GeoTransolver, unit drive | mixed | 0.0465 | 0.0468 |
| Transolver, unit drive | unif | 0.0520 | 0.1702 |
| Transolver, unit drive | area | 0.3289 | 0.0540 |
| Transolver, unit drive | mixed | 0.0493 | 0.0500 |

Seed means of two seeds. Swap penalties S (error on the other convention ÷
error on the training convention) and mixing costs C (mixed model ÷
specialist on the specialist's own convention):

| architecture | S unif → area | S area → unif | C on unif | C on area |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA, similarity gauge (3e-3) | 1.92x | 1.46x | 0.92 | 0.91 |
| GeoTransolver, unit drive | 6.43x | 7.31x | 0.92 | 0.90 |
| Transolver, unit drive | 3.27x | 6.09x | 0.95 | 0.93 |

**Against the bars.** Swap: every architecture pays (bar ≥ 1.10x), the
similarity-gauge ISLA least by a wide margin (1.9x and 1.5x) and
GeoTransolver most (6.4x and 7.3x); the prediction that ISLA would be
convention-independent (≤ 1.03x) is falsified, in the same direction and
size as the consistency benchmark's area-sampler reading at 10,000 cells
(@sec-nb-bench-verdict: D_area +122% for the gauge, +260% and +612% for the
baselines), so the two instruments agree. Mixing: every architecture mixes
for free (bar ≤ 1.03; the mixed models are in fact 5–10% *better* than
either specialist on the specialist's own convention), so the prediction
that the baselines would pay for mixing is falsified too; the caveat
preregistered with the design applies, that the mixed lanes took twice the
optimizer steps, and part of the gain is that.

**Reading.** Two facts and their consequence. First, a model trained on one
sampling convention does not transfer to another at 10,000 cells, and the
size of the failure orders the architectures by how much of the
sampling law they read: ISLA with measure weights 1.5–1.9x, Transolver
3–6x, GeoTransolver 6–7x. Second, a model trained on both conventions
handles both, for every architecture, at no in-distribution cost: the
baselines' dependence on the convention is a training-distribution effect
that data diversity removes, not an architectural incapacity. The
consequence for the long-game claim of @sec-nb-mix-prereg is that
"train on several meshers, deploy on another" is not yet a property any
architecture has at 10,000 cells; it is a property of the training data.
What the measure-consistent estimator buys is a smaller penalty on the
*unseen* convention (a fifth to a quarter of the baselines'), which is the
same convergence advantage the benchmark measured. The mechanism that
separates the two readings is the count: the benchmark shows the
measure-weighted ISLA's swap penalty falling toward zero as the sample
grows while the baselines' stays flat, so at fine enough sampling the
measure-consistent model transfers across conventions without having seen
them and the baselines never do. A mixed-convention training run at 40,000
cells, and the same test on HiLiftAeroML where the two conventions differ
by orders of magnitude in local density, are the two follow-ups that would
sharpen this into a deployment rule; neither proposes an architecture
change.

## 2026-09-11 — Verdict, RELFRAME (interim: HiLift sampler lanes and FRAME-FULL pending): with no frame at all ISLA keeps the constant gauge's accuracy on DrivAerML at the 1.2x density floor, and pays 11% at 35 HiLift cases — the same price as the measure-centred frame, so the HiLift price is not frame variance {#sec-nb-relframe-verdict}

RELFRAME (@sec-nb-relframe-prereg) removes every centroid-dependent
quantity from ISLA: the four positional seed features (|r|, log|r|,
r̂·d̂, r̂·n̂; the seed reduces to n̂·d̂ and the measure) and the two
centroid-referenced relational invariants (|z_s|, ẑ_s·d̂; the relational
set reduces to its six anchor-relative members plus the second-moment
terms), with the vector head's radial basis taken from the token's
measure-weighted soft anchor rather than the centroid; positions enter only
through anchor-relative differences, scaled by the stated reference length
(arm "ref") or by the square root of the total surface measure (arm
"meas"). Translation invariance holds to 10⁻¹² with no centering, and the
sampling-consistency contract holds in the unit tests. Eight lanes (two
arms, two datasets, two seeds; unit drive, lr 1e-3, 500 epochs, snapshot
code_frame), float32 evaluation under code_eval_frame (identity-checked to
7e-8 on a legacy checkpoint; no loader warnings). Artifacts:
results/relframe_reduction_2026-09-11.json,
results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_rf_2026-09-11.json.

| arm | DrivAerML pressure (seeds → mean) | vs 0.0557 | density 10:1, sample frame (seeds → mean) | HiLift 35 pressure (seeds → mean) | vs 0.1377 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| relative, reference length | 0.0564 / 0.0567 → **0.0566** | +1.5% | 1.20 / 1.22 → **1.21x** | 0.1568 / 0.1491 → **0.1530** | **+11.1%** |
| relative, √(total measure) | 0.0547 / 0.0557 → **0.0552** | −0.9% | 1.20 / 1.27 → **1.235x** | 0.1567 / 0.1490 → **0.1529** | **+11.0%** |

BENCH samplers on the DrivAerML checkpoints (reference-length arm): D_area
+41% → +3.4% and D_biased +19% → +2.5% from 10,000 to 40,000 cells; the
total-measure arm +60% → +5.9% and +24% → +3.3%; both converge toward the
uniform answer as the measure-centred arm did (@sec-nb-bench-mcenter).

**Against the bars.** DrivAerML: the joint pass it nearly is. Both arms are
within 3% of the constant gauge, and the total-measure arm is 0.9% *more*
accurate (0.0552 against 0.0557); the density factor sits at the 1.2x bar
(1.20 / 1.22 → 1.21x) for the reference-length arm and just over it for the
total-measure arm (1.20 / 1.27 → 1.235x, with one seed at 1.20), and both
converge under all three samplers. On the cars the frame-free model is the
principled configuration at no accuracy cost. That 1.2x is the same floor the
similarity gauge (1.21x) and the measure-centred frame (1.17x) show, and a
model with no frame statistic cannot owe it to a frame: it is the variance
of the measure-weighted routing integral itself under a 10:1 sample (the
effective sample size in the sparse half falls tenfold), which is what the
convergence with count removes. HiLift 35 cases: **the accuracy bar fails on
both arms, by 11%.** The preregistered falsifier therefore fires: a model
with no frame and no frame-estimate variance pays the same price the
measure-centred frame paid (10.4%) and more than the similarity gauge
(7.6%), so the HiLift price of leaving the plain-mean frame is not the
variance of a frame statistic. The joint pass is not met on both datasets
and RELFRAME does not become the flagship by the preregistered rule; the
reference stays under decision.

**What the frame tables say the plain mean was reading.** The full-geometry
frame tables computed for FRAME-FULL (@sec-nb-frame-full-prereg; float64
over every cell of every training and validation surface) put the number on
it: on HiLiftAeroML the plain mean of the surface cells sits **0.131 body
lengths** (2.4–4.7% was DrivAerML's figure; here the range is 0.11–0.15)
from the geometric centroid ∫x dA / ∫dA, and the plain mean of *all* cells
gives the same displacement as the plain mean of a 10,000-cell uniform
sample (0.131 against 0.131), so the displacement is mesh-density bias, not
sampling noise; the Horvitz–Thompson estimate of the geometric centroid from
10,000 cells has a noise of 0.0065 body lengths (maximum 0.046). On
DrivAerML the displacement is 0.034 body lengths. The constant gauge's frame
therefore encodes, on a wing, where the mesher put its cells, to a tenth of
a chord.

**Two readings, one discriminator, thresholds stated now.** Either the 11%
is the positional information that the four dropped seed features carried
(a model whose seeds know only n̂·d̂ must reconstruct a point's location
from its anchors), or it is the mesh-density content of the plain-mean
frame, an in-distribution advantage of a non-physical input. FRAME-FULL
(exact geometric frame from the full mesh as global data, positional terms
kept, zero variance; @sec-nb-frame-full-prereg) separates them, with the
readings fixed before it lands: *recovers* if its 35-case error is within
3% of 0.1377 at a density ratio ≤ 1.2x; *pays* if it is ≥ 7% worse. If it
recovers, the exact geometric frame carries information the relative
construction lacks, which is legitimate (the frame is a property of the
geometry, available for any shape at inference) and makes FRAME-FULL, not
RELFRAME, the reference candidate under the ruling; the follow-up is then
a relative-position encoding that restores the positional information
without a frame. If it pays, the price is the mesher's pattern, the stated
cost of the principle, and not a reason to reinstate a sample statistic. The
HiLift sampler lanes of the RELFRAME checkpoints complete the consistency
half of the row.

**Peter's ruling and the decision rule (2026-09-11).** The Horvitz–Thompson
centroid is acceptable if it buys significant accuracy; at equal accuracy
the frame-free construction is preferred. On the numbers on file the
frame-free total-measure arm equals the measure-centred frame and the
constant gauge on DrivAerML (0.0552, 0.0548, 0.0557) and equals the
measure-centred frame at 35 HiLift cases (0.1530 against 0.1520), so at
equal accuracy RELFRAME with the total-measure scale is the reference
candidate on both datasets and the measure-centred frame is not adopted.
**Rule: the reference is RELFRAME (total-measure scale) unless FRAME-FULL
passes its joint bar** (within 3% of 0.1377 at 35 HiLift cases at a density
ratio ≤ 1.2x), in which case the exact geometric frame has bought
significant accuracy with a property of the geometry and FRAME-FULL becomes
the reference candidate instead. The chapters stay "under decision" until
FRAME-FULL lands; the same ruling governs the repaired baselines' datapipe
frame (an area-weighted `CenterMesh` is acceptable for them only if it buys
accuracy over the plain mean), which the MWAW lanes test.

## 2026-09-11 — BENCH addendum: with the frame held by the pipeline, the measure-weighted baselines are the most sampler-consistent arms measured (|D| ≤ 0.9% at 40,000 cells on both datasets, ≤ 0.8% at 10,000 on HiLift); the aggregation defect is fixed, the frame defect is the datapipe's {#sec-nb-bench-mw}

The ten measure-weighted baseline checkpoints of @sec-nb-mw-verdict went
through the benchmark's three samplers at 10,000 and 40,000 cells (snapshot
code_mw with the *_mw model configs; float32; 60 lanes, one teardown fault
rerun, no loader warnings; artifact
results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_mw_2026-09-10.json). Frame
convention: the benchmark pipeline, like the campaign-E probes, centres
every architecture's coordinates on the plain mean of the 320,000-cell
uniform pool before the samplers, so these are pool-frame values for the
baselines (their sample-frame collapse is @sec-nb-mw-postcenter); the ISLA
arms centre in the model and are frame-independent.

| arm | 10k: unif / area / biased | 40k: unif / area / biased | D_area 10k → 40k | D_biased 10k → 40k |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver, measure-weighted pooling, DrivAerML | 0.0504 / 0.0526 / 0.0511 | 0.0511 / 0.0516 / 0.0513 | +4.4% → +0.9% | +1.4% → +0.3% |
| Transolver, measure-weighted pooling, DrivAerML | 0.0525 / 0.0549 / 0.0532 | 0.0529 / 0.0534 / 0.0530 | +4.7% → +0.9% | +1.4% → +0.2% |
| GeoTransolver, measure-weighted pooling, HiLift 35 (3 seeds) | 0.1169 / 0.1164 / 0.1175 | 0.1165 / 0.1168 / 0.1168 | -0.4% → +0.3% | +0.5% → +0.3% |
| Transolver, measure-weighted pooling, HiLift 35 (3 seeds) | 0.1211 / 0.1210 / 0.1220 | 0.1207 / 0.1211 / 0.1211 | -0.0% → +0.3% | +0.8% → +0.4% |

**Reading.** With the frame fixed, giving GeoTransolver and Transolver the
surface measure in their slice pooling makes their aggregation as
consistent as an integral should be: the area-proportional draw, whose
Horvitz–Thompson weights span three to four decades and leave a third of
the kept cells at the clamp on the wings, changes their answer by under 1%
at 40,000 cells and by under 5% at 10,000 on the cars, and by under 1% at
either count on the wings, where the unweighted twins read the distribution
by 150–260% and the measure-centred ISLA holds at −2% to +4%. This is the
cleanest separation of the two defects the program has: measure weighting
repairs the aggregation completely, and what remains for the baselines is
the frame, which in the surface recipe is a datapipe choice (`CenterMesh`
on the plain mean of the pool) rather than a model property. The same
datapipe transform has an area-weighted mode (`use_area_weighting`), which
would give the baselines the Horvitz–Thompson estimate of the geometric
centroid as their frame, the datapipe analogue of the question put to Peter
in @sec-nb-bench-mcenter; a relative-position input encoding is the
frame-free alternative for a raw-coordinate architecture and has not been
built. The accuracy price of measure awareness on uniform sampling is
+1–2% on the cars and +6% at 35 HiLift cases for the baselines (0.1165
against 0.1100; 0.1207 against 0.1145), against +11% for the
measure-centred ISLA on the same rung; the two rows of @tbl-consistency-40k
that carry these arms are added.

## 2026-09-11 — Preregistered: MWAW, the repaired baselines with an area-weighted datapipe frame (acceptable only if it buys accuracy) {#sec-nb-mwaw-prereg}

Peter's ruling on frames applies to the measure-weighted baselines' datapipe
frame as well: `CenterMesh` on the plain mean of the pool is a sample
statistic that reads the mesher (0.034 body lengths off the geometric
centroid on DrivAerML, 0.131 on HiLift); its area-weighted mode
(`use_area_weighting: true`) is the Horvitz–Thompson estimate of the
geometric centroid, acceptable for the baselines only if it buys accuracy
over the plain mean. Eval-only is not possible (the mw checkpoints were
trained in the plain frame), so four lanes: GeoTransolver and Transolver
with measure-weighted pooling, unit drive, reference learning rates, on
DrivAerML 435 cars with the training and validation datapipe centring by the
area-weighted mean (seeds 42/43; run ids mwaw_dr_gt_unit_lr1e3_seed{42,43},
mwaw_dr_transolver_unit_lr3e3_seed{42,43}; snapshot code_mw; recipe copy
recipe_mw with `drivaer_ml_surface_aw.yaml`). **Readouts.** Float32
in-family error against the plain-frame mw twins (0.0498 / 0.0522) and the
density probe with the centring applied after the draw in the area-weighted
mode (sample frame, the frame a biased mesher delivers, now estimated with
HT weights). **Bars.** *Buys accuracy* if ≥ 3% better than the plain-frame
twin; *equal* within ±3% (then the plain-mean frame stays for the baselines
by the ruling, with its sample-frame collapse stated); *costs* if ≥ 3% worse.
Density: ≤ 1.5x under the sample frame is the expected floor for an
HT-estimated frame (ISLA's measure-centred frame gives 1.17x); a value near
the plain-frame collapse (12–16x) would mean the baselines' sensitivity is
not only the centroid. **Prediction.** Equal accuracy (the frame shift is
0.034 body lengths on cars) and density ≈ 1.2x: the area-weighted frame
removes the collapse at no accuracy cost, which under the ruling does not
adopt it for the baselines but does establish that their density
dependence is entirely the datapipe frame.

## 2026-09-10 — Preregistered: FARWAKE, far-field oversampling of the interior training queries (is the far-wake eddy-viscosity deficit an under-sampling effect?) {#sec-nb-farwake-prereg}

*Setting.* At matched parameters ISLA's interior query-token configuration
leads GeoTransolver-volume on pressure, velocity and eddy viscosity
everywhere except the far wake beyond 0.4 body lengths downstream, which
holds 2.2% of a uniform interior sample and carries the whole 18%
eddy-viscosity deficit (companion notebook entry #sec-nb-far-wake; chapter 8).
Anchor-geometry explanations were closed: anchors follow the query mass, the
wake tokens moved anchors into the far wake and improved it 6%, and the
query seed's azimuth blindness did not survive the routing-mass probe. The
surviving hypothesis is under-sampling: the network sees few far-wake
queries in training, so the slices and the readout are shaped by the 98% of
queries near the body. Peter approved the arm on 2026-09-10 ("either we get
the right answer, or we rule out one more cause").

*Mechanism (why it should work).* Training queries are drawn from the
interior; the loss is a plain mean over them, so the spatial weighting of
the objective is the sampling density. Drawing more queries from the far
wake raises both the gradient signal and the anchor mass there. This is a
training-distribution change with no new input and no architecture change,
of the same kind as query-count augmentation (@sec-nb-qcount-prereg); it
does not inject a non-physical signal, since the query positions are
already inputs, and the inclusion probabilities are exact and recorded so
the objective's reweighting is known.

*Instrument.* Recipe transform `SdfBiasedSubsampleInteriorPoints`
(`unified_external_aero_recipe/src/domain_transforms.py`, contract-tested:
expected count, exact inclusion probabilities, Horvitz–Thompson recovery of
the original band shares, reproducibility, identity on small interiors and
bare meshes). The reader draws a 40,000-point uniform interior pool
(`interior_n_points_range=(40000, 40000)`, boundaries untouched), the SDF
transform runs on it, and the new transform keeps points with probability
proportional to a step function of the signed distance: weight 1 below
0.05 body lengths, 3 between 0.05 and 0.4, 8 beyond 0.4, normalized to an
expected 10,000 kept points. On the measured band fractions (77% / 11% /
7.8% / 2.2%) this gives training shares of about 60% / 8.5% / 18% / 13.6%,
so the far band rises from 10% to 32% of the queries and the far wake
beyond 0.4 L from 2.2% to 14%. Arm: the reference query-token + signed
distance configuration (`v0_qt2` lanes, hidden 192, similarity gauge,
otherwise frozen protocol, `code_qcount` snapshot which carries the reader
option), two seeds (v0_isla_qtsdfval_farwake_seed{42,43}), recipe copy
`recipe_farwake`. Evaluation in float32 under the guarded snapshot on the
standard uniform 10,000-point validation sample (so the metric's point
distribution is unchanged), plus the wall-distance band decomposition of
the saved predictions.

*Bars (float32, two-seed means, band units of the companion's
decomposition; reference ISLA hidden 192/256 far band ≥ 0.05 L about 0.101,
GeoTransolver-volume 0.068).* Supported if the far-band eddy-viscosity
error is ≤ 0.085 (at least half the gap closed) with the near-wall band
within 3% of the reference and the recipe-metric pressure and velocity
within 3%; falsified if ≥ 0.095 (no more than a fifth of the gap); between
otherwise. Secondary: the ≥ 0.4 L shell (reference 0.108 against 0.071).
Readings written in advance: supported means the far-wake deficit was a
training-distribution effect and the principled remedy is a sampling law,
which then needs its own consistency check (the model must still converge
to the same field under the uniform sampler); falsified means the far-wake
deficit is neither anchor geometry nor sampling and the representational
conjecture (the downstream coordinate is only implicit in ISLA's seed) is
the remaining candidate; a near-wall or pressure regression beyond 3% is
the objective-reweighting cost and is reported as such. Owner: this
session.
